Students take a core set of gerontology courses, participate in an interdisciplinary seminar, and conduct research that incorporates a focus on aging.

The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to this specific program.
Department: College of Agriculture (Department of Horticulture and Landscape Architecture)
Description: The Department of Horticulture and Landscape Architecture (HLA) offers programs leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. Graduate students in Horticulture select a research focus from several areas of specialization: genetics and genomics, molecular biology and physiology, controlled environment and protected cultivation, postharvest biology, and sustainable food and farming systems. Students work with a major professor to design a program of study and research tailored to their individual needs and interests. The department has modern research facilities, including state-of-the-art laboratories and extensive greenhouse and field research sites.

Department: White Lodging-J.W. Marriott, Jr. School of Hospitality and Tourism Management
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Hospitality and Tourism Management is designed for students seeking careers in academia and high-level research positions. Our programs emphasize how research can be used to improve the lives of individuals and families. The doctoral program prepares students for positions as researchers and faculty in universities, as well as for leadership roles in public and private institutions and agencies.

Description: The Purdue School of Industrial Engineering (IE) offers the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree. The PhD degree is a research-based degree, and its primary objective is the development of an individual’s ability to perform independent and original research. The program of study for the PhD degree is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of the field of industrial engineering and to develop their ability to conduct independent research. The School of Industrial Engineering provides opportunities for students to conduct research in several areas, including human factors, manufacturing, operations research, and production systems.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Research Assistantships (RA), Graduate Teaching Assistantships (TA)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Languages and Cultures
Requirements: Applicants to the Ph.D. in Languages and Cultures must provide official transcripts from all institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a resume, a statement of purpose, and a diversity essay. A writing sample (typically 15-20 pages) is also required to demonstrate research ability. For international applicants whose native language is not English, evidence of English proficiency must be submitted (TOEFL or IELTS scores). The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to this program.
Concentration: Applied Linguistics, Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Russian, and Spanish
Description: The Ph.D. in Languages and Cultures is an interdisciplinary program that offers students the opportunity to specialize in one of several languages and cultures, or in applied linguistics. The program is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the field while allowing for specialized research in their chosen area of focus.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Linguistics
Requirements: Applicants to the Doctor of Philosophy in Linguistics should have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0/4.0. The GRE is not required. Application requirements include a completed application and non-refundable application fee, official transcripts from every institution of higher education attended, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Resume, a Writing Sample, and a Diversity Essay. International applicants must also provide proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo scores).
Description: The Interdisciplinary Program in Linguistics (SLC-LING) allows students to obtain a Doctor of Philosophy degree in Linguistics. The primary objective of the program is to provide students with a well-rounded and integrated background in linguistics. Students can pursue specialized interests in various areas of linguistics, including phonology, phonetics, syntax, semantics, historical linguistics, sociolinguistics, second language acquisition, and computational linguistics. Students in this program are active in research and the program hosts a variety of conferences and workshops throughout the year.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Management

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Materials Engineering
Requirements: The Materials Engineering (MSE) graduate program is designed for students with a bachelor's or master's degree in engineering or the physical sciences. Applicants should have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale. Three letters of recommendation are required for the application. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to the Materials Engineering graduate program. International applicants must provide proof of English proficiency through TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Concentration: Computational Science and Engineering, Ecological Sciences and Engineering
Description: The School of Materials Engineering offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science in Materials Engineering (MSMSE) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. The graduate program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the science and engineering of materials, while allowing for specialization in a variety of research areas. Research in the school spans the breadth of materials science, including research in metals, polymers, ceramics, electronic materials, and biomaterials, with applications in energy, transportation, medicine, and microelectronics. The PhD program is a research-intensive program that culminates in a dissertation and requires a minimum of 90 credit hours beyond the baccalaureate degree.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics
Requirements: The Mathematics Department requires that applicants for the Ph.D. program have an undergraduate major in mathematics or its equivalent. Specifically, it is expected that applicants have successfully completed courses in real analysis and abstract algebra equivalent to MA 44000 and MA 45300. In addition, it is expected that applicants have some exposure to more advanced topics such as complex analysis, topology, and/or differential equations.
Concentration: Computational Finance, Computational Science and Engineering
Description: The Department of Mathematics offers programs leading to the Master of Science (M.S.) and the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees. The department is a community of scholars representing many areas of mathematics. Research areas include algebra, algebraic geometry, analysis, applied mathematics, complex analysis, differential equations, differential geometry, harmonic analysis, logic, mathematical biology, mathematical physics, number theory, numerical analysis, operator algebras, probability, and topology. Both the M.S. and Ph.D. programs are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in mathematics and to prepare them for careers in research, teaching, and industry.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the PhD program in Mechanical Engineering, applicants must have a bachelor's or master's degree in engineering or a related field. Successful applicants typically have a graduate GPA of 3.2/4.0 or higher. Required application materials include: an online application, transcripts from every institution attended, three letters of recommendation, an Academic Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a Resume/CV. International applicants must provide proof of English proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS). The GRE is not required for admission.
Concentration: Computational Science and Engineering; Ecological Sciences and Engineering
Description: Mechanical engineering is the most diverse of all engineering disciplines. At Purdue, our world-class faculty and facilities provide an environment where students can pursue research in a variety of areas. The PhD program is research-oriented, requiring a dissertation that provides a significant original contribution to the field of mechanical engineering. Each student’s program of study is individual in nature and is developed in conjunction with their major professor and advisory committee to reach the highest level of proficiency in their chosen area of specialization.

International applicants whose native language is not English are required to provide proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo).
Description: The Ph.D. program is the highest degree offered by the School of Nuclear Engineering. It is awarded to candidates who have demonstrated a breadth of knowledge in nuclear engineering and a depth of knowledge in a specific area of research, as well as the ability to conduct independent and original research. The program is designed for students who want to pursue a career in research and development in the nuclear industry, national laboratories, or academia. This program requires the completion of advanced coursework, passing a qualifying exam and a preliminary exam, and the successful defense of a doctoral dissertation based on original research.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Nursing
Requirements: Admission requirements for the PhD program include: 1. A master’s degree in nursing or a related field, or a baccalaureate degree in nursing for the BS-PhD track, from an accredited program. 2. A grade point average of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale in previous academic work. 3. Registered nurse license or eligibility for licensure in Indiana. 4. Evidence of ability to do doctoral work. 5. Statement of scholarly goals and research interests. 6. Three letters of recommendation from persons who can assess the applicant’s potential for doctoral study. 7. Graduate Record Exam (GRE) taken within the last 5 years is recommended but not required. 8. English Proficiency for international students (TOEFL or IELTS). 9. Curriculum Vitae or Resume. 10. Sample of Scholarly Writing. 11. Interview with School of Nursing graduate faculty.
Description: The PhD program in nursing at Purdue University prepares the next generation of nurse scientists, scholars, and educators to improve health and healthcare. Graduates of the program will be leaders in the nursing profession who contribute to the development of nursing science through research and scholarship. The program emphasizes the development of research skills and the application of nursing science to address the complex health needs of individuals, families, and communities. The PhD program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct independent research in nursing and related fields. The curriculum includes coursework in nursing science, research methods, statistics, and a cognate area. Students also complete a dissertation that represents an original contribution to nursing science.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Teaching Assistantships, Graduate Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Nutrition Science
Requirements: Applicants must have a minimum of a B (3.0 on a 4.0 scale) or better average in prior study from an accredited college or university. International students must have a score of 550 or higher on the paper-based Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), 213 or higher on the computer-based test, or a minimum total score of 80 on the Internet-based test (iBT). Required application documents include an Academic Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a Resume, and three letters of recommendation. The GRE is not required for the Nutrition Science Graduate Program.
Concentration: Biochemical and Molecular Nutrition, Human and Clinical Nutrition, Animal Health and Comparative Nutrition, and Public Health and Health Promotion
Description: The Purdue Interdepartmental Nutrition Program (INP) provides an opportunity for students to study nutrition through a variety of lenses. INP faculty members represent a range of departments across the university, providing a multidisciplinary approach to the study of nutrition. The program aims to train students to be leaders in nutrition research and education.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy
Requirements: Applicants for the Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy must submit an online application through the Purdue Graduate School. Required materials include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) describing philosophical interests and goals, a resume or curriculum vitae, and a writing sample (approximately 15-20 pages). International applicants whose native language is not English are required to submit proof of English proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS scores).
Concentration: Applied Philosophy, Bioethics, Philosophy and Literature
Description: The Department of Philosophy at Purdue University offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree. Our program is a 'pluralistic' one, in that we have faculty and students working in a wide range of philosophical traditions and styles, including analytic, continental, and historical approaches. We have particular strengths in the history of philosophy (including ancient, medieval, modern, and 19th and 20th century philosophy), ethics and social-political philosophy, and the continental and analytic traditions. Our goal is to train students to be excellent researchers and teachers, and to help them find professional employment in philosophy or related fields.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Forestry and Natural Resources
Requirements: Admission to the Department of Forestry and Natural Resources is based on an evaluation of the student’s undergraduate record (and previous graduate record if applicable), three letters of recommendation, and a statement of purpose. Most students admitted to the M.S. and Ph.D. programs have an undergraduate grade point average of 3.2 or higher. The GRE is not required.
Concentration: Ecology and Biology; Management and Marketing of Natural Resources; Genetics, Tree Improvement, and Biotechnology; Spatial Data Analysis; Human Dimensions; and Wood Science and Engineering
Description: The Department of Forestry and Natural Resources offers two master’s degrees: the Master of Science (M.S.) and the Master of Science in Forestry (M.S.F.). The M.S.F. degree is intended for individuals with an undergraduate degree in forestry who wish to enhance their professional training. For most other students, the M.S. degree is appropriate. All programs are thesis programs. The Ph.D. program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in research and/or teaching. Major areas of study include: Ecology and Biology; Management and Marketing of Natural Resources; Genetics, Tree Improvement, and Biotechnology; Spatial Data Analysis; Human Dimensions; and Wood Science and Engineering.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Global Supply Chain Management
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Application materials include a current resume, a statement of purpose, two online recommendations, and official transcripts from all colleges or universities attended. Standardized test scores (GMAT or GRE) are optional for the MS Global Supply Chain Management program, and waivers are available for applicants with at least 3 years of full-time professional experience. International applicants must also provide proof of English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS).
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Global Supply Chain Management (GSCM) program builds upon Purdue University’s core strength in operations, supply chain management, and business analytics to provide students with skills that will well position them for a career in managing global supply chains. It is also highly ranked by Gartner and QS. The MS GSCM program is a 30-credit, 10-month (August – May) program that provides students with the expertise needed to lead in the global supply chain management field. Students will develop skills in the areas of sourcing, logistics, and distribution, as well as in the use of data analytics to improve supply chain performance. The program also offers students the opportunity to participate in a global supply chain project with an industry partner. The program’s curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the global supply chain and the tools and techniques needed to manage it effectively. Students will learn how to design and manage supply chains, how to use data analytics to improve supply chain performance, and how to lead in the global supply chain management field.
Accredidation: The Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

The program prepares students for leadership roles in a variety of health and kinesiology-related careers or for further study at the doctoral level. Students work closely with a faculty mentor to develop a plan of study that meets their individual needs and interests. The program typically takes two years to complete and culminates in a thesis or a non-thesis option.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Physics
Requirements: The School of Health Sciences requires the following for a complete application: Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Three (3) letters of recommendation. A resume or curriculum vitae. A statement of purpose. Proof of English proficiency (for international students). The GRE is not required for application to any of our graduate programs.
Description: The Health Physics (HP) program within the School of Health Sciences is one of the premier programs in the country. We provide students with a rigorous academic environment, while offering them the opportunity to participate in various research projects. Health Physics is the profession devoted to the protection of people and their environment from the hazards of ionizing radiation, while making it possible to enjoy the beneficial uses of radiation. Health physicists are needed wherever radiation or radioactive materials are used. They work at medical institutions, in government, for industry, in education, and for the military. The Purdue Health Physics program has been in existence since 1959 and has produced some of the top people in the field. The curriculum is designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge and skills to become leaders in the field. Faculty research areas range from radiation biology and epidemiology to Monte Carlo modeling and instrumentation.
Accredidation: The Purdue Health Physics program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission (ANSAC) of ABET (http://www.abet.org).

Description: Graduate programs in the School of Health Sciences provide a unique and interdisciplinary environment for students to pursue advanced degrees. Our programs are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the basic and health-related sciences while offering specialized training in several core areas: Health Physics, Medical Physics, and Occupational and Environmental Health Sciences (which includes Toxicology and Industrial Hygiene). The School of Health Sciences offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science (MS) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Our graduate program is dedicated to protecting human health and the environment. Students work with faculty to address complex health challenges through research and education.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Medicinal Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a background in chemistry, biology, or a related field. Application materials must include an Academic Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a professional resume or CV, and three letters of recommendation. Description: The Department of Medicinal Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology (MCMP) focuses on the discovery and development of new drugs for the treatment of various diseases and the study of the molecular mechanisms by which drugs act. The Master of Science (M.S.) degree is only available to students already enrolled in the MCMP Ph.D. program or the College of Pharmacy Pharm.D. program. The graduate program is uniquely positioned at the intersection of the chemical and biological sciences. The curriculum and research provide students with the foundations and tools to understand how drugs and other molecules affect biological systems, and how to create new molecules to study or treat disease. Research in the department is interdisciplinary and covers several areas including cancer biology, neuroscience, immunology, infectious disease, and metabolic disease.

Accredidation: Recognized by the Society of Actuaries as a Center of Actuarial Excellence

ProgramName: Advanced Global Technology Minor
Requirements: The Advanced Global Technology minor is designed to recognize students who have successfully completed the Purdue Polytechnic Institute Global Technology minor and choose to take additional coursework and/or participate in a second study abroad/global professional experience. To be eligible to complete the Advanced Global Technology minor, students must first complete all requirements of the Global Technology minor (GLBT).
Description: This minor is designed to provide students with the opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of the global technological environment and its impact on society. Students will be able to: Demonstrate an understanding of the impact of technology on society and the environment in a global context. Demonstrate an understanding of the global technological environment and its impact on society.

ProgramName: Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering, BSAAE
Requirements: The BSAAE degree requires a total of 130 credits. The School of Aeronautics and Astronautics admits students into the professional program after they have completed the requirements of the First-Year Engineering (FYE) program. A student must have a minimum of 30 semester hours of credit before being admitted to the School of Aeronautics and Astronautics. Admission is competitive and based on the student’s academic record. To be eligible for graduation, students must earn a C- or better in all AAE and required MA, PHYS and CHM courses.
Description: Aeronautical and astronautical engineering is a field that deals with the design, development, testing, and production of aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems and equipment. The curriculum provides a thorough preparation in the basic sciences, engineering sciences, and the social and humanistic areas. The professional courses provide students with a strong background in the fundamental areas of aerospace engineering: aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, dynamics and control, and systems design.
Accredidation: The Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Engineering Technology,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, first-year applicants must meet minimum high school course requirements: 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Lab Science (for Engineering Technology: Biology, Chemistry, and Physics are recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Evaluation is based on high school coursework, grades, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions.
Description: Aeronautical engineering technology (AET) graduates apply engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and maintenance of aircraft and their systems. Graduates of this program are typically employed in the fields of aircraft manufacturing, maintenance, and systems testing.
Accredidation: The Aeronautical Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Financial Analysis,
Requirements: Students must earn a C- or better in all AT, MGMT, and ECON courses and any course that is a prerequisite to an AT, MGMT, or ECON course. A minimum of 120 credit hours are required for graduation.
Description: The Aerospace Financial Analysis major is designed to prepare students for careers in the financial and business sectors of the aerospace and aviation industries. This program combines a strong foundation in aviation and aerospace with business and financial analysis skills. Students will gain an understanding of the aerospace industry, including its history, regulations, and technological advancements, while also developing proficiency in financial modeling, investment analysis, and risk management. Graduates will be equipped to work in a variety of roles, such as financial analysts, consultants, and managers within aerospace companies, airlines, and government agencies.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI)

ProgramName: Aerospace Studies Minor
Requirements: The Aerospace Studies minor is available to all undergraduate students at Purdue University. It consists of the courses listed below.
Description: The Aerospace Studies minor is available to all students who meet the course requirements. It provides a unique opportunity for students to gain a broader understanding of the Department of the Air Force and its role in national security. Students will explore leadership and management principles, global security issues, and the evolution of air and space power.

ProgramName: African American Studies Minor
Requirements: 15 credits. Required Courses: AAS 27100 - Introduction To African American Studies (3.00 credits). African American Studies Electives: Select 12 additional credits of African American Studies courses. At least 3 credits must be at the 30000-level or above (3.00 credits). 9 additional credits (9.00 credits). Note: Students must earn a GPA of 2.0 or higher in the minor courses.
Description: African American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the African-American experience in the United States, as well as the experiences of people of African descent throughout the African Diaspora (e.g., in the Caribbean, South America, and Europe). It offers students a variety of perspectives through which to examine these experiences, including history, literature, sociology, political science, and the arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies,
Requirements: To earn a degree in the College of Liberal Arts, students must complete at least 120 credits, complete the College of Liberal Arts core requirements, and complete the requirements for a major. The Liberal Arts core involves the following: I. Foundations (Mathematics/Statistics, Science, Foreign Language) and II. Exploration (Aesthetics and Culture, Social Science, Individual and Society, Individual and Global Perspective, Global Perspective).
Description: African American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that offers a comprehensive approach to the study of the history, culture, and social organization of people of African descent. Drawing from the humanities and social sciences, the program helps students understand the African American experience from historical and contemporary perspectives. Students develop skills in research, critical thinking and communication, which prepare them for careers in law, public policy, education, social services and the arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness,
Requirements: For admission to the Agribusiness, BS program, applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Purdue is a test-required institution; therefore, SAT or ACT scores are mandatory for application. High school preparation should include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. To graduate with a BS in Agribusiness, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, including specific major requirements in agricultural economics, business, and quantitative methods.
Concentration: Agribusiness Management, Agricultural Marketing, Commodity Marketing, Finance, Real Estate, Sales and Marketing, Value Added and Food Systems
Description: Students in the Agribusiness major receive a strong foundation in management, marketing, finance, and data analysis. The Agribusiness degree provides students with the management and analytical tools required for a successful career in a wide variety of agribusinesses, including firms in the food, fiber, and biofuels supply chains. Students take courses in the College of Agriculture and the School of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Communication,
Requirements: Admission to the Agricultural Communication major is competitive. Applicants must meet Purdue University's general freshman admission criteria, which includes the completion of at least 15 academic units: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Applicants are evaluated based on their high school curriculum, grades, standardized test scores (SAT or ACT), and a personal essay including Purdue-specific responses.
Description: The agricultural communication major is offered by the Department of Agricultural Sciences Education and Communication. It is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in agricultural journalism, broadcasting, public relations, advertising, or marketing communication. Students may tailor the curriculum to meet their career goals through a wide variety of communication electives and a specific area of interest in agriculture or the environment.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Economics,
Requirements: Admission to the Agricultural Economics, BS program follows Purdue University's undergraduate admission criteria. Applicants must submit a completed Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, and 6 semesters of Social Studies. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for admission. The selection process is holistic, evaluating academic performance, strength of curriculum, test scores, and personal background.
Concentration: Applied Agricultural Economics, Data Science, Policy and Pre-Law, Quantitative Analysis
Description: The Agricultural Economics major provides students with a broad background in the business and economics of the food and fiber industry. Students in Agricultural Economics will develop a strong foundation in economic theory, quantitative methods, and the application of these tools to the agricultural and food sectors. This major prepares students for careers in management, marketing, finance, and policy analysis.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Education,
Requirements: To earn the Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Education (BSAE), students must satisfy University requirements for a bachelor's degree; fulfill Program Major Requirements; General Education Requirements; College of Agriculture Core Requirements; and Concentration Requirements (Agricultural Science and Business or Communication and Leadership). Students must also fulfill a teacher certification requirement. In addition to the GPA required for a BSAE, students must also have a 2.5 average in Agricultural Education (ASEE and ASEC) and content courses. No grade lower than a C- will be accepted for these courses. Students must also pass the CORE Content Area assessments. To be eligible for student teaching, students must have a 2.8 cumulative GPA. Total credits required: 120.
Description: Students in the Agricultural Education program prepare for careers as teachers of agriculture in junior and senior high schools. The program also prepares graduates for careers in agricultural industry, non-formal education, and the Cooperative Extension Service. Students complete coursework in all areas of agriculture and in education. Graduates are eligible to receive a license to teach agriculture in the State of Indiana. Graduates may also be licensed to teach in other states.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Agricultural Engineering, BSAGE
Requirements: The programs are joint between the College of Agriculture and the College of Engineering and are administered by the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering. The faculty are members of both colleges. The Agricultural Engineering and Biological Engineering programs are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org. Students are admitted to Agricultural Engineering or Biological Engineering after completing the First-Year Engineering requirements.
Department: College of Agriculture and College of Engineering
Concentration: Machine Systems Engineering and Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering
Description: Agricultural Engineering (AE) is an engineering discipline that applies engineering principles to the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural products and the management of natural resources. Agricultural engineers are trained in the basic mathematical and physical sciences. Their specialty includes a sequence of engineering science and design courses. Agricultural engineers are unique in that they apply engineering principles to biologically based systems. In the sophomore year, students begin to focus on one of two concentrations in the major. Both concentrations culminate in a capstone senior design sequence. Machine Systems Engineering concentration focuses on the design and development of machines used in the agricultural, construction, forestry and landscape industries. Machine systems engineers design, test and evaluate machines such as tractors and implements, combines, lawn and garden equipment, and construction and off-road equipment. Students are trained in power and energy systems, electronic sensors and control systems, fluid power, and machine design. Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering (ENRE) concentration focuses on the application of engineering principles and techniques to solve problems involving the environment and our natural resources. ENRE engineers work to improve water quality and protect our soil, air and water resources. Students are trained in hydrology, soil and water conservation, irrigation and drainage, and ecological engineering. ENRE engineers often work in government agencies, consulting firms, and non-profit organizations.
Accredidation: The Agricultural Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Agricultural Systems Management Minor
Requirements: The minor in Agricultural Systems Management requires the completion of 15 credits of ASM coursework. Of those 15 credits, 9 must be 30000 level or higher. ASM 10500 is not applicable to the minor. At least 50% of the credits used to satisfy the minor must be earned at Purdue University. All courses must be taken for a letter grade and a C- or better is required. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required for those courses used to satisfy the minor.
Description: The Agricultural Systems Management minor is for students who want to develop their knowledge and skills in managing technological systems for food, fiber, and natural resources.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Systems Management,
Requirements: Admission to the Agricultural Systems Management (BS) program is based on Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. Required components include a completed application via the Common App, a personal essay, and high school transcripts showing completion of core requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are required for all freshman applicants.
Description: Agricultural Systems Management (ASM) is for students who want to be solvers of technical problems for the global food and agricultural industry. The ASM program is a bridge between engineering and the end users of technologies. ASM graduates are professionals who manage technical systems such as machinery, agricultural production, and food processing systems. Students study a variety of topics including machine systems, soil and water systems, electricity and electronics, structural systems, and precision agriculture. Students also take several business courses to develop management and leadership skills. A professional internship is a requirement for the program. Students can select electives to focus on a particular area of interest such as data analytics, unmanned aerial systems, natural resources, or machine systems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agronomy,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Science degree in Agronomy, a student must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours. The program offers four options: Agronomic Business and Marketing, Crop Science, International Agronomy, and Soil and Water Sciences. General Purdue undergraduate admission requirements include the completion of a high school curriculum (including English, Math, Laboratory Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), the Common App essay, and the submission of SAT or ACT scores.
Concentration: Agronomic Business and Marketing, Applied Meteorology and Climatology, Crop and Soil Management, International Agronomy, Plant Genetics and Breeding, Soil and Environmental Science
Description: Agronomy is the science of managing the soil and the plant in such a way as to maximize the benefit of both. Students study the basic sciences and apply them to the production of food, feed, and fiber, and the management of land resources for environmental protection. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in the agribusiness sector, government agencies, and research organizations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Air Traffic Control,
Requirements: Admission to the Air Traffic Control, BS program requires high school course completion (English, Math, Lab Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. A program-specific requirement is that students must be able to obtain a second-class FAA medical certificate. For graduation, students must complete 120 credit hours with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0.
Department: School of Aviation and Transportation Technology
Description: Air traffic controllers are responsible for the safe, orderly and efficient movement of aircraft in the National Airspace System. Purdue’s air traffic control (ATC) program is one of a select few in the nation that is part of the FAA’s Air Traffic Collegiate Training Initiative (AT-CTI). You will learn about the technology, regulations and procedures used to manage air traffic in our National Airspace System. You’ll use state-of-the-art simulators to gain hands-on experience in various ATC environments, including tower, terminal and en route operations.
Accredidation: The School of Aviation and Transportation Technology is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

ProgramName: Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance Minor
Requirements: The Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance Minor is available to students who have been admitted to the Professional Flight Technology major or the Aviation Management major. Enrollment in this minor is limited. Applications are due the semester prior to the student starting the minor.
Department: Purdue Polytechnic Institute (School of Aviation and Transportation Technology)
Description: The Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance minor is intended for students in the Aeronautical Engineering Technology and Aviation Management majors who desire to obtain the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) mechanic certificate. The A&P certificate is a requirement for many entry-level positions in the aviation industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Airline Management and Operations,
Requirements: Admission to the Airline Management and Operations program is based on a holistic review of academic factors including high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of lab science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of world language), grades in core academic courses, strength of curriculum, and SAT or ACT scores. Personal background and experiences are also considered through the personal essay and Purdue-specific questions.
Department: School of Aviation and Transportation Technology
Description: Modern aviation needs managers with a holistic view of the entire aviation ecosystem. The Airline Management and Operations (AMO) major focuses on the business, operational, and management aspects of the airline industry. Students study the core principles of airline operations, revenue management, fleet planning, and crew scheduling. They gain insights into the regulatory framework, safety management systems, and the economic factors that drive airline decision-making. Through case studies and projects, students learn to optimize airline performance while ensuring safety and efficiency. This major prepares graduates for diverse leadership roles within airlines, from network planning and operations control to customer service management and regulatory compliance.

ProgramName: American Studies Minor
Requirements: The American Studies minor requires 15 credit hours of AMST coursework. Required Course: AMST 20100 - Interpreting America (3 credits). Elective Courses: 12 additional credits of AMST courses, 6 of which must be at the 30000 level or above.
Description: The American Studies Minor provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American culture, past and present. It is designed to complement a student’s major by providing a broader perspective on the American experience.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies,
Requirements: To apply for the American Studies, BA program at Purdue University, freshman applicants must meet high school course requirements, including 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Mathematics (Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue is a test-required institution for students applying for the Fall 2024 term and beyond, meaning a score from the SAT or ACT is required. Applicants must also submit a personal essay and answer Purdue-specific questions as part of their application.
Description: American Studies is the study of the people, places and ideas that comprise the United States. It involves a critical look at the American experience from various perspectives and involves several different academic departments. Students can explore such diverse topics as popular culture, film, literature, history and social justice. Because American Studies is interdisciplinary, students have the flexibility to tailor their education to their specific interests.

ProgramName: Animal Science Minor
Requirements: Minimum of 18 credits must be earned. Required courses may have prerequisites. ANSC 49100, ANSC 49300 and ANSC 49400 can only be used as 'Other Animal Science courses' and cannot exceed 3 credits towards the minor.
Description: The Animal Science minor is designed for students who want to develop a basic understanding of the animal sciences to supplement their major program of study. The minor is available to any student at Purdue University with the exception of those majoring in Animal Sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Animal Sciences,
Requirements: The Animal Sciences program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences (genetics, physiology, nutrition, and products) and the opportunity to apply those sciences to the production and management of animals (including food animals, horses, and companion animals) or the processing of meat, milk, and eggs. The program requires 120.0 credits for graduation and offers five concentrations: Animal Agribusiness, Behavioral Well-being, Biosciences, Pre-Veterinary Medicine, and Production and Management. Applicants must complete the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions, and provide high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores.
Concentration: Agribusiness, Animal BioHealth/Pre-Professional, Behavioral Well-being, Biosciences, and Production and Management
Description: Animal sciences is the study of animals that live alongside humans. Most often, that means livestock species (beef and dairy cattle, poultry, sheep, pigs) and companion animals. Animal science students study everything from the cell to the whole animal and how to best manage these animals to ensure they are healthy and productive. Students in the animal sciences major gain a foundation in biology and the physical sciences. Students also choose one of five concentrations to specialize in: Agribusiness, Animal BioHealth/Pre-Professional, Behavioral Well-being, Biosciences, or Production and Management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Animation and Visual Effects,
Requirements: The Animation and Visual Effects major focuses on the 3D computer graphics (CG) that are used in the creation of digital animation for the entertainment industry (film, TV, video games), and as a tool for communication and visualization in many other industries. Skills such as 3D modeling, lighting, rendering, and technical direction are emphasized. Freshman applicants must meet general Purdue high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.
Description: The Animation and Visual Effects major focuses on the creative side of the animation process. Students will learn the principles of animation, character design, storytelling, and visual effects for film and games. The program integrates traditional art techniques with industry-standard software to prepare students for careers in the entertainment and media industries.
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Anthropology Minor
Requirements: The minor in Anthropology requires 15 total credits. Required Course (3 credits): ANTH 10000 - Being Human: Introduction To Anthropology. Selective Course (3 credits): Select one of ANTH 20400 - Introduction To Biological Anthropology and Archaeology, ANTH 20500 - Human Cultural Diversity, ANTH 21000 - Technology And Culture, or ANTH 23000 - Gender Across Cultures. Anthropology Electives (9 credits): Select 9 credits of Anthropology courses, 6 credits of which must be at the 30000 level or higher.
Description: The Anthropology minor is designed to provide students with a general introduction to the four fields of the discipline: sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. It offers students an opportunity to explore the diversity of human cultures, past and present, and the biological foundations of humanity.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology,
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology requires a total of 120 credit hours for graduation. Of these, 33 credit hours must be in anthropology, 15 credits of which must be in upper-division (30000-level or above) courses. A 2.0 GPA in the major is required for graduation. All major courses must be taken for a letter grade. Anthropology courses with a grade of C- or lower cannot be used to satisfy major requirements.
Concentration: Applied Anthropology, Environmental Anthropology
Description: Anthropology is the study of human diversity across time and space. It is a holistic discipline, which means that anthropologists study all aspects of human life, including our biology, our history, our language, and our culture. The Anthropology major at Purdue University provides students with a broad background in the four fields of anthropology: socio-cultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. Students also have the opportunity to specialize in particular areas of interest through elective coursework and research opportunities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Agricultural Economics,
Requirements: To apply for the Applied Agricultural Economics, BS program, students must meet high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Precalculus, Trigonometry, or Calculus), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Applicants must submit an application through the Common Application, which includes a personal statement (essay). Official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores are required for admission.
Description: The Applied Agricultural Economics major is for students who want to study the principles and concepts of economics and how they are applied to the food system, the environment, and the world. This major provides students with a strong background in economic theory and the quantitative tools needed to analyze real-world problems. Students will learn about agricultural marketing, resource economics, policy analysis, and international development.
CostPerCredit: $347.85 per credit hour (Resident); $948.30 per credit hour (Non-Resident)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Leadership,
Requirements: The Applied Leadership degree program is intended for students who have earned an Associate of Science (AS) or Associate of Applied Science (AAS) from a regionally accredited institution. Admission is based on a student’s previous academic record. Students must have at least a 2.0 cumulative GPA for admission into the program.
Description: The B.S. degree in Applied Leadership is a degree-completion program for students who have completed an Associate of Science (AS) or Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree in a technical or professional field. The program is designed to provide students with the leadership and management skills needed to advance in their careers. Students will learn about organizational behavior, leadership theory, human resource management, and project management. The program is offered at several locations throughout Indiana and online.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Meteorology and Climatology,
Requirements: Applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Official high school transcripts or self-reported coursework must be submitted. Admission to the College of Science requires the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science (including biology, chemistry, or physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Admission is competitive and based on a holistic review of academic performance and standardized test scores.
Description: The Applied Meteorology and Climatology major provides a foundation for students who want to become professionals in the fields of operational meteorology or applied climatology. Students will gain experience in the areas of weather and climate analysis, observation, and forecasting. The curriculum is designed to meet the requirements for employment as a meteorologist with the National Weather Service and other government agencies, and for employment as a meteorologist in the private sector.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Physics,
Requirements: To earn the Bachelor of Science Degree in Applied Physics, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, including the Physics, Mathematics, and Science/Engineering courses specified, and satisfy the College of Science Core requirements. Admission to the program requires meeting Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which includes high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), the Common App personal essay, and official SAT or ACT scores.
Concentration: Applied Physics, Atmospheric/Planetary, Business, Computer Science, Geology, Geophysics, or Physical Chemistry
Description: The Applied Physics major is for students who wish to pursue a career in an area of applied physics or in an interdisciplinary field. It is also an excellent program for students who wish to enter the job market immediately after graduation. The curriculum for the Applied Physics major includes the core physics courses of the Physics major, but replaces some of the more advanced elective courses with a concentration of 12-18 credit hours in a specific area of applied physics or in a related field. Students may choose from among several established concentrations, such as atmospheric/planetary science, business, computer science, geology/geophysics, and physical chemistry, or may design their own concentration.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Statistics,
Requirements: To be competitive for admission to the College of Science, you should have taken at least four years of mathematics (including precalculus or calculus). Purdue University is test-required for students applying for Fall 2024 and beyond. We evaluate you based on: High School Course Expectations, Grades and Test Scores, Personal Achievement, and the Purdue Admission Essay. High school course expectations include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.
Description: The Bachelor of Science with a major in applied statistics provides students with a strong background in statistical methods and their applications in a variety of fields. This program is designed to prepare students for careers in business, industry, government, and healthcare, and for graduate study in statistics or related fields. Students learn to use statistical software, analyze data, and interpret results to make informed decisions. Upon completion of this degree, students will be able to demonstrate a solid foundation in statistical theory, apply statistical methods to analyze data from various fields, use statistical software for data analysis, and communicate statistical results effectively.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aquatic Sciences,
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Aquatic Sciences program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, with an emphasis on the ecology and management of aquatic ecosystems. Students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses in the Forestry and Natural Resources (FNR) core. Students must also complete the University Core Curriculum and the College of Agriculture core requirements. All students in the Forestry and Natural Resources department are required to complete a 5-week summer practicum.
Concentration: Marine and Freshwater Biology; Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
Description: Students in the aquatic sciences major choose between two concentrations: marine and freshwater biology or fisheries and aquatic sciences. The marine and freshwater biology concentration provides a strong foundation in the biology and ecology of aquatic systems and the organisms that inhabit them. Students learn about the physiological, ecological, and behavioral adaptations that allow organisms to survive and thrive in aquatic environments. The fisheries and aquatic sciences concentration provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to manage and conserve fish and other aquatic organisms. Students learn about fish biology, ecology, and management, as well as the physical and chemical properties of aquatic systems and how they affect aquatic life.

ProgramName: Arabic Language and Culture Minor
Requirements: Total 15 credits. A minimum grade of C- is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor requirements. All ARAB courses must be taken for a letter grade. No more than one course (3 credits) used to satisfy the minor requirements may be taken from a source other than Purdue University. A maximum of one course (3 credits) from a pre-approved list of English-taught courses related to the Middle East may be used to satisfy the minor.
Description: The Arabic Language and Culture minor is designed to provide students with a basic proficiency in the Arabic language and a broad understanding of the culture and history of the Arabic-speaking world.

ProgramName: Architectural Engineering Minor
Requirements: The Architectural Engineering Minor requires a total of 18 credit hours. Completion of the minor requires a minimum GPA of 2.0 in the courses used to satisfy the minor. At least 50% of the credits used to satisfy the minor must be earned at Purdue University. The minor is available to students in the Lyles School of Civil Engineering and the School of Mechanical Engineering.
Description: The Architectural Engineering Minor is designed for students who want to develop a background in the design and construction of buildings and their systems. Students take courses in architectural design, building systems, and construction management.

ProgramName: Art and Design Studio Minor
Requirements: 18 credits required. Required Courses (9 credits): AD 10500 - Design I, AD 11300 - Drawing I, AD 11400 - Drawing II. Elective Courses (9 credits): Select 9 additional credits from Art and Design Studio courses at the 20000 level or above (excluding AD 10500, 11300, and 11400). A minimum of 6 credits must be taken at Purdue University. All courses must be completed with a C- or better.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Art and Design Studio minor allows students to pursue creative interests in various studio disciplines, including ceramics, drawing, painting, photography, printmaking, and sculpture. This minor provides students with the opportunity to develop their artistic skills and explore personal expression through a structured sequence of studio courses.
Accredidation: Accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Art History Minor
Requirements: 15 credit hours. Required Courses (6 credits): AD 22600 - History Of Art To 1400 and AD 22700 - History Of Art Since 1400. Art History Electives (9 credits): Nine additional credits of upper-division (30000-level or higher) Art History courses. Note: At least 9 credit hours must be taken at Purdue.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Art History minor is designed for students who are interested in the history of art and who wish to complement their major field of study with a concentration in this area. The minor provides a broad overview of the history of art, as well as the opportunity to pursue more specialized coursework in specific periods and styles.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, applicants must meet minimum high school coursework requirements, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of World Language. Purdue utilizes a holistic review process that considers high school grades, academic strength, SAT or ACT test scores, and a personal essay.
Description: The program in Art History provides students with a broad knowledge of the history of art and design from around the world. In addition to gaining a deep understanding of specific periods, cultures, and media, students develop skills in visual analysis, critical thinking, research, and writing. The curriculum prepares students for careers in museums, galleries, auction houses, and cultural organizations, as well as for graduate study in art history and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence,
Requirements: Purdue University uses a holistic review process for undergraduate admissions. Requirements include completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and answers to Purdue-specific questions.
Department: College of Science and College of Liberal Arts
Concentration: AI in Health, AI in Modern Society, AI in Philosophy, Autonomous Systems, Foundations of AI, Mathematical and Computational Foundations of AI
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence is a joint degree program between the College of Liberal Arts, the College of Science, and the Purdue Polytechnic Institute. This program will offer students a choice between three majors, based on their individual interests and career goals. Each major will have a common core of courses and specialized courses. Students who complete this degree will be able to: Use foundational knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence (AI) to solve problems across a range of AI contexts. Effectively use data to inform AI models and generate and apply AI solutions to real-world problems. Develop AI systems that demonstrate an understanding of ethical and societal implications of AI.

ProgramName: Asian American Studies Minor
Requirements: To complete the minor, students should consult with their academic advisor and submit the Asian American Studies Minor Declaration Form.
Description: Asian American Studies at Purdue University is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the histories, experiences, and cultures of people of Asian descent in the United States. Our courses provide students with a foundational understanding of the diversity within Asian American communities and the historical and contemporary issues they face.

ProgramName: Asian Studies Minor
Description: The Asian Studies program offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the history, politics, religion, philosophy, and cultures of Asia. This program provides students with a foundational understanding of Asian societies and prepares them for further study or for careers in a globalized world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies,
Requirements: The interdisciplinary Asian Studies major offers students the opportunity to study the many different aspects of Asia: its history, culture, language, politics, and society. The Asian Studies major consists of 30 credits of coursework, including 15-18 credits in their chosen area of concentration (China, Japan, or General Asia). Students are also required to complete two years of an Asian language (Chinese or Japanese) or the equivalent and at least 15 credits must be at the 30000-level or higher. A total of 120 credits is required for the degree.
Description: The Asian Studies program provides students with a broad-based knowledge of Asian cultures, history, politics, and languages. Students select courses from a variety of disciplines, including anthropology, art history, history, philosophy, political science, and sociology. The major requires the study of an Asian language (Chinese, Japanese, or Korean) and offers opportunities for study abroad in Asia.

ProgramName: Astronomy Minor
Requirements: The Astronomy minor is intended for students with a strong background in physics. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue. All courses must be taken for a grade of A, B, C, or D. Courses may not be taken Pass/Not-Pass. Minimum GPA in minor courses: 2.00.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Astronomy,
Requirements: Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for individuals applying for undergraduate admission. Freshman admission is based on a holistic review of criteria including high school coursework (Core 40 or equivalent), overall grades, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and answers to Purdue-specific questions. For the Astronomy, BS program, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours for the degree and maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA in all Physics (PHYS) courses.
Description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers an Astronomy major for students who are interested in the study of the universe, from the solar system to the most distant galaxies. It provides a solid foundation in both the theoretical and observational aspects of modern astronomy and astrophysics. The curriculum includes courses in physics, mathematics, and computer science, as well as specialized courses in astronomy and astrophysics. Students will have the opportunity to participate in research projects with faculty members, which can lead to publications in scientific journals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Atmospheric Science/Meteorology,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Science degree, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, which include at least 32 credit hours of 30000-level or higher courses in residence at Purdue University, and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00. All courses used to meet major requirements must be taken for a grade. Courses may not be taken Pass/No Pass. Applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores.
Description: Atmospheric Science is the study of the Earth’s atmosphere and the processes that cause what we know as weather. Most atmospheric scientists work to improve our understanding and forecasting of weather and climate. Students in atmospheric science will develop a strong background in physics and mathematics to understand the physical and chemical processes that govern the atmosphere. The Atmospheric Science program at Purdue University meets the requirements for employment with the National Weather Service and satisfies the curriculum recommendations of the American Meteorological Society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Audio Engineering Technology,
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Audio Engineering Technology, BS program, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific supplemental questions. Official high school transcripts and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are required as part of Purdue University's admission process. The program curriculum consists of 120 credit hours, focusing on the science and technology of sound, including areas such as electronics, digital signal processing, and audio production.
Description: Audio Engineering Technology is a profession for those who want to be involved in the technical side of the audio and entertainment industry. AET students learn about the equipment, software and electronics that make music, film and television sound great. They also learn how to use these tools to create their own audio productions.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology,
Requirements: Admission to the Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology, BS program is based on Purdue University's general undergraduate admission criteria. This includes a review of high school coursework (meeting minimum subject requirements), academic grades, SAT or ACT scores, and the personal essay provided in the application. The degree requires a total of 120 credit hours for graduation, including core engineering technology courses, math, science, and technical electives.
Description: The Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology program prepares graduates to solve the technical and design problems that involve the creation, construction, and operation of automated systems. It provides students with a broad-based knowledge of engineering technology and automation systems with specific emphasis on robotics, sensors, industrial networking, and automation software.
Accredidation: The Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Manufacturing Engineering Technology Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aviation Management,
Requirements: Admission to the Aviation Management program is based on high school coursework, including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Purdue University is a test-required institution, requiring either SAT or ACT scores. Evaluation also considers grades, grade trends, strength of curriculum, and a personal essay.
Description: The Aviation Management program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive background in the aviation industry. In addition to a core of aviation courses, the student will have a foundation in management, marketing, accounting, and finance. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers with airlines, airports, aircraft manufacturers, and government agencies. This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).
Accredidation: This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Barley,
Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry (AG),
Requirements: The Biochemistry (AG) program is a program of the Department of Biochemistry within the College of Agriculture. The program requires 120.00 total credits for graduation and is designed to provide students with a strong background in chemistry and the biological sciences. Admission requirements include the completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language), a personal essay, and the submission of SAT or ACT scores.
Description: Biochemistry focuses on the chemical processes that occur in all living organisms. Biochemistry is the intersection of biology and chemistry. It is the study of life at the molecular level. This field has applications in many areas, including medicine, agriculture, and biotechnology. The Biochemistry major provides students with a strong foundation in chemistry and biology, as well as the specialized knowledge and skills needed for a career in biochemistry or a related field. Students have the opportunity to participate in research and gain hands-on experience in the laboratory.
Accredidation: Accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) and the Royal Society of Biology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry (CHM),
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, applicants must meet the following minimum high school course requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and advanced math), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (for Science majors, this must include chemistry), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single World Language. Purdue is a test-required institution; applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores. Evaluation is also based on high school grades, the strength of the curriculum, and the personal essay.
Description: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical processes within and relating to living organisms. By controlling information flow through biochemical signaling and the flow of chemical energy through metabolism, biochemical processes give rise to the complexity of life. Over the last decades of the 20th century, biochemistry has become so successful at explaining living processes that now almost all areas of the life sciences from botany to medicine to genetics are engaged in biochemical research. Today, the main focus of pure biochemistry is on understanding how biological molecules give rise to the processes that occur within living cells, which in turn relates greatly to the study and understanding of whole organisms. This major is for students who want to work in the field of medicine, or in the biotech or pharmaceutical industries.
Accredidation: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) approved

ProgramName: Biochemistry Minor
Requirements: Credits must be earned at Purdue University. Credit by examination or transfer credit cannot be used to satisfy the requirements for this minor. Some of the courses listed below may have prerequisites. Please check the course descriptions for more information. Enrollment in some courses may be limited.
Description: The minor in Biochemistry is available to any student at Purdue University, with the exception of students majoring in Biochemistry (BCHM) or Biochemistry (BIOL). A minimum of 15 credit hours are required for the minor. All courses must be taken for a grade. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses. Students must complete at least 6 credits of the minor in-residence at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.

ProgramName: Bioinformatics Minor
Requirements: To earn the Bioinformatics Minor, students must complete 18-24 credit hours of the following courses: Core Courses (15-20 credits) including Computer Science, Biological Sciences, Mathematics, and Statistics; Elective Courses (3-4 credits). A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: Modern biology generates large amounts of data. This data needs to be effectively organized, synthesized and analyzed to advance the life sciences. The Bioinformatics minor is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the computational tools and methods used in this field.

ProgramName: Biological Engineering, BSBE
Requirements: Admission to the Biological Engineering program requires meeting Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, Purdue University requires the submission of official SAT or ACT scores for all undergraduate applicants. Applicants must also complete the Common Application and Purdue-specific essay questions.
Concentration: Bioprocess Engineering, Cellular and Biomolecular Engineering, and Food and Biological Process Engineering
Description: The Biological Engineering program is offered by the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering. Students may enter the program through either the College of Agriculture or the College of Engineering. Biological Engineering is a field of engineering that focuses on the development and use of biological processes and materials to produce high-value products, to develop better processes for biological systems, and to manage biological systems. The Biological Engineering program at Purdue University is designed to provide students with a strong background in the biological and physical sciences, as well as engineering sciences. Students will learn to apply engineering principles to solve problems involving plants, animals, microorganisms, and biological materials. The program prepares students for careers in industries such as food processing, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and environmental management, as well as for graduate study or professional school in medicine or dentistry.
Accredidation: The Biological Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Biological Sciences Minor
Requirements: Students must complete 16-21 credits. All courses must be taken for a grade (no pass/no-fail). A 2.0 GPA in the minor courses is required. Credit in BIOL 11000 and 11100 or BIOL 12100 and 13100 or equivalent credit is required. Any student at Purdue University is eligible to complete a minor in Biological Sciences, with the exception of students majoring in Biological Sciences.
Description: The Biological Sciences minor is available to any student at Purdue University, West Lafayette, with the exception of students majoring in Biological Sciences, Biochemistry (Biology), and Science Education (Biology). This minor is designed for students who wish to supplement their major with a background in the biological sciences and provides a broad overview of the field, from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. A minimum of 19 credits in Biological Sciences is required for the minor. All courses must be taken for a grade, and a minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in the courses that are used to satisfy the minor. At least 10 of the credits must be taken at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology Education,
Requirements: Admission to the Biology Education Program occurs in three phases: Gateway 1, Gateway 2, and Gateway 3. Information about these Gateways can be found at: https://education.purdue.edu/undergraduate-students/current-students/gateways/. Key requirements include a grade point average of 3.0 or higher in professional education and content courses with no grade lower than a C; completion of Professional Education courses and relevant content courses; and passing the Indiana CORE Assessments for Educators (or equivalent) in both Developmental (Pedagogy) and Content Area(s).
Department: College of Science and College of Education
Description: This program, offered jointly by the Department of Biological Sciences and the College of Education, leads to the Bachelor of Science degree and eligibility for Indiana licensure to teach life science in grades 5-12. The program provides a broad background in the biological sciences, including a core of biology courses and additional biology electives, as well as the professional education courses and field experiences required for teacher certification.
Accredidation: Purdue University’s teacher education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and the Indiana Department of Education.

ProgramName: Biomedical Engineering, BSBME
Requirements: All students who wish to pursue a degree from the College of Engineering must first complete the First-Year Engineering program. Upon completion of the First-Year Engineering requirements, students are eligible to apply for professional status in the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering. Admission to these schools is competitive and is based on a student’s academic performance in the First-Year Engineering program.
