The BSBME program requires a minimum of 130 credit hours for graduation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Health Sciences,
Requirements: Admission to the Biomedical Health Sciences, BS program is based on several factors including high school coursework, grade point average (GPA), SAT or ACT test scores, and personal essays. High school course expectations include: 8 semesters of English; 8 semesters of Math (Algebra I & II and Geometry/Trigonometry); 6 semesters of Lab Science (Biology and Chemistry recommended); 6 semesters of Social Studies; and 4 semesters of World Language. Evaluation also considers the strength of the high school curriculum and the applicant's personal background and experiences.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Biomedical Health Sciences (BMHS) major is designed for students who have a strong interest in biological and physical sciences and are interested in pursuing a career in medicine or another health profession (e.g., physician assistant, physical therapy, occupational therapy, dentistry, optometry, etc.). The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, while also allowing students to take courses in the behavioral and social sciences, and the humanities. The BMHS major provides students with the flexibility to tailor their education to meet their individual interests and career goals.

ProgramName: Biometrics Minor
Requirements: 15 credit hours are required for the Biometrics minor. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at the 30000-level or higher. All courses must be completed with a C- or better. A cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required in these courses.
Description: Biometric systems are becoming increasingly important for identity management and person authentication. Biometric applications include person identification at borders, in secure facilities, on personal computers and cell phones, and in civilian and forensic investigations. Biometric systems are multidisciplinary and bring together topics from human factors, social and legal issues, hardware, algorithms, and databases. The biometric minor allows students to take courses that cover the fundamentals of biometrics and specialize in areas that focus on systems, algorithms and applications.

ProgramName: Biotechnology Minor
Requirements: 19 Credits. Students interested in the Biotechnology minor should contact the Biology department advisor. Some of these courses have prerequisites. Required courses include AGRY 10500, biological sciences foundations (BIOL 11000/11100 or 12100/13100), Genetics/Cell Biology (BIOL 23100/23200 or 27000 and 28100 and 28600), Biochemistry (BCHM 30700 or CHM 33300 or CHM 53300), and a Biotechnology elective.
Description: The Biotechnology Minor is available to students who have completed BIOL 11000 and 11100 (or equivalent) and CHM 11500 and 11600 (or equivalent). Students can earn the minor by completing 17-21 credit hours of specified coursework.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Brain and Behavioral Sciences,
Requirements: The Brain and Behavioral Sciences (BBS) major requires 120 credits. The curriculum is designed to provide a strong foundation in the fundamental areas of psychology and specialized knowledge in the brain and behavioral sciences. Students must complete 120 total credits, which include all of the course requirements listed below.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Brain and Behavioral Sciences major is for students interested in the biological and health foundations of behavior. Core courses in the brain and behavioral sciences major provide a foundation in psychological sciences (e.g., developmental, social, and clinical psychology). Beyond these core courses, students focus their studies on the biological and health-related aspects of psychology through courses on the brain, learning, and health psychology. Research experience is a key part of the brain and behavioral sciences major, and students are required to complete at least two semesters of research. Our students go on to graduate study in psychology or medicine (e.g., medical school, physician assistant programs, or physical therapy) or work in various healthcare-related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Building Information Modeling,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, applicants must complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 7 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, and 6 semesters of Social Studies. Additionally, Purdue requires the Common App personal essay and official SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.
Description: Virtual construction, also known as building information modeling (BIM), is the future of the construction industry. The building information modeling program teaches you how to manage the construction process and the construction site using 3D modeling and other technologies. You will use various tools to help owners, architects, and engineers visualize the construction project before construction begins. You also will use BIM tools to track and manage the progress of construction after it begins.

ProgramName: Business Economics Minor
Requirements: 15.00 Credit Hours. Required Courses: ECON 25100, ECON 25200, MGMT 20000 (or MGMT 21200 or AGEC 33000). Elective Courses: 6.00 credit hours from ECON 30100, 34000, 35200, 36000, 36100, 36700, 37000, 38000, 38500, 45100, 46100, 46600, or 47100. Available to non-Daniels School of Business students only. Students must meet Daniels School of Business minor residency requirements and have a 2.0 GPA in minor courses.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: This minor is intended for students who are not majoring in any of the Daniels School of Business undergraduate majors. Students must complete 12 credits of Daniels School of Business coursework to earn a minor from the Daniels School of Business.

ProgramName: Business French Minor
Requirements: Students must complete 15 credits of coursework in French at the 30000-level or above. Required courses include FR 30100 (French Level V), FR 30200 (French Level VI), and FR 42400 (Business French), plus 6 additional credits of French electives at the 30000-level or above. No more than 6 credits may be transferred from a non-Purdue program. A minimum grade of C- is required in all courses for the minor.
Description: The Business French minor is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the French language and a comprehensive understanding of the business environment in the Francophone world. Students will develop their linguistic skills in French, focusing on the vocabulary and cultural knowledge necessary for professional communication.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology program at Purdue University, applicants must meet the following high school course requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including academic/college-prep courses), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, and Physics recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Purdue University is test-required; either SAT or ACT scores are required for admission. For the completion of the Bachelor of Science degree, a minimum of 120 credits is required with a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA.
Description: Cell, Molecular and Developmental Biology (CMDB) focuses on how individual cells and molecules work together to create a living organism. CMDB students will learn about the mechanisms that control cell growth, differentiation, and communication. This program is excellent preparation for students interested in research, medicine, or the biotechnology industry.

ProgramName: Chemical Engineering, BSCHE
Requirements: To be admitted to the professional program, students must have completed the First-Year Engineering requirements, as well as CHM 11600 (General Chemistry) or its equivalent. For guaranteed entry into the professional program, students must have a minimum 3.3 GPA. For students with a GPA between 2.0 and 3.29, admission is on a space-available basis.
Description: Chemical engineering is a discipline that is based on chemistry, physics and mathematics. However, it also includes aspects of other engineering disciplines, as well as the social sciences and humanities. A chemical engineer is someone who uses the principles of chemistry, physics, mathematics and other engineering disciplines to solve problems that involve the production or use of chemicals and other products. Chemical engineers are involved in many areas, including: research and development, design, manufacturing, and technical sales. The Purdue University School of Chemical Engineering provides a broad-based education in chemical engineering, preparing its graduates for a variety of careers in industry, government and academia.
Accredidation: The Chemical Engineering (BSCHE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Chemistry Minor
Requirements: Credit Hours: 19.00 to 25.00. The minor requires General Chemistry (CHM 11500 and 11600) or (CHM 12500 and 12600) or (CHM 12901 and 13600); Organic Chemistry (CHM 25500, 25501, 25600, 25601) or (CHM 26505, 26300, 26605, 26400); plus 6 credit hours of 30000 level or higher chemistry courses. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue University.
Description: A minor in chemistry provides a student with a broad range of knowledge in the various fields of chemistry. Students can gain experience in analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry. The minor consists of five to six courses and is open to all students at Purdue who are not majoring in Chemistry or Biochemistry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Chemistry, BS program, applicants must complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus, trigonometry, or calculus for the College of Science), 6 semesters of Lab Science (including biology, chemistry, or physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of additional academic electives. Applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry degree is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous education in the principles and practice of chemistry. This program prepares students for a wide range of careers in industry, government, and academia, as well as for admission to graduate and professional schools. Students receive a strong foundation in the five major areas of chemistry: analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry.
Accredidation: This program is certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS).

ProgramName: Chemistry, BSCHM
Requirements: The Chemistry, BSCHM program requires 120 credit hours for graduation, maintaining a minimum GPA of 2.0. Applicants must meet Purdue University’s freshman admission criteria, which include high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue University is test-required; applicants must submit either SAT or ACT scores. The curriculum includes the Science Core (e.g., Composition, Foreign Language, Statistics) and the Chemistry Core (General, Organic, Analytical, Physical, and Inorganic Chemistry).
Description: The Chemistry (BSCHM) program is the professional chemistry major. It is specifically designed to prepare students for graduate study in chemistry or for a career in the chemical industry. This program is accredited by the American Chemical Society (ACS).
Accredidation: Accredited by the American Chemical Society (ACS)

ProgramName: Chinese Minor
Requirements: The Chinese minor requires a minimum of 18 credit hours. Required courses include CHNS 20100 (Chinese Level III), CHNS 20200 (Chinese Level IV), CHNS 30100 (Chinese Level V), and CHNS 30200 (Chinese Level VI), plus 6 credits of electives. At least 50% of the credits must be earned at Purdue University. A C- or better is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor. Students must meet all of the requirements of their home college/department and the specific requirements of the minor.
Description: The Chinese minor is designed for students who wish to gain a solid foundation in Chinese language and culture. Through a sequence of language courses and electives in literature, linguistics, or culture, students develop communicative competence and a deeper understanding of the Chinese-speaking world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Studies,
Requirements: Admission to the Chinese Studies, BA program is based on Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include high school coursework (4 years of English, 3 years of math, 3 years of laboratory science, 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of foreign language), overall grades, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.
Description: The Chinese Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on Chinese language, literature, culture, history and society. You will gain proficiency in Mandarin Chinese and a broad understanding of the Chinese-speaking world through a variety of courses offered by the School of Languages and Cultures, and the departments of history, philosophy and political science. This program prepares you for careers in international business, government, education, and further graduate study.

ProgramName: Civil Engineering, BSCE
Requirements: The program requires a total of 128 credits for graduation. Students must complete the First-Year Engineering (FYE) requirement (29-30 credits) before being admitted to the Lyles School of Civil Engineering. The Lyles School of Civil Engineering core requirements consist of 51 credits. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad background in civil engineering and includes courses in construction engineering and management, environmental engineering, geomatics engineering, geotechnical engineering, hydraulic and hydrologic engineering, materials engineering, structural engineering, and transportation engineering.
Description: Civil engineering is the oldest of the engineering professions. It is the field of engineering most directly related to the public and its welfare. Our society faces many challenges including: clean water, sustainable energy, traffic congestion, and failing infrastructure. Civil engineers deal with these and other issues. Our graduates are leaders in the development and application of advanced technologies to improve our infrastructure and the environment. The Lyles School of Civil Engineering at Purdue University is one of the most highly ranked and well-respected programs in the nation.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering degree program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Classical Studies Minor
Requirements: The minor requires a minimum of 15 credits. 6 credits must be at 30000-level or higher. All courses must be taken for a grade. Required Course (3 credits): Select one from CLCS 23010, CLCS 23100, CLCS 23300, CLCS 23500, CLCS 23700, or CLCS 23900. Electives (12 credits): Select 12 additional credits in CLCS, GREK, or LATN.
Description: The Classical Studies minor provides students with an interdisciplinary introduction to the ancient Greek and Roman civilizations that are the roots of much of Western culture. Students take courses in ancient history, classical literature (read in translation), and ancient philosophy and religion.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies,
Requirements: Required: High school transcript, SAT or ACT scores, Essay and Purdue-specific questions
Concentration: Classical Languages; Material Culture and History
Description: Classical Studies is the study of the languages and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome. The Classical Studies program at Purdue offers students the opportunity to study ancient history, literature, philosophy, religion, and art, as well as the Greek and Latin languages. Students in this major choose one of two concentrations: Classical Languages or Material Culture and History.

ProgramName: Communication Minor
Requirements: A minimum of 18 credits are required for the minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken at the 30000-level or higher. Note: At least 9 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication,
Requirements: Purdue University utilizes a holistic admissions process. Applicants to the Communication, BA program are evaluated based on high school coursework (including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), grades, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and extracurricular activities.
Department: Brian Lamb School of Communication, College of Liberal Arts
Concentration: General Communication, Communication Management, Health Communication, Human Relations, Media and Mass Communication, Political Communication, and Public Relations and Strategic Communication
Description: The study of communication is the study of how people use messages to generate meanings within and across various contexts, cultures, channels, and media. The Bachelor of Arts in Communication provides students with a broad understanding of communication processes and their impact on individuals, organizations, and society. Students develop strong written, oral, and visual communication skills, as well as critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
Accredidation: The concentration in Public Relations and Strategic Communication is certified (CEPR) by the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Composition,
Requirements: To be admitted to the major in Music (any concentration), students must pass an audition. For the concentration in Composition, students must submit a portfolio of original scores. In addition to the audition/portfolio, students must be admitted to Purdue University.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in music is a liberal arts degree. It is designed for students who wish to study music within the context of a broad-based university education. It provides a foundation in music theory, history, and performance.
Accredidation: Purdue University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Computer and Information Technology Minor
Requirements: Requires 18 credits for completion. Open to all students. CIT majors are not eligible for this minor. Students must have a minimum GPA of 2.0 to be eligible to apply for the CIT minor.
Description: The Computer and Information Technology (CIT) minor is available to any student outside of CIT who is interested in broadening their knowledge of the application of computers and information technology to their own major. Students gain basic knowledge of computing logic, systems development, information systems, and databases, and choose an upper-level elective based on their personal interest.
Accredidation: The Computer and Information Technology program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer and Information Technology,
Requirements: To earn the Bachelor of Science in Computer and Information Technology, students must complete 120 credit hours of coursework. Admission to the program is based on a holistic review of the applicant's academic record, including high school coursework (4 years of English, 3-4 years of math, 3 years of lab science, 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of foreign language), SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific responses regarding the choice of major and use of Purdue's facilities.
Concentration: Cybersecurity; Data Analytics, Technologies and Applications; Network Engineering Technology; Systems Analysis and Design
Description: The Computer and Information Technology program provides students with a solid foundation in the principles and practices of information technology. The curriculum focuses on the application of computing technology to solve business and organizational problems. Students gain expertise in areas such as networking, cybersecurity, systems analysis and design, database management, and software development. The program emphasizes hands-on learning and prepares graduates for a wide range of careers in the IT industry.
Accredidation: The Computer and Information Technology program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

ProgramName: Computer Engineering, BSCMPE
Requirements: Students may enter the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering after completion of First-Year Engineering (FYE) requirements. For more information, please see ECE’s transition website: https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE/Academics/Undergraduates/UGO/T2M.
Department: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Description: Computer engineering is the design, development, and application of digital and computer-based systems. A computer engineer is a professional with a background in both electrical engineering and computer science. Such a professional is prepared to analyze and design computer hardware and software and to understand their trade-offs. The computer engineering curriculum includes courses in computer software and hardware, and it allows students to choose technical electives in several areas. Examples of these areas include computer architecture, operating systems, networking, communications, control systems, signal processing, and integrated circuit design. Students in this program are encouraged to choose a sequence of electives that will provide both depth and breadth in their area of interest.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET

ProgramName: Computer Science Minor
Requirements: Students must complete 17 to 20 credits from the following courses. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue University. Computer Science majors are not eligible for the Computer Science minor. All minor courses must be taken for a letter grade. A grade of C or better is required in each course used for the minor.
Description: The Computer Science minor is available to students in all majors except Computer Science and Data Science. Students must complete a set of core courses and then choose from elective courses that interest them.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science,
Requirements: To be eligible for freshman admission, applicants must complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of World Language. Purdue is a test-required institution; applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores. Admission to the Computer Science major is highly competitive, and applicants are evaluated based on their academic strength, SAT/ACT scores, and the personal essay and Purdue-specific questions included in the Common Application.
Concentration: Computational Science and Engineering, Computer Graphics and Visualization, Database and Information Systems, Foundations of Computer Science, Machine Intelligence, Programming Languages, Security, Software Engineering, Systems Software
Description: Computer science is a discipline that involves the understanding and design of computers and computational processes. In its most general form, it is concerned with the understanding of information transfer and transformation. Particular interest is placed on making processes efficient and endowing them with some form of 'intelligence.' The discipline ranges from theoretical studies of algorithms to practical problems of implementation in terms of software and hardware.
Accredidation: The Computer Science program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Construction Engineering Minor
Requirements: Students must have completed the First Year Engineering (FYE) program and be enrolled in a degree-granting engineering program. All prerequisite courses must be satisfied. Required Courses (18 credits): CE 22200 - Biomechanics Or CE 27000 - Introductory Structural Mechanics; CE 32201 - Project Control and Life Cycle Analysis; CE 35000 - Environmental Engineering I Or CE 35500 - Engineering Environmental Sustainability; CE 42100 - Construction Project Management; CE 42400 - Human Resource Management in Construction; CEM 20100 - Introduction to Construction Management.
Department: Division of Construction Engineering and Management
Description: The Lyles School of Civil Engineering offers a minor in Construction Engineering to students in the Schools of Engineering. The Construction Engineering Minor is designed for students who are interested in the construction industry and wish to enhance their engineering education with a focus on construction management and engineering.

ProgramName: Construction Engineering, BSCNE
Requirements: Admission to the Lyles School of Civil Engineering is through the First-Year Engineering Program. Students who are interested in Construction Engineering and Management (CEM) enter the program after completing the First-Year Engineering (FYE) requirements.
Concentration: Mechanical Emphasis, Electrical Emphasis, General Emphasis
Description: Construction Engineering (CNE) is a unique program that blends engineering and management. Construction Engineering focuses on the design and execution of construction processes to create infrastructure. The program provides students with a solid foundation in engineering principles and construction management. Students will learn about structural design, construction materials, project scheduling, cost estimation, and legal aspects of construction.
Accredidation: The Construction Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Construction Graphics Minor
Requirements: Minor Code: CGRA. At least 15 credit hours are required for this minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. Any course used to fulfill this minor must be taken on a graded basis. Required Courses: CGT 11000 - Technical Graphics Communication (3.00 credits), CGT 16400 - Graphics For Civil Engineering And Construction (3.00 credits), CGT 26200 - Introduction To Construction Graphics (3.00 credits), CGT 36200 - Applications Of Construction Graphics (3.00 credits), CGT 46200 - Virtual Design And Construction (3.00 credits).
Description: Construction graphics is an important component of the construction industry. As modern technology advances, the use of graphics is essential to every segment of the industry. The construction graphics minor focuses on the graphical representation and communication of information between owners, designers, and contractors during the design and construction phases of a building project.

ProgramName: Construction Management Minor
Requirements: Students must have a 3.0 cumulative GPA to be eligible for the minor. A maximum of 40 students per year will be admitted to the minor. Students must have completed 30 credit hours. Minor applications will be accepted twice a year (August 1st through September 1st and January 1st through February 1st). All Construction Management (CM) courses are restricted to those who are admitted to the minor or a CM major.
Department: Polytechnic Institute (School of Construction Management Technology)
Description: The minor in construction management provides an opportunity for students in other disciplines to gain an understanding of the management of construction projects. The minor is available to any student outside of the construction management major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Construction Management Technology,
Requirements: Admission to the Construction Management Technology program is based on the general Purdue University requirements for admission as an undergraduate student. These include high school course expectations: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, Geometry, and a fourth year of higher math), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single Foreign Language (recommended but not required). Purdue's admission process is holistic and also considers SAT or ACT scores, grades, and a personal essay.
Description: Construction management is the act of managing the construction process. It is a professional service that uses specialized, project management techniques to oversee the planning, design, and construction of a project, from its beginning to its end. The purpose of construction management is to control a project’s time, cost and quality. Construction managers are responsible for coordinating and managing people, materials, and equipment; budgets, schedules, and contracts; and the safety of employees and the general public. Construction management technology is a good fit for people who are interested in the construction industry, want to lead and manage people, and like to see a tangible result for their work. The Construction Management Technology (CMT) program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills to lead in the construction industry. The CMT program is management-oriented and provides a wide range of educational experiences, including both technical and management courses. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in many areas, including: building information modeling; construction graphics; construction surveying; materials and methods; scheduling; cost estimating; construction law; and structures. In addition to technical and management courses, the curriculum also includes courses in: communication; humanities; social sciences; and leadership. This well-rounded education prepares students for a variety of career opportunities in the construction industry.
Accredidation: The Construction Management Technology program is accredited by the American Council for Construction Education (ACCE), 825 W. Bitters Rd., Suite 103, San Antonio, TX 78216. Telephone: 210.495.6161. Website: www.acce-hq.org.

ProgramName: Creative Writing Minor
Requirements: A minor in creative writing is available for all students at Purdue University, with the exception of English majors in the Creative Writing concentration. The minor consists of 15 credits, including an introductory course (ENGL 20500 - Introduction To Creative Writing) and 12 credits of elective courses chosen from a specific list.
Description: The Creative Writing minor is designed to help students grow as writers of poetry and/or fiction. Students take a series of workshops and courses in literature and craft.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing,
Requirements: Degree: MFA; Area of Study: Creative Writing; Total Credit Hours Required: 42; Minimum GPA: 3.0; TOEFL: 77 (Minimum subscores: Reading 19, Listening 14, Speaking 18, Writing 18); Writing Sample: Required; Resume: Required; Statement of Purpose: Required; Letters of Recommendation: 3; GRE - General Test: Not Required; GRE - Subject Test: Not Required.
Concentration: Poetry and Fiction
Description: The MFA program in creative writing at Purdue is a three-year residency program. Its primary goal is to provide talented writers with the time and support to develop their craft. Students take workshops in fiction and poetry, craft classes, and literature seminars. The program also offers opportunities for students to serve on the staff of the Sycamore Review, our nationally recognized literary journal.

ProgramName: Crop Science Minor
Requirements: Credit Hours: 18-19. Required: AGRY 10500 (3 cr.), AGRY 37500 (3 cr.), AGRY 50500 (3 cr.). Selectives: 9-10 credits from the following: AGRY 25500, AGRY 33500, AGRY 33700, AGRY 45000, AGRY 48000, AGRY 51500, AGRY 52500, AGRY 53500, BTNY 30100, BTNY 30400, or ENTM 30600. At least 9 credits must be 30000 level or higher. A minimum of 6 credits must be taken at the West Lafayette Campus. Credits from 'Pass/No Pass' courses do not count toward this minor.
Description: The Crop Science minor provides students with a foundation in the principles of crop production and management. It includes courses in plant science, soil science, and pest management, as well as elective courses in crop physiology, weed science, and crop ecology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Crop Science,
Requirements: Crop science is a professional field that includes the study of plant genetics and breeding, plant physiology, crop production and management, and weed science. General admission requirements for freshmen at Purdue include the completion of 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. A personal essay and official SAT or ACT scores are also required. The Crop Science, BS program requires a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation.
Concentration: International Agriculture, Plant Breeding and Genetics, Crop Management
Description: The crop science major is designed for students who are interested in the basic sciences related to crop production. Students in this major take a core of courses in chemistry, biology, mathematics, and physics. They also take courses in crop production, genetics, plant physiology, and soil science. The major is flexible and allows students to choose from several concentrations, including plant breeding and genetics, crop management, and international agriculture. Graduates of this major are prepared for careers in research, industry, and government, or for graduate study in the plant sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Cybersecurity, BS program, freshman applicants are evaluated based on high school coursework (including English, Math, Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), overall grades and grade trends, and SAT or ACT test scores. Purdue University requires a complete application through the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. For this specific program, students must complete a total of 120 credits, maintaining a minimum GPA as required by the Polytechnic Institute.
Description: The Cybersecurity major provides a comprehensive education in the technical and non-technical aspects of cybersecurity. Students learn how to design, implement, and manage secure information systems, and how to detect and respond to security threats. The program also covers the legal and ethical issues related to cybersecurity. Graduates are prepared for careers in a variety of cybersecurity roles, including security analyst, security engineer, and digital forensics investigator.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science program in Cybersecurity is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Cybersecurity and Similarly Named Computing Programs.

ProgramName: Dance Minor
Requirements: Minors are only available to students already enrolled in a Purdue degree program. Credits Required: 17. Some courses within the minor, such as DANC 25000 and DANC 35000, have enrollment limitations based on previous course completion or by audition.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Dance Minor provides students with a broad base of study in the field of dance. The required coursework involves the student in three areas: technique, theory/history, and performance. In addition to a core of required courses, students may choose to emphasize one area of dance more than others (e.g. technique, choreography, or history/theory) through their choice of elective courses.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications (DATA), BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission requirements. This includes the completion of high school coursework: 4 years of English, 4 years of Mathematics (including Pre-Calculus or equivalent), 3 years of Laboratory Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. Purdue University is a test-required university; students must submit SAT or ACT scores. Admission is competitive and based on high school GPA, rigor of curriculum, and standardized test scores.
Description: The major in Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications (DATA) provides students with a strong foundation in data science, including statistical and computational methods, and their application to real-world problems. Students will learn how to collect, manage, analyze, and interpret large and complex data sets, and how to communicate their findings to a variety of audiences. The major is designed to prepare students for careers in a wide range of fields, including business, government, and non-profit organizations. This major provides a curriculum that integrates the areas of statistics, computer technology, and data science. Students will gain the skills and knowledge to manage, analyze, and interpret data to solve complex problems and inform decision-making in various industries. The program focuses on hands-on learning and practical application of data analytics tools and techniques.

ProgramName: Data Driven Agriculture Minor
Requirements: The Data Driven Agriculture minor is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge of how data and data-driven technology are used in the agricultural industry. To earn the minor, students must complete 15 credits from the specified course list. A minimum of 6 credits must be at the 30000 level or higher. The minor is available to any student at Purdue University.
Description: The undergraduate minor in Data Driven Agriculture will prepare students with the knowledge and skills to utilize data and information technology to improve the efficiency, productivity, and sustainability of agriculture and natural resources. This minor provides a foundational understanding of data science and its applications in the agricultural and natural resources industries. Students will develop proficiency in data management, analysis, and visualization, and will learn to apply these skills to solve real-world problems in agriculture and natural resources.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Science,
Requirements: Purdue University's admission process is holistic. For freshman applicants to programs like Data Science, the following are required: a completed Common Application including the personal essay and Purdue-specific questions, official high school transcripts, and official SAT or ACT scores. Admission is competitive and based on high school course expectations, grades in core academic areas, and the strength of the high school curriculum.
Description: Data Science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from data in various forms, both structured and unstructured. Data Science is essentially a combination of Statistics and Computer Science. It is a field that is growing rapidly and has a wide range of applications in industry, government and academia.

ProgramName: Design and Innovation Minor
Requirements: Admission to the minor is through the student’s home college. The program requires 15-18 total credits, consisting of a Foundational Course (TECH 12000 or TECH 12000H), a Required Course (ENGR 20100), and 9-12 credits of breadth and depth selectives.
Department: Honors College and the Purdue Polytechnic Institute
Description: The Design and Innovation minor provides students with the chance to engage in collaborative, design-based projects to identify and solve problems. This minor prepares students for careers and further study in a variety of fields, including: high-tech, business, non-profit, and education. It is open to students in any major, who want to develop their ability to communicate, innovate and lead. The minor is a partnership between the Honors College and the Purdue Polytechnic Institute, with additional contributions from the College of Liberal Arts and the Krannert School of Management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Developmental and Family Science,
Requirements: Admission to the Developmental and Family Science major is based on freshman admission criteria including high school course preparation (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of laboratory science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a single foreign language), SAT or ACT scores, academic achievement, and an application essay. The degree requires 120 total credits for graduation, including 36 credits of major-specific courses.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: Child Development, Family and Community Health, Human Development and Family Science
Description: Developmental and Family Science is for students who are interested in people and in improving the lives of individuals and families. It is an interdisciplinary study of the development of individuals and families across the lifespan in various contexts. You will learn about the physical, cognitive, social and emotional development of humans and how to work with people in a variety of settings.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Digital Criminology,
Requirements: Purdue reviews every application holistically, looking for students who will succeed and contribute to the campus community. Factors considered include high school course expectations (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language), grades in core academic courses, strength of curriculum, SAT or ACT test scores, personal background and experiences, a personal statement (essay), and Purdue-specific questions.
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Digital Criminology is a joint program between the Department of Sociology and the Department of Computer and Information Technology. This program addresses the convergence of the physical and digital worlds, and how that impacts crime and its investigation. The program provides students with the foundational and specialized knowledge in both Sociology and Computer and Information Technology to analyze cybercrime and cybersecurity from a social science perspective.

ProgramName: Digital Natural Resources Minor
Requirements: Only students with a declared major in Forestry (FORS) or Wildlife (WILD) are eligible for this minor. Students must complete a minimum of 18 credits from the lists below. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. All courses must be taken at Purdue University.
Description: The Digital Natural Resources minor is intended to provide students with a strong foundation in the use of digital technologies for managing natural resources. Students will learn to use geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and other digital tools to collect, analyze, and visualize data related to natural resources.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in UX Design,
Requirements: The User Experience Design (UX Design) major will provide students with the skills and knowledge to design digital products and services. Students will learn about the design process, including research, ideation, prototyping, and testing. To earn the degree, students must complete 120 total credit hours, which include 45 credits of program major courses. Students must earn a C- or better in all CGT courses that are required for the major. Admission is based on a holistic review of high school coursework, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal statement.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs,
Requirements: The Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs (ECEN) program is a joint program between the Department of Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) in the College of Health and Human Sciences and the Department of Educational Studies (EDST) in the College of Education. Students are required to complete 120 credit hours.
Description: The Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs (ECEEN) program focuses on the development and education of children from birth through age 5 (Pre-K). This program provides a strong foundation in child development and prepares students to work with children who are developing typically as well as those with exceptional needs. The curriculum includes course work in child development, early childhood education, and special education, along with extensive supervised field experiences. Students who complete the ECEEN program are eligible for Indiana licensure in both Early Childhood Education (Infant-Grade 3) and Early Childhood Special Education (Infant-Grade 3).
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences Minor
Requirements: The Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences minor is available to all students except those in the Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences major. The minor consists of 15 credits in EAPS courses as follows: 1. One introductory EAPS course selected from: EAPS 10000, 10400, 10500, 10900, 11100, 11200, 11300, 11600, 11700, 12000, 12500, 12900, 13800, 22100, or 22500. 2. At least 12 additional credits in EAPS courses at the 20000 level or higher. 3. At least 6 of the 12 additional credits must be at the 30000 level or higher. 4. No more than 6 credits of EAPS 39100 or 49100 may be used toward the minor.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Ecology, Evolution, and Environmental Sciences,
Requirements: To apply for the Ecology, Evolution, and Environmental Sciences, BS program, freshman applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required documents include high school transcripts and official SAT or ACT scores. High school coursework requirements for the College of Agriculture include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of laboratory science (biology, chemistry, and physics), 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a world language.
Description: Students in the ecology, evolution and environmental sciences (EEES) major learn to think like a scientist as they explore how nature works. They gain a solid foundation in biology, chemistry and physics while studying the environment at all levels — from the genes of individual organisms to the interactions of species and their roles in ecosystems. EEES students have the flexibility to customize their education by choosing from a wide range of elective courses that align with their career goals, whether they involve research, conservation, or environmental policy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics Honors,
Requirements: Economics Honors majors must have a Major GPA of 3.5 or higher and a Cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher at time of graduation. The program requires the completion of specific quantitative coursework including Calculus I (MA 16100 or MA 16500) and Calculus II (MA 16200 or MA 16600). Additionally, students must complete a 3-credit Senior Honors Thesis (ECON 49900).
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The economics honors program is designed for students who want a more rigorous curriculum in economic theory and quantitative methods. It is excellent preparation for graduate study in economics, business, or law, and for professional careers requiring strong analytical skills.
Accredidation: AACSB International

ProgramName: Economics Minor
Requirements: Minors are only available to students with a non-Economics major. 1. A minimum grade of C- is required in each course in the minor. 2. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken in residence at the West Lafayette campus. 3. Students must have a 2.0 overall GPA to enter the minor. 4. Admission to the minor requires at least a 2.0 GPA in ECON 25100 and ECON 25200 (or equivalent).
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The Economics minor is intended for students who want to supplement their major with a strong foundation in economic theory and its applications. It is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of how markets work and how individuals and firms make decisions.
Accredidation: Accredited by AACSB International

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics,
Requirements: Students must complete 120 credits for the degree. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required for graduation. Students must complete a minimum of 32 credit hours of coursework at the 30000 level or above at the Purdue University West Lafayette campus. Requirements include Economics Major Courses (30 credits), Other Departmental / Program Course Requirements (44-67 credits), Electives (23-46 credits), and University Core Requirements.
Description: Economics is the study of how people make choices under conditions of scarcity and of the results of those choices for society. Economic analysis is a powerful tool used to understand how markets work, how people make decisions, and why some societies are wealthier than others. Students learn how to analyze data, how to think logically about complex issues, and how to communicate their findings to others. The BA in Economics is designed for students who want a broad education in the liberal arts and sciences, combined with a strong foundation in economic theory and applications. The program provides students with the analytical skills and knowledge needed for careers in business, government, law, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in economics, business, and other fields.
Accredidation: The Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics,
Requirements: The Economics, BS program requires a total of 120 credits for graduation. The curriculum includes Mathematics requirements (MA 16100 or MA 16500), a Business Core, an Economics Core (including ECON 25100, 25200, 34000, 35200, 36000, 45100), and Economics Electives. Students must maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA overall for all courses taken at Purdue and a 2.0 GPA in all ECON courses. Undergraduate admission to Purdue requires the submission of SAT or ACT scores, and students applying to the Daniels School of Business are expected to have a strong mathematical background, typically including at least one semester of calculus.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: Economics is the study of how people and societies choose to use the scarce resources that nature and previous generations have provided. It is a behavioral science that provides a toolkit for understanding and improving decision making in various contexts including finance, health, the environment and public policy. Economics is an excellent major for students who want a strong analytical and quantitative background to prepare for careers in business, government or for graduate study in economics, law or other fields.

ProgramName: Electrical and Computer Engineering Minor
Requirements: 15.00-18.00 credits required. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses used in the minor. Required courses include ECE 20001 (Next Generation Computing), ECE 20007 (Next Generation Computing Lab), ECE 20002 (Electrical Engineering Fundamentals II), and ECE 20008 (Electrical Engineering Fundamentals II Lab). Additionally, 6-9 elective credits of ECE courses at the 20000-level or above are required.
Department: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering

ProgramName: Electrical Engineering Technology Minor
Requirements: A minimum of 15 credits are required for this minor. Students must earn a grade of 'C-' or higher in all minor courses.
Description: The Electrical Engineering Technology minor is for students who want to develop their knowledge and skills in the areas of electricity and electronics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering Technology,
Requirements: Purdue University is test-required, meaning all students applying for freshman admission must submit scores from the SAT or ACT. The admission process evaluates students based on high school coursework, grades, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions. Recommended high school preparation includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.
Description: The Purdue Polytechnic’s degree in electrical engineering technology (EET) is a hands-on, professionally oriented program that provides a combination of courses in electricity, electronics, and computers. You will learn to use computer-based design and analysis tools, work with state-of-the-art equipment in labs, and collaborate on projects with other students. The program provides a balance of theory and hands-on experience that gives you the skills needed to design, develop, and test electrical and electronic systems. EET graduates are prepared for a variety of careers, including electrical and electronics design, system integration, technical sales, and project management. They work in industries such as aerospace, automotive, energy, and telecommunications.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Electrical Engineering, BSEE
Requirements: Admission to the Electrical Engineering BSEE program requires the completion of the Common Application, including the personal essay and Purdue-specific short-answer questions. Applicants must meet high school course expectations, which include 4 years of English, 4 years of Math (including pre-calculus or higher), 3 years of Lab Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. SAT or ACT scores are required for admission. The program also requires the completion of the First-Year Engineering curriculum before transitioning into the Electrical Engineering major.
Department: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Description: The School of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers two undergraduate degrees: the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) and the Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering (BSCmpE). Electrical engineering is a broad field that encompasses many diverse areas such as: Automatic Control; Bioengineering; Communications, Networking, Signal and Image Processing; Fields and Waves; Microelectronics and Nanotechnology; Power and Energy Systems; VLSI and Circuit Design. The BSEE degree provides students with a broad background in the theory and practice of electrical engineering, and the opportunity to specialize in one or more of these areas through elective courses.
Accredidation: The Electrical Engineering (BSEE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Electronic and Time-Based Art Minor
Requirements: 15 credits required. Students must earn a grade of C- or better in all courses for the minor. The program consists of 6 credits of required courses (AD 23300 - Electronic Media Studio I and AD 30400 - Contemporary Art) and 9 credits of elective courses chosen from a specified list of AD courses.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Electronic and Time-Based Art Minor (ETB) is a multi-disciplinary area of study within the Department of Art and Design that is dedicated to the usage of electronics and digital technology in the production of contemporary art. While some classes are specific to a single genre, many take a cross-disciplinary approach. ETB studio courses cover such topics as computer programming for artists, physical computing, digital video, and art and technology history/theory. Students are encouraged to use these tools and concepts in ways that are investigative and experimental, pushing the limits of the media while creating work that is personally and socially relevant.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Elementary Education,
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific supplemental questions. Official high school transcripts and either SAT or ACT scores are required for admission. For the Elementary Education, BA program specifically, students must maintain a minimum 2.80 cumulative GPA and earn a grade of C- or better in all professional education, content, and core courses to remain in the program and meet graduation and licensure requirements.
Description: The Elementary Education program leads to a Bachelor of Arts degree and Indiana initial licensure in Elementary Generalist (K-6). The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the content areas they will teach, as well as the pedagogical knowledge and skills needed to be successful in the classroom. Students in the program complete a series of field experiences in local schools, starting in their freshman year and culminating in a full-semester student teaching experience.
Accredidation: The College of Education at Purdue University is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Engineering and Public Policy Minor
Requirements: The Engineering and Public Policy Minor is available to all students at Purdue University. This minor is available to any student who has a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. The minor requires a minimum of 15 credits. Only courses with a grade of C or better will be counted toward the minor.
Description: The goal of the minor is to provide students with the knowledge and tools they need to better understand the intersection of engineering and public policy and to apply their engineering skills to public policy problems. The minor is designed for students in engineering, but is open to all students at Purdue. This minor is intended to prepare engineering students for careers in the public sector, or for careers in the private sector that involve significant interaction with government. It is also intended to help all students understand the role of technology in public policy and the role of public policy in the development and application of technology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Technology Teacher Education,
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application including a personal essay. Official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores are required for freshman admission. For the Engineering Technology Teacher Education, BS program, students must complete 120 credits for the degree, with at least 32 credits of 30000-level or higher courses taken at Purdue University. To be eligible for teacher licensure, students must maintain a 2.8 GPA and complete all GATE and EDPS courses with a C- or better.
Description: The Engineering Technology Teacher Education (ETTE) program prepares students to become middle and high school teachers in technology and engineering education. ETTE graduates use a variety of laboratory facilities, and state-of-the-art equipment to apply math, science, and technology principles to solve real-world problems. ETTE graduates learn to design, build, and use various technologies to create products, systems, and environments that solve problems. Students are also prepared to teach in a wide range of content areas, including: Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Construction, Communication, Computer Systems, Design, Electronics, Energy and Power, Manufacturing, Robotics, Transportation, and Woodworking. ETTE students also participate in field-based clinical experiences in middle and high schools, and complete a 16-week student teaching internship during their final semester. Upon successful completion of the program, graduates are eligible for an Indiana REPA Initial Practitioner License in Engineering and Technology Education (Grades 5-12).
Accredidation: The Teacher Education Program is a unit of the College of Education at Purdue University that is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and the Indiana Department of Education. The Engineering Technology Teacher Education (ETTE) program is also accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission (ETAC) of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: English Minor
Requirements: The Department of English offers a 15-hour minor for students in other departments and schools. To declare the English minor, students must go to their own academic advisor. Requirements include: One course in British literature (3 cr.); One course in American literature (3 cr.); One course in Shakespeare or early modern literature (3 cr.); Two ENGL electives at the 30000-level or higher (6 cr.). Total Credits: 15.
Description: The English minor consists of 15 credit hours in English, including introductory and upper-division courses. Students choose from courses in literature, creative writing, and professional writing to tailor the minor to their interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English,
Requirements: Purdue University expects applicants to have completed the following high school coursework: 4 years of English, 3 years of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 3 years of Laboratory Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. Purdue University is test-required, meaning SAT or ACT scores are required for undergraduate admission.
Description: The English major provides students with a broad knowledge of literature in English and its historical and cultural contexts, as well as the ability to analyze and interpret texts and to write clearly and persuasively. The program offers a solid foundation in the study of literature, language, and writing, where students explore the diversity of human experience through the analysis of texts and develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills essential for a wide range of careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Entomology,
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Official high school transcripts are required, and Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for students applying for Fall 2025 and beyond. High school students interested in Entomology should have a strong background in science (especially biology and chemistry) and math.
Description: The Entomology major provides a broad background in the life sciences and prepares students for a variety of careers in the public and private sectors. Students study insects and their relatives, their roles in the ecosystem, and their impact on human health, agriculture, and the environment. The curriculum includes courses in insect biology, ecology, physiology, taxonomy, and management, as well as foundational courses in biology, chemistry, and mathematics. Students can choose from several areas of emphasis to tailor their degree to their interests and career goals.

ProgramName: Environmental and Ecological Engineering Minor
Requirements: The Environmental and Ecological Engineering minor provides a path for students in most other engineering majors to explore EEE. Any student in the College of Engineering who is in good standing is eligible to enroll in the EEE minor. Credit Hours: 18.00.
Description: Environmental and Ecological Engineering (EEE) is the multi-disciplinary engineering field that focuses on the protection of human health and the environment through the application of engineering and science. EEE uses a systems approach to solve environmental problems and minimize human impact on the environment. The EEE minor provides students with the opportunity to gain a broader understanding of the principles of EEE and their applications.

ProgramName: Environmental and Ecological Engineering, BSEEE
Requirements: The BSEEE degree requires 128 credit hours. In addition to the University Core Requirements, the EEE program requires the following: General Education Requirements (24 credits), Mathematics Requirements (18 credits), Science Requirements (15 credits), EEE Core (34 credits), EEE Selectives (21 credits), and Technical Electives (6-10 credits). Admission for freshman applicants also requires completion of a college-preparatory high school curriculum including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.
Description: Environmental and Ecological Engineering (EEE) addresses the interactions between human activities and the environment. EEE engineers use engineering and science principles to design systems that protect human health and the environment, and to promote sustainable development. The EEE curriculum is uniquely designed to integrate traditional environmental engineering with ecological engineering and systems thinking. Students in the BSEEE program gain a broad foundation in engineering, biological sciences, and chemistry, and participate in design experiences that address real-world environmental challenges.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental and Ecological Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Environmental Engineering and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering, BSENRE
Requirements: To enter the Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering (BSENRE) program, students must first complete the First-Year Engineering Program (30-32 credits). For undergraduate admission to Purdue University, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required high school coursework includes 8 semesters of Mathematics, 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, and 6 semesters of Social Studies. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.
Department: Agricultural and Biological Engineering (College of Engineering and College of Agriculture)
Description: Environmental and natural resources engineers use their engineering skills to protect our natural resources. They design systems and solutions for environmental problems like water and air pollution, waste management and recycling, and sustainable food and fiber production. Environmental and natural resources engineering is part of the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering.
Accredidation: The Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental and Natural Resources,
Requirements: Admission to the Environmental and Natural Resources, BS program is based on a holistic review of each applicant. Freshman requirements include the completion of specific high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math (including algebra, geometry, and advanced math), 6 semesters of lab science (including biology, chemistry, or physics), 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language. Additionally, applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores and a personal essay.
Concentration: Applied Biology; Environmental Quality; Environmental Policy and Management; Land and Water Resources; Sustainability Science
Description: The Environmental and Natural Resources (ENR) major provides students with a broad background in the biological, chemical and physical sciences, and an understanding of the social, political and economic aspects of environmental and natural resource issues. Students choose one of five concentrations: Applied Biology; Environmental Quality; Environmental Policy and Management; Land and Water Resources; or Sustainability Science. In addition to a solid foundation in the sciences, ENR students develop skills in communication, problem-solving, and critical thinking that prepare them for a wide range of careers in environmental and natural resource management, policy, and research.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Geosciences,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission, freshman applicants must meet high school course requirements including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Evaluation is based on academic achievement, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.
Description: The Environmental Geosciences major provides a sound foundation in the Earth sciences and also incorporates a range of courses in biology, chemistry, and other areas of science. This major is intended for students who wish to pursue careers in environmental consulting, water resources, or other areas of the environmental sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Health Sciences,
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) provides students with the academic and professional skills needed to protect human health by identifying, evaluating, and controlling environmental and occupational hazards. Students in this major take a variety of science courses (e.g., biology, chemistry, physics) and learn how these sciences apply to public and occupational health. Our graduates find employment as environmental health and safety (EHS) professionals in industry (e.g., pharmaceuticals, chemical, automotive, energy, electronics, consulting) and as public health professionals in the government (e.g., EPA, CDC, OSHA, state and local health departments).
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: Environmental Health, Occupational Health Science
Description: Environmental Health is the study of how our environment (air, water, food, and workplace) affects human health. Environmental health professionals use the latest technologies to identify, evaluate, and control chemical, biological, and physical factors in the environment that can cause disease or injury. Students choose from one of two tracks: (1) environmental health science or (2) occupational health science (industrial hygiene). Graduates in environmental health work as sanitarians, hazardous waste specialists, air and water quality specialists, and environmental health and safety (EHS) officers. Graduates in occupational health science work as industrial hygienists (identifying and controlling workplace hazards) or EHS officers. Both tracks prepare students for professional certifications, graduate study in environmental health or other health-related fields, or professional school (medical, dental, or veterinary).
Accredidation: The environmental health science track is accredited by the National Environmental Health Science and Protection Accreditation Council (EHAC). The occupational health science track is accredited by the Applied Science Accreditation Commission (ASAC) of ABET.

ProgramName: Environmental Politics and Policy Minor
Description: The environmental politics and policy minor is for students who want to focus on the political and policy-making processes that shape environmental outcomes. This program provides students with the social science tools to understand environmental problems and the political and economic systems that impact environmental policy.

ProgramName: Event and Meeting Management Minor
Requirements: The event and meeting management minor is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the event and meeting management industry. The minor is available to any Purdue student. A minimum grade of C- is required in each course. Total credits: 15. Required courses include HTM 17300, HTM 20200, and HTM 37300, plus 6 credits of selective courses.
Department: White Lodging-J.W. Marriott, Jr. School of Hospitality and Tourism Management
Description: The Event and Meeting Management minor provides students with a foundational knowledge of the event and meeting management industry. Coursework focuses on the planning, management, and execution of various events including meetings, conventions, and festivals.

ProgramName: Exploratory Studies
Requirements: Exploratory Studies is a one- or two-semester program (up to four semesters maximum) for students who have not yet decided on a major. During their time in the program, students meet with an academic advisor and take a three-credit career planning course (EDPS 10500) designed to help them make informed choices about majors and careers. Students work with their advisors to select a degree-granting major by the end of their fourth semester.
Description: Exploratory Studies is an undergraduate advising program that provides students the opportunity to explore the University’s more than 200 majors before they commit to a specific degree-granting college or school. Students work with a professional academic advisor who is specifically trained to help them with the process of choosing a major. Students can remain in the program for up to four semesters. Students participate in the course EDPS 10500 - Academic And Career Planning, which is designed to help students evaluate their interests, skills, and values as they relate to majors and careers.

ProgramName: Farm Management Minor
Requirements: 18.00 Credits Required. Required Courses (9 credits): AGEC 21700 - Fundamentals Of Agricultural Business Management, AGEC 31100 - Farm Management, AGEC 41100 - Farm Business Management. Elective Courses (9 credits): Select three courses from the following list: AGEC 33000 - Management Of Resident Instruction Farms, AGEC 42100 - Consolidating Tax and Accounting for Agricultural Businesses, AGEC 45100 - Applied Policy Analysis, AGEC 31000 - Farm Organization, AGEC 33100 - Principles Of Selling In Agricultural Business, AGEC 41200 - Farm Business Management Workshop, AGEC 42400 - Financial Management Of Agricultural Business, AGEC 42500 - Estate Planning And Property Transfer, AGEC 45600 - Federal Income Tax Law.
Description: The Farm Management minor is designed to provide students with the business and management skills required to be successful in a production agriculture environment. Students will gain knowledge in the areas of farm management, production economics, farm business and estate planning, and farm business financial management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Farm Management,
Requirements: The Farm Management major provides students with a strong foundation in business and economics, along with a broad understanding of the technical aspects of agriculture. Students learn to apply economic and management principles to the problems of firms in the food and fiber industry. To earn a Bachelor of Science degree in the College of Agriculture, a minimum of 120 credits is required. Students must complete specific requirements in International Understanding, Communication, Humanities and Social Sciences, Mathematics and Physical Sciences, Biological Sciences, and Agricultural Economics. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required for graduation.
Description: The farm management major provides students with the management and economic skills to analyze the complex factors involved in farm operation and business. This major is well suited for students interested in production agriculture, professional farm management, or agribusiness. Farm management graduates often start their careers in farming, agricultural banking and finance, professional farm management, or retail agricultural sales.

ProgramName: Fermentation Sciences Minor
Requirements: A minimum of 15-16 credits is required to complete the minor. Minimum GPA 2.0 (C or better) required in all minor courses. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue.
Department: Department of Food Science, College of Agriculture
Description: The Fermentation Sciences minor provides a core of courses that introduce students to the field of fermentation science. Students will gain an understanding of the biology, chemistry, and processing associated with fermented foods and beverages.

ProgramName: Film and Video Studies Minor
Requirements: A minimum of 15 credits is required for the Film and Video Studies minor. At least 6 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette. Minor is available to undergraduate students. Minimum GPA required: 2.000. Students must apply for the minor through their primary academic advisor.
Description: The Film and Video Studies program (FVS) provides students with a solid foundation in the history, theory, and practice of film, video, and moving-image media. Students may emphasize either history and theory or production, though they are expected to take courses in both areas. The minor in Film and Video Studies complements many major areas of study at the university and offers students the chance to understand the cinematic arts as a form of cultural expression and global communication.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Video Studies,
Requirements: Application to the Film and Video Studies, BA program requires the submission of the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must also provide official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores. The program requires 120 total credits for graduation, including 33 credits in the major (covering Technical/Production and History/Theory), 33-51 credits in the Liberal Arts Core, and 36-54 elective credits. Students must earn a C- or better in all courses used to satisfy the major.
Description: The Interdisciplinary Program in Film and Video Studies provides students with the opportunity to study film and video as art forms and as cultural phenomena. Students may choose from a wide variety of courses in film and video history, theory, and production. The program offers a major and a minor in Film and Video Studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Finance,
Requirements: Admission to the Finance, BS program at Purdue University requires the submission of the Common Application along with a required personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must provide high school transcripts and are required to submit official SAT or ACT scores. Recommended high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including coursework through pre-calculus or calculus), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language.
