For graduation, the program requires the completion of 120 credit hours, a minimum 2.0 graduation GPA, and completion of the Management core and Finance concentration courses.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Concentration: Accounting, Analytical Consulting, Business Analytics, General Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Supply Chain, Information, and Analytics
Description: Finance is the study of how people, institutions, and markets evaluate and manage risk and return. It involves a mix of conceptual analysis, quantitative math, and computer applications. The finance major prepares students for careers in corporate finance, investment management, and the financial services industry. Graduates can pursue careers as financial analysts, portfolio managers, investment bankers, and consultants.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, financial need, and leadership

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Financial Counseling and Planning,
Requirements: Purdue University is test-required. Application criteria for freshman admission includes: High school coursework, grades in core academic subjects, strength of your high school curriculum, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. For the Financial Counseling and Planning, BS program specifically, all CSR courses must be completed with a C- or better and a 2.0 GPA is required for graduation.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Financial Counseling and Planning program focuses on the financial planning process and its application to individuals and families. The program prepares students for professional careers in the financial services industry, including financial planning, counseling, and related fields. Students learn to analyze financial situations, develop and implement comprehensive financial plans, and communicate effectively with clients.
Accredidation: This program is registered with the Certified Financial Planner (CFP) Board of Standards, Inc. and the Association for Financial Counseling and Planning Education (AFCPE).

ProgramName: Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences Minor
Requirements: The Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences minor is open to all Purdue students except those in the Aquatic Sciences and Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences majors. Minor is not available to students on probation. Students wishing to enroll in this minor should consult with the FNR Office of Student Services, FORS 103.
Description: A minor in Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences (FNR) is available to any student at Purdue University with an interest in the field. Students must complete a minimum of 18 credits from the list of courses below. A minimum of 15 credits must be taken at the West Lafayette campus.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Flight (Professional Flight Technology),
Requirements: Admission to the Professional Flight Technology major is for the fall semester only. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for Purdue University. A critical requirement specific to this program is that students must obtain a first-class medical certificate from a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved medical examiner before they begin flight training. The program is highly competitive and is part of the Purdue Polytechnic Institute.
Concentration: Professional Flight Technology
Description: The professional flight program is designed to prepare students for the flight deck of a major commercial airline. Flight students begin flying during the first week of their freshman year and proceed through several certificates and ratings including private pilot, commercial pilot with multi-engine and instrument ratings, and certified flight instructor with an instrument rating. At the completion of the program, students have the qualifications and experience necessary to meet the requirements of any commercial airline.
Accredidation: The Professional Flight program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

ProgramName: Food and Agribusiness Management Minor
Requirements: The minor consists of 15 credits. Note: Open to all students except Agribusiness majors. Required courses include introductory economics (AGEC 20300, AGEC 21700, ECON 21000, or ECON 25100), macroeconomics (AGEC 20400 or ECON 25200), AGEC 33000 (Management Methods for Agricultural Business), and 6 additional credits from AGEC courses numbered 30000-59900 (excluding 33000, 33100, 49600, and 49800).
Description: A student may choose a minor in Food and Agribusiness Management. This minor will provide the student with an opportunity to supplement his or her major with a set of courses that provide a foundation in the management and marketing of firms in the food and agribusiness industry.

ProgramName: Food Science Minor
Requirements: A cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher is required to graduate with a minor. Required Courses (12-13 credits): FS 16100 - Science Of Food, FS 34200 - Food Chemistry, FS 36200 - Food Microbiology, FS 45300 - Food Processing I. Selective Courses (3-5 credits): Select one or two of the following: FS 34100 - Food Analysis, FS 36300 - Food Microbiology Laboratory, FS 44200 - Food Chemistry Laboratory, FS 44400 - Confectionary Science, FS 45400 - Food Processing II, FS 46700 - Food Plant Sanitation, FS 46900 - Food Packaging.
Description: The Food Science minor is designed for students who are interested in the application of the basic sciences (chemistry, microbiology, physics, etc.) to the manufacturing, preservation, storage, and distribution of foods. The minor will provide students with the opportunity to gain a basic understanding of food chemistry and analysis, food microbiology, food processing and food product development. This minor is appropriate for students interested in careers in the food industry, research, and academia.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food Science,
Requirements: Selection of students for the College of Agriculture is based on several criteria: high school record (including courses taken and grades earned); standardized test scores (SAT or ACT); personal statement/essay; and leadership and/or school and community activities. Minimum course requirements for admission to the College of Agriculture include: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 4 semesters of Social Studies, 8 semesters of College Prep Electives.
Description: Food science is an applied science that uses the principles of chemistry, microbiology, and engineering to study the nature of foods, the causes of their deterioration, and the principles underlying food processing. Food science is also the application of this knowledge to the development of new food products and the design of new processes to improve the safety and quality of foods. Students learn the chemistry and microbiology of food, how food is processed, and how to ensure the safety and nutritional value of our food supply. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research, internships, and study abroad programs.
Accredidation: The Food Science major is approved by the Higher Education Review Board of the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT).

ProgramName: Foods and Nutrition Minor
Requirements: Credit Hours: Minimum 15. Required Courses: NUTR 10500, NUTR 10600, NUTR 10700, and either NUTR 20500 or NUTR 30300. Electives: Select from NUTR courses at the 20000-level or higher to total 15 credits for the minor. Additional Requirements: Minimum Grade of C- is required in each course for the minor. Note: Dietetics (DIET-BS) and Nutrition and Dietetics (NUDI-BS) majors are not eligible for this minor.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Foods and Nutrition minor is available to all students except those in the Nutrition Science, Dietetics, or Nutrition, Fitness and Health majors. A minimum of 15 credits is required. Courses used to satisfy the minor requirements must be taken for a grade. A minimum grade of C- is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor. At least 6 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette.

ProgramName: Forensic Sciences Minor
Requirements: The minor in forensic sciences is designed to provide students with a basic foundation in the application of scientific principles to the investigation of crime. This minor is open to all students at Purdue University, with the exception of those majoring in forensic science.
Description: The Forensic Sciences minor is an interdisciplinary minor designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the various aspects of forensic science. Students will learn about the application of scientific principles and techniques to legal matters, including the collection, preservation, and analysis of physical evidence. The minor is open to all students at Purdue University.

ProgramName: Forest Ecosystems Minor
Requirements: The Forest Ecosystems minor is available to all students except those in the Forestry major.
Description: The Forest Ecosystems minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the biological and physical processes in forest ecosystems and the management of these ecosystems for a variety of products and services.

ProgramName: French Cultural Studies Minor
Requirements: Credits: 15.00. Students must complete 6 credits of the minor in residence at Purdue. No more than two courses may be used for both the minor and a French major. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better.
Description: The French Cultural Studies minor is designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of the French-speaking world, through its literature, cinema, history, and politics. This minor requires 12 credits of coursework beyond FR 20200.

ProgramName: French Minor
Requirements: The French minor requires 12 to 15 credits of course work in French at the 30000 level or above. No more than one course taught in English (e.g., FR 33000) can be used to satisfy the requirements for the minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken in residence at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.
Description: The French Minor allows students to develop an intermediate-high level of proficiency in the French language and to gain knowledge and understanding of French and Francophone cultures.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Arts in French, students must complete a total of 120 credit hours. The program requires 33 credit hours of French courses above the level of FR 20200. Students must also complete the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements. Undergraduate admission requires high school transcripts and the submission of SAT or ACT scores.
Description: A major in French at Purdue University gives you the chance to study the language, literature, and culture of France and the French-speaking world. In addition to developing proficiency in the French language, students gain a deep understanding of the history and cultural traditions of France and other Francophone countries. Students are also encouraged to study abroad in a French-speaking country to further develop their language skills and cultural understanding.

ProgramName: Furniture Design Minor
Requirements: The Furniture Design minor is available to all Purdue students. It requires 15 credit hours of study. Required Courses (15 credits) include: AD 23000 - Design I, AD 24200 - Furniture Design I, AD 33000 - Design II, AD 34200 - Furniture Design II, and AD 44200 - Furniture Design III.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Furniture Design minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of furniture design and construction. The minor is available to all students except for those in the Industrial Design program.
Accredidation: The Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Game Development and Design,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, you must meet the following minimum high school course requirements: 8 semesters of English; 8 semesters of Math (including Algebra I, II and Geometry); 6 semesters of Lab Science (including Biology, Chemistry or Physics); 6 semesters of Social Studies; and 4 semesters of Foreign Language (recommended). Additionally, Purdue University is a test-required institution and requires applicants to submit SAT or ACT scores for admission.
Description: The Game Development and Design major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the design and development of digital games. This degree program prepares students to lead the creation and development of digital games through the lenses of art, design, technology, and storytelling. Students gain a deep understanding of the diverse technical and creative processes involved in making games and learn how to apply those skills to various industries including entertainment, education, healthcare, and business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in General Education-Curriculum and Instruction,
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include: high school coursework, overall grades in academic coursework, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. For the General Education: Curriculum and Instruction, BA program specifically, students must complete a total of 120 credits, including University Core requirements (30 credits) and Major Requirements (84 credits). This program is a non-licensure track.
Description: The General Education major is for students who are interested in the field of education but do not intend to teach in a P-12 classroom. This major does not lead to teacher licensure. Students in this major may be interested in working in education-related fields such as non-profit organizations, museums, corporate training, or other community-based organizations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in General Music,
Requirements: Students wishing to major in General Music (BA) must complete an audition for admission into the major.
Concentration: General Music Concentration; Music History and Theory Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in General Music is intended for students who want a broad-based, liberal arts-oriented music degree. This degree provides students with basic musicianship, knowledge of music history and literature, and performance experience. It allows for flexibility in the choice of music electives and is ideal for students who wish to double major or minor in another area of study.
Accredidation: The Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD) and the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Genetics,
Requirements: Admission to Purdue University and the Genetics, BS program is based on a holistic review of several factors. Requirements for freshman applicants include: High School Coursework (completion of minimum high school subject requirements including English, Math, Lab Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), Grades in core academic areas, Strength of your high school curriculum, SAT or ACT test scores, Personal essay (Common App personal statement), and Purdue-specific questions (Supplemental essays).
Description: Genetics is the study of heredity. It is the core of biology, influencing the structure and function of every living cell. Understanding how genetics works is essential to understanding the complexities of life itself. The genetics major is for students interested in how genes influence the development, health and characteristics of organisms. The genetics program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of genetics and their application to a wide variety of biological problems. Students study a wide range of topics, from the molecular structure of genes and genomes to the inheritance patterns in individuals and populations. Graduates are prepared for careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and more.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geology and Geophysics,
Requirements: The Geology and Geophysics major is a flexible program that can be tailored to several different career goals in the solid-earth sciences, including such areas as environmental and engineering geology, petroleum and mineral exploration, and geophysics. The major leads to the Bachelor of Science degree. A total of 120 credits is required for graduation.
Description: Geology and geophysics is the study of the solid earth and the processes that shape it. The Geology and Geophysics major provides a broad foundation in the physical sciences and mathematics, with an emphasis on the study of the Earth’s composition, structure, and history. Students learn to use a variety of tools and techniques to investigate geological and geophysical problems, and to apply their knowledge to a wide range of practical and societal issues, such as natural hazards, resource management, and environmental protection. The curriculum includes classroom, laboratory, and field experiences that prepare students for careers in the energy and mineral industries, environmental consulting, government agencies, and for graduate study.

ProgramName: German Minor
Requirements: The German minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours. Required courses include GER 20100 (German Level III) and GER 20200 (German Level IV), plus 9 credits of German courses at the 30000 level or above. Credits used to satisfy the requirements of a minor may also be used to satisfy other degree requirements (e.g., majors, core, or electives). At least 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue. Grade of C- or better required for all courses.
Description: German remains an important language of international business, research, and culture. A minor in German will help you gain proficiency in the language and familiarize you with the culture and history of the German-speaking world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German,
Requirements: Students must meet the degree requirements of both the University and the College of Liberal Arts. Total Credits: 120.00. Students must complete a minimum of 30 credits of German above the 20200 level. GPA Requirement: 2.0 GPA required in all German courses.
Description: The German major offers students the opportunity to gain a high level of proficiency in the German language while also exploring the literature, culture, and history of German-speaking countries. Our courses cover a wide range of topics, including medieval literature, Enlightenment philosophy, 19th-century realism, modernism, and contemporary German culture. Students are encouraged to study abroad in a German-speaking country to further enhance their language skills and cultural understanding. Graduates with a degree in German pursue careers in a variety of fields, including education, international business, government, and non-profit organizations.

ProgramName: Global Engineering Studies Minor
Requirements: The Global Engineering Studies Minor is designed for students in the College of Engineering who want to formalize their global engineering and professional experiences. The minor requires a minimum of 12 credits total, including ENGR 20200 (Global Engineering Professional Preparation) and ENGR 40200 (Global Engineering Professional Seminar). A minimum of 10 elective credits must be completed from the approved global/cultural courses or foreign language courses. A grade of C or better is required in all courses for the minor. Additionally, students must complete an approved international experience (study abroad, internship, or research) of at least 6 weeks in duration.
Description: Purdue University’s Global Engineering Studies Minor is a cross-disciplinary program that is intended for students who wish to supplement their primary engineering major with a set of courses and international experiences that will help to prepare them for professional practice in an increasingly global environment. Students should have a minimum of 3.0 GPA to be admitted into the program. Students may use up to six credits of engineering-related courses taken during an international study or work experience toward their primary engineering degree with the approval of their degree-granting program.

ProgramName: Global Food and Agriculture Systems Minor
Requirements: The Global Food and Agriculture Systems minor is available to any student at Purdue University. 15 credits total. Students must earn a minimum C- in AGR 20100 and a minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses used to satisfy the minor. At least 50% of the credits must be earned at Purdue University. The minor requires completion of AGR 20100, one Global Food Production course (3 credits), one International Agricultural Issues course (3 credits), one International and Cross-Cultural Perspectives course (3 credits), and an International Study Abroad experience (minimum 3 credits).
Description: The Global Food and Agriculture Systems minor is an interdisciplinary minor available to all students at Purdue University. The minor provides students with a broad understanding of the global food and agriculture system, including the economic, social, and environmental factors that shape it. Students will learn about the challenges and opportunities facing the global food and agriculture system and will develop the skills needed to address these issues in a variety of professional settings.

ProgramName: Global Liberal Arts Studies Minor
Requirements: The Global Liberal Arts Studies minor requires 15.00 total credits. Students must complete 3 credits from an Introductory Liberal Arts course (AGRY 12000, ANTH 10000, HIST 10400, or POL 13000). A mandatory study abroad or international internship of at least 3 credits is required. Distribution requirements include 9 credits total: 3 credits from Global Studies and 6 credits from Global Perspectives. A minimum grade of C- or higher is required in all minor courses, and at least 6 credits must be taken at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.
Description: The Global Liberal Arts Studies (GLAS) minor is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with the opportunity to explore international and global issues from a variety of perspectives.

ProgramName: Global Studies Minor
Requirements: The Global Studies minor is designed for students across the university who want to develop the analytical and practical tools to understand the major issues and problems that affect our world. In addition to a core course, students choose from a list of context courses and language or intercultural options to complete the 12-15 credit minor. Students in the College of Liberal Arts follow the world language requirements of the Global Studies major to complete the language/culture/intercultural portion of the minor. Students in other colleges use the language/culture/intercultural options listed below.
Description: Global Studies is an interdisciplinary minor designed to provide students with a perspective on the globalization of the world and its impact on the local, national and international community. This minor allows students to pursue their interests in the world as a single unit or system, the complex interrelationships of the people and nations of the world, and the multiple ways in which global processes occur. In short, it provides students with a global context for their disciplinary major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies,
Requirements: The Global Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of global issues, processes, and trends. It is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the world and the complex challenges facing it in the 21st century. Students analyze global issues through an interdisciplinary lens, specializing in a specific world region and developing proficiency in a second language. Application requirements for Purdue undergraduate programs include high school transcripts, a personal essay, and SAT or ACT scores.
Concentration: Thematic or Regional
Description: Global Studies is an interdisciplinary major that allows students to explore the ways in which people, ideas, and things have become increasingly interconnected across the globe. Students in the major gain a broad understanding of the historical, political, economic, and cultural processes that shape our world today. The major is designed to be flexible, allowing students to pursue their specific interests through a choice of concentrations and electives. In addition to coursework, students are required to complete a global experience, which can be fulfilled through study abroad, an international internship, or other approved activities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Graphic Design,
Requirements: Students must meet the following requirements to be admitted into the Professional Program in Graphic Design: Completion of AD 10500 Design I, AD 11300 Drawing I, AD 10600 Design II, AD 22800 Visual Communication Design I, and AD 22900 Design History with a minimum GPA of 3.0 in those five courses.
Description: Graphic design is the communication of information and ideas through images and text. At Purdue, the Graphic Design program prepares students for a variety of careers in the field of visual communication. Our curriculum focuses on the development of conceptual, aesthetic, and technical skills. Students learn to use a variety of media to create visual solutions for a wide range of problems. The program also emphasizes the importance of design history, theory, and criticism.
Accredidation: The Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health and Disease,
Requirements: Admission to the Health and Disease, BS program follows Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. Required high school coursework includes 4 years of English, 3-4 years of Mathematics (4 years including pre-calculus, trigonometry, or calculus are required for College of Science majors), 3 years of Laboratory Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. Applicants must also provide SAT or ACT scores and a personal essay. The program requires 120 credit hours for completion, including foundational courses in Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics.
Description: The Health and Disease major provides a solid foundation in the basic sciences (biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics) while allowing students to focus on the study of health and disease from a biological perspective. Students learn how cells and organisms function in health and how these functions are disrupted in disease. This major is excellent preparation for medical, dental, or other health professional schools, as well as for graduate study in the life sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health,
Requirements: The Health, BS program requires a total of 120 semester hours for graduation. The curriculum includes requirements for Civics Literacy Proficiency, Mathematics, Science, Information Literacy, Oral Communication, Quantitative Reasoning, and Science, Technology & Society. Students must also complete major-specific requirements and concentration-specific courses as outlined by the School of Health Sciences.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences

ProgramName: History Minor
Requirements: The History Minor provides students with an opportunity to delve into the study of the human past and to gain a deeper understanding of the world today. By examining the diverse experiences of people across time and space, students develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills that are essential for success in any field. 15 credits in History are required for the History Minor. At least 9 credits must be at the 30000-level or above. At least 9 credits must be taken at the West Lafayette campus.
Description: The minor in History is available to all students in the University. Students from any major can enhance their education with a history minor, which provides them with the opportunity to study a variety of topics, periods, and regions while developing skills in critical thinking, research, and communication.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History,
Requirements: To earn a degree from the College of Liberal Arts, students must complete at least 120 credit hours. They must also complete the College of Liberal Arts Core Curriculum, the requirements for their major, and any other requirements specified by their department or the College.
Description: The study of history provides an essential basis for understanding the contemporary world. History students examine the diverse cultures and societies of the past, and they learn to think critically, research effectively, and communicate clearly. The Department of History offers courses in a wide variety of fields, including United States, European, Latin American, Asian, African, and Middle Eastern history. The History major is flexible, allowing students to pursue their own interests while developing a broad understanding of the past. History graduates are well-prepared for careers in law, business, education, government, and many other fields.

ProgramName: Horticulture Minor
Requirements: The Horticulture Minor provides students with an opportunity to gain knowledge in the art and science of growing and handling fruits, vegetables, and ornamental plants. 18 credits are required. Required courses include HORT 10100 - Fundamentals Of Horticulture and HORT 20100 - Plant Propagation. Students must earn a C- or better in all courses for the minor. A minimum of 9 credits must be 30000-level or higher, and a minimum of 9 credits must be taken at West Lafayette.
Description: A minor in horticulture provides a foundation for students who want to integrate horticulture with other majors such as biology, business, education, communication, entomology, and landscape architecture. Students from all majors are welcome.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticulture,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Science in Horticulture, students must complete a total of 120 credits. The curriculum includes the College of Agriculture Core Requirements (Mathematics and Statistics, Physical Sciences, Life Sciences, Communications, Humanities, Social Sciences, International Understanding, and Multicultural Awareness) and Horticulture-specific core courses. Students must select one of five concentrations: Horticultural Science, Landscape Design, Public Horticulture, Horticultural Production and Marketing, or Turfgrass Science.
Concentration: Horticultural Science, Horticulture Production and Marketing, Landscape Architecture, Public Horticulture, and Sustainable Food and Landscape Systems
Description: Horticulture is the science and art of growing, marketing, and using finished ornamental plants, fruits, and vegetables. It is a diverse field with many career opportunities in production, management, marketing, education, and research. Students can choose from five concentrations: Horticultural Science, Horticulture Production and Marketing, Landscape Architecture, Public Horticulture, and Sustainable Food and Landscape Systems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality and Tourism Management,
Requirements: Admission to the Hospitality and Tourism Management, BS program follows Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes a holistic review of high school coursework (specifically 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of lab science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language), grade point average, SAT or ACT scores, and a required personal essay.
Department: White Lodging-J.W. Marriott, Jr. School of Hospitality and Tourism Management
Description: The Hospitality and Tourism Management (HTM) program provides students with a broad-based education in the management of hospitality and tourism organizations. The curriculum emphasizes the application of management principles to the hospitality and tourism industry, including food and beverage, lodging, tourism, and event management. Students gain practical experience through internships and professional development opportunities. The program prepares graduates for leadership roles in various sectors of the global hospitality and tourism industry.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration (ACPHA).

ProgramName: HTM International Studies Minor
Requirements: A minimum of three weeks of an approved international experience outside the United States is required. The program must be approved by the program director. Documentation of completion of the international experience is required. Students must have been a full-time student for two semesters prior to the international experience and be in good academic standing (GPA 2.0 or higher).
Department: White Lodging-J.W. Marriott, Jr. School of Hospitality and Tourism Management
Description: The international study minor provides students with the opportunity to gain a global perspective on the hospitality and tourism industry. To earn the minor, students must complete at least 12 credit hours of coursework while participating in a Purdue-approved study abroad program.

ProgramName: Human Development and Family Studies Minor
Requirements: The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of how individuals develop and how families function within various contexts. 15 credits are required for the minor. Required courses include HDFS 20100 (Introduction To Family Processes) and HDFS 21000 (Introduction To Human Development). Additionally, 9 credits of electives must be chosen from the following: HDFS 28000, 31100, 31200, 31300, 31800, 33000, 33200, 34100, or 34600. A C- or better is required in each course for the minor. A minimum of 9 credits must be completed at Purdue University and a minimum of 9 credits must be taken at the 30000-level or higher.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The minor in Human Development and Family Studies is available to students in all colleges and schools of the University. It is designed for students who want a better understanding of human development and family life, but do not want to major in the field.

ProgramName: Human Resource Management Minor
Requirements: Students must be admitted to the Krannert School of Management or have completed 45 credit hours to enroll in Krannert (OBHR) courses. A grade of C- or higher is required in all courses for this minor. Minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in minor courses.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: A minor in Human Resource Management (HRM) allows students to learn how to help organizations strategically manage their employees. HRM is the function in an organization that focuses on the recruitment of, management of, and providing direction for the people who work in an organization. The HRM minor provides students with a solid foundation in the concepts and techniques of human resource management, including staffing, training and development, compensation and benefits, and employee relations. The minor is a valuable addition to any major, as it provides students with the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively manage people in any organizational setting.

ProgramName: Human Rights Studies Minor
Requirements: The minor in Human Rights Studies requires 15 credit hours. At least 6 credits must be taken at the 30000-level or higher. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or higher.
Description: Human rights studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws upon a variety of methods and perspectives from the humanities and social sciences to investigate how humans have conceived of rights and how these conceptions have been implemented, ignored, or challenged throughout history and in the present. The minor is intended to prepare students to be informed and engaged citizens in a global society and to provide a foundation for those who wish to pursue further study or careers in law, public policy, non-governmental organizations, or international affairs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Services,
Requirements: Purdue University's admission process is holistic. Requirements for freshman applicants include completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal statement. The university reviews applications based on grades, grade trends, and the strength of the high school curriculum.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Human Services major is a Council for Standards in Human Service Education (CSHSE) accredited program. The human services major provides a strong foundation for students interested in working with children, youth, adults, and families in a variety of human service settings. Students develop knowledge and skills to provide services that help people through every stage of the life cycle. The curriculum covers individual and family development, professional ethics, family and community resource management, diverse family structures and functions, and communication skills. In addition to regular coursework, students take three semesters of supervised field experience, during which they apply their classroom knowledge in real-world settings. Students find employment in a wide range of settings, including community centers, mental health centers, residential treatment programs, child care centers, elder care facilities, and government agencies. The major also provides a solid foundation for graduate study in fields such as social work, counseling, psychology, and public health.
Accredidation: The Human Services major is a Council for Standards in Human Service Education (CSHSE) accredited program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Industrial Design,
Requirements: Admission to the Industrial Design program is a two-stage process. All students are first admitted to the Pre-Industrial Design program. Admission to the Industrial Design program occurs after the first year of study (during the spring semester) and is based upon a review of the student’s first-year course work, a portfolio of work from first-year art and design courses, and a weighted GPA. In the second stage, a limited number of students are selected for the BFA program.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Industrial Design program prepares students for the professional practice of industrial design. Industrial designers create and develop concepts and specifications that optimize the function, value, and appearance of products and systems for the mutual benefit of both user and manufacturer.
Accredidation: The Department of Art and Design is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Industrial Engineering, BSIE
Requirements: Students may be admitted to the School of Industrial Engineering after they have completed the First-Year Engineering Program (FYE) requirements. The First-Year Engineering Program is a prerequisite for all engineering majors. To be eligible for admission to the School of Industrial Engineering, a student must have completed all of the courses in the First-Year Engineering Program. Total Credits Required: 126.00.
Description: Industrial Engineering is the branch of engineering that is concerned with the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, materials, information, equipment, and energy. It draws upon specialized knowledge and skill in the mathematical, physical, and social sciences together with the principles and methods of engineering analysis and design to specify, predict, and evaluate the results to be obtained from such systems. Through their education and training, industrial engineers (IEs) learn to view any organization as a whole system. They focus on improving the way these systems function. Because their focus is on the entire system, IEs can be found in a wide variety of industries: health care, retail, manufacturing, finance, government, transportation, and entertainment.
Accredidation: The Industrial Engineering (BSIE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Management,
Requirements: The Industrial Management major combines a traditional management education with a strong technical component. Students complete a concentration in a technical or quantitative field, such as engineering, science, or technology. This program is unique in its focus on integrating management with technical and analytical fields. Students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours for the degree.
Description: The Industrial Management (IM) program is designed for students who have an interest and aptitude for business management as well as a strong interest in a technical or quantitative area. In addition to the core business and economics courses, IM students choose a concentration in a technical or quantitative area (e.g., computer science, engineering, or science). This enables IM graduates to bridge the gap between a firm’s technical and management functions.
Accredidation: All of the Krannert School of Management’s programs are accredited by AACSB International (the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Innovation and Transformational Change Minor
Requirements: The Innovation and Transformational Change minor is open to any student regardless of major. A minimum of 12 credit hours must be completed for the minor. A 2.0 GPA or higher is required in all courses used to satisfy minor requirements. All courses must be taken for a grade.
Description: A minor in Innovation and Transformational Change (ITC) is for students who want to develop a mindset and tools for innovation and leading change within organizations. Students will explore multiple aspects of innovation, with focus on identifying opportunities, understanding users, creative problem solving, and design thinking. Additionally, students will develop skills for leadership, teamwork, and agility to effectively lead change. Students from any major can earn an ITC minor.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $329.05 per credit hour; Non-resident: $929.50 per credit hour

ProgramName: Insect Biology Minor
Requirements: The Insect Biology minor requires 15-18 credits. Core Requirements (4 credits): ENTM 20600 - General Entomology and ENTM 20700 - General Entomology Laboratory. Additional Requirements: 11 to 14 credits from any other ENTM courses (specifically ENTM 21000, 21800, 22810, 22820, 25220, 31100, 31800, 44200, or 50000-59999). A maximum of six (6) credits from this minor can be used to meet the requirements of a student’s major, another minor, or a certificate. Minimum of nine (9) credits must be taken at Purdue University.
Description: The minor in Insect Biology is intended for students who have an interest in insects but do not have the room in their curriculum for a second major. It can be tailored to meet your individual needs or interests, like forensic entomology, public health, molecular biology, or ecology. The program will help prepare students for graduate study or careers in many fields of biology, as well as broaden your appreciation for the most successful animals on Earth.

ProgramName: Intellectual Property Law for Engineers Minor
Requirements: The minor consists of five courses that are to be taken in sequence: IE 34300 - Engineering Economics, IE 41000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Introduction To Patents, IE 42000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Advanced Patents, IE 43000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Trademarks, Copyrights And Trade Secrets, IE 44000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Intellectual Property Transactions. Total Credits: 15.00.
Description: The Intellectual Property Law for Engineers minor is designed to provide engineering students with a basic understanding of the legal principles that protect technological innovation. Students will learn about the four main areas of intellectual property law: patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets. The minor is intended for students who are interested in pursuing a career in intellectual property law or who want to learn more about how to protect their own inventions and designs.

ProgramName: Integrated Business and Engineering, BSIBE
Requirements: The Integrated Business and Engineering (IBE) degree is a unique interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers at the intersection of business and technology. This degree combines a strong foundation in business principles with a rigorous engineering curriculum, providing students with the analytical and technical skills needed to solve complex problems in today’s global economy. The program is a partnership between the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business and the College of Engineering.
Description: The Integrated Business and Engineering (IBE) degree program prepares students to solve problems at the intersection of business and engineering. This interdisciplinary program, offered jointly by the School of Management and the College of Engineering, provides students with a solid foundation in both business and engineering. IBE graduates will be well-prepared for careers in technical sales, supply chain management, operations, and product management, where they can bridge the gap between technical and business teams.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Integrated Digital Media,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission, applicants should complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Math (including Algebra I, II and Geometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for admission. Admission is also based on factors such as high school grades, the personal essay, and overall academic strength.
Description: Integrated Digital Media (IDM) is an interdisciplinary major that focuses on the creative use of digital technology in art and design. IDM students learn to use a variety of digital tools and techniques to create interactive and time-based media, including web design, motion graphics, video, and sound. The program emphasizes a critical and historical understanding of digital media and encourages students to explore the social and cultural implications of their work. Integrated Digital Media students can pursue careers in web design, motion graphics, video production, game design, and interactive art.
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies,
Requirements: The Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies program is for students who want a solid engineering foundation but who do not plan to practice engineering. IDES provides a pre-professional or a multi-disciplinary education. IDES students must meet with an IDES advisor to develop an individualized Plan of Study. Students are expected to complete the First-Year Engineering program requirements. Students must have a cumulative GPA of 2.50 or higher to be admitted to IDES.
Concentration: Engineering Management, General Engineering, Health Solutions, Visual Design Engineering
Description: The Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies (IDES) program is designed for students who want an engineering education but do not plan to practice engineering. Students in this program want to use their engineering background as a foundation for a career in another field, such as law, medicine, business, or education, or for students whose interests in engineering are not satisfied by one of the traditional professional engineering programs. The IDES program allows students to customize their education by combining a core of engineering courses with a concentration in another field. Students in IDES must choose one of the available concentrations or work with an advisor to create an individualized plan of study. The concentrations currently available in the Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies program are: Engineering Management, General Engineering, Health Solutions, Visual Design Engineering.
Accredidation: The IDES program is not an ABET-accredited engineering program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Interior Design,
Requirements: All Art and Design programs begin with a Foundation program. Students are admitted to the Interior Design program through a selective process that occurs at the end of the freshman year. This selection occurs once a year during the spring semester. The selection process includes a review of the student’s performance in the foundation courses and a portfolio review.
Department: Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance
Description: The Interior Design program is a professional degree program accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA). The program provides a rigorous curriculum that prepares students for the complexities of the interior design profession. Students engage in design studios that address a variety of project types, including residential, commercial, and institutional spaces. The program emphasizes the importance of design thinking, technical knowledge, and professional practice. Graduates are prepared to enter the workforce as entry-level interior designers or to pursue advanced studies in the field.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA)

ProgramName: International Studies in Agriculture Minor
Requirements: The International Studies in Agriculture minor is for students in the College of Agriculture to gain an international perspective through coursework and international experiences. The minor requires 15-21 credits. Credits must include: Required Course (AGR 20100 - Communications Across Cultures, 3 credits), Foreign Language (3-12 credits), International Experience (6-9 credits such as Study abroad, International internship or research), and Electives (3-6 credits). Students should contact the International Programs in Agriculture (IPIA) office to discuss the minor and the international experience requirement.
Description: The International Studies in Agriculture minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to help students better understand the international/global aspects of agriculture and the food industry. This minor will provide students with the opportunity to gain a deeper knowledge of the history, culture, language, and economic, political and social systems of other countries. It is intended to prepare students for careers in the international arena.

ProgramName: Islamic Studies Minor
Requirements: The Islamic Studies Minor requires a minimum of 15 credit hours. This includes a core requirement of ARAB 10100 (Modern Standard Arabic I) for 3 credits and 12 credits of interdisciplinary electives chosen from a specified list of history, political science, religion, sociology, and Arabic courses. Students can count no more than 6 credit hours of Arabic language (ARAB) toward the minor.
Description: The Interdisciplinary Minor in Islamic Studies is intended to give students a multi-disciplinary perspective on the historical and contemporary formations of Islamic society and culture. The minor requires 15 credit hours of course work in Islamic Studies and related fields. Six (6) of these credits must be at the 30000 level or above.

ProgramName: Italian Minor
Requirements: The Italian minor consists of 12 credits of courses in Italian above the 100-level. Only grades of C- or higher can be counted towards the minor. No more than 3 credits of transfer credit can be counted towards the minor.
Description: The Italian program at Purdue University offers students the opportunity to study one of the most important and influential cultures in the world. Students gain proficiency in the Italian language and explore the rich tradition of Italian literature, cinema, and art history. The curriculum is designed to develop communicative competence and cultural awareness, preparing students for careers in international business, education, the arts, and more.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies,
Requirements: Admission to the Italian Studies major requires a 2.0 GPA or better and completion of the LC 10100 and 10200 or LC 10300 or LC 10500 sequence.
Description: The Italian Studies major is an interdisciplinary program of study. In addition to a focus on the Italian language, students may choose from a wide variety of courses in art history, history, philosophy, and other areas.

ProgramName: Japanese Minor
Requirements: Total Credits: 15.00. Students may not take JPNS courses for Pass/Not Pass for the minor. Students with prior knowledge of Japanese should contact the SLC advisor for placement. Required Courses: JPNS 20100 - Japanese Level III, JPNS 20200 - Japanese Level IV, JPNS 30100 - Japanese Level V, JPNS 30200 - Japanese Level VI, and JPNS 40100 - Japanese Level VII.
Description: Students must complete 15 credits of course work in Japanese at the 20000 level or above. No more than six credits of the 15 can be at the 20000 level. All courses must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a minimum grade of C-.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese,
Requirements: To apply for the Japanese, BA program, applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants are required to submit self-reported high school grades and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT). Specific high school coursework requirements include 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Math (Algebra VI, Geometry, and Algebra VII), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. The Japanese, BA program requires 120 total credits for graduation, including 33 credits in the Japanese major and completion of the College of Liberal Arts Core.
Description: The Japanese major provides students with a high level of proficiency in the Japanese language, along with a deep understanding of Japanese culture, literature, and society. Students develop skills in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Japanese, and they explore the rich historical and contemporary contexts of Japan.

ProgramName: Jewish Studies Minor
Requirements: 15 credits required. Minimum grade of C- required for each course. At least 6 credits must be at the 30000 level or above. Only 6 credits of Hebrew language can be used toward the minor.
Description: The Jewish Studies Program is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people. The program offers a minor that is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of Jewish life and thought from antiquity to the present. Students take courses in a variety of disciplines, including history, philosophy, political science, sociology, and English.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology,
Requirements: To earn a degree in Kinesiology, a student must complete the Purdue Core, Health and Kinesiology Degree Core, and the Kinesiology Concentration. A total of 120.00 semester credits is required. Kinesiology majors must earn a C- or better in specific major courses, including BIOL 20300, BIOL 20400, HK 25300, HK 25800, HK 26300, HK 36800, HK 37200, and HK 46500. Application requirements include the submission of high school transcripts, the Common Application personal essay, and SAT or ACT scores.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: Clinical Exercise Physiology, Health and Fitness Professionals, Human Movement/Pre-Professional, Sports Medicine/Athletic Training
Description: The undergraduate major in Kinesiology provides students with a broad knowledge of the physiological, psychological, and sociological aspects of human movement. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for a variety of careers in health-related fields and for graduate study in kinesiology or other healthcare professions.

ProgramName: Landscape Architecture, BSLA
Requirements: The professional Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA) program at Purdue University is a four-year plus one summer co-op program. The program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB). Students are admitted to the professional program through a selective portfolio review process after completing the first year of the Pre-Landscape Architecture curriculum.
Description: Landscape Architecture is the art and science of design, planning and management of the land. Landscape architects design environments that are beautiful, functional, and sustainable. They design parks and playgrounds, trails and greenways, urban plazas and corporate campuses, and large-scale regional plans. The professional program in landscape architecture at Purdue University is a five-year program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA) degree. The studio is the core of the program, where students are challenged with design projects that range from small-scale site designs to large-scale urban and regional plans. The program also includes a required one-year professional co-op experience, which provides students with the opportunity to gain practical experience in a professional office environment.
Accredidation: The Landscape Architecture program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB).

ProgramName: Landscape and Turf Minor
Requirements: The Landscape and Turf Minor is available to all students except those majoring in Landscape Architecture, Sustainable Food and Farming Systems, Horticulture, or Turf Management. To complete the Landscape and Turf minor, 18 credit hours must be earned from the courses listed below. All courses must be taken for a grade. A minimum grade of C- is required in each course for the minor.
Description: The Department of Horticulture and Landscape Architecture offers a minor in Landscape and Turf to all students in the University. This minor is not available to students in the landscape architecture or turf management and science majors. This minor is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge of plants and their management in the landscape.

ProgramName: Landscape Management Minor
Requirements: Students must have completed 30 credit hours and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. Courses must be completed with a grade of C or better. Students must complete at least 10 credits towards the minor that are not used to fulfill their major's requirements.
Description: Landscape Management is a diverse and growing professional field that includes the design, installation, and management of residential and commercial landscapes. The Landscape Management minor is intended for students who have an interest in some aspect of the green industry and would like to learn more about the plants used in landscapes, how to select those plants and where to use them, and the sustainable methods for managing landscapes. The courses focus on the business of the green industry and the science of plant health and sustainable landscape management.

ProgramName: Latin American and Latino Studies Minor
Requirements: The interdisciplinary minor in Latin American and Latino Studies is designed to provide students with a broad and systematic approach to the history, politics, culture, and society of Latin America and of Latino/a communities in the United States. 12 credits. Select 12 credits from the lists below. At least 6 credit hours must be taken at the 30000 level or above. Course credits used to satisfy the requirements for a minor may not be used to satisfy the requirements for another minor.
Description: The Latin American and Latino Studies Program (LALS) provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the peoples and cultures of Latin America and the Latino experience in the United States. LALS offers a minor that complements a wide variety of majors in the humanities, social sciences, and professional fields. Our curriculum covers a broad range of topics, including history, literature, politics, sociology, and the arts. Through this minor, students will gain a deeper appreciation for the diverse cultural heritage of the Americas and develop a critical understanding of the historical and contemporary issues facing Latin American and Latino communities.

ProgramName: Law and Society Minor
Requirements: 15 credits are required. Required Course (3 credits): SOC 32400 - Introduction To Law And Society. Electives (12 credits): Select 12 credits from the following: ANTH 37900, COM 25000, COM 35300, HIST 33300, HIST 33400, HIST 38200, HIST 38300, PHIL 27000, PHIL 28000, POL 32700, POL 36000, POL 41100, POL 43300, POL 43500, PSY 35000, SOC 32600, SOC 32700, SOC 32800, SOC 40200, SOC 41100, SOC 52500, SOC 52600. Notes: A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in all courses taken for the minor. At least 6 credits must be taken at the Purdue-West Lafayette campus.
Description: The Law and Society minor provides students with an overview of the role of law in society and an opportunity to explore the relationship between law and other social institutions. The minor is designed for students who are interested in law and legal institutions, as well as those who are interested in social problems and social change.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Law and Society,
Requirements: Admission to the Law and Society, BA program is based on a holistic review of several factors, including: High School Coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), Grades in Academic Coursework, Strength of High School Curriculum, Trends in Achievement, SAT or ACT scores, and a Personal Essay.
Description: The Law and Society major provides a broad-based liberal arts education and is an excellent major for students who are interested in law-related careers. The program is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to the study of law and legal institutions and to the relationship between law and society. The major is interdisciplinary and includes courses from several departments across the university. Students in the Law and Society major will learn about the role of law in society, the relationship between law and social change, and the ways in which law is used to address social issues.

ProgramName: Learning Sciences in Educational Studies Minor
Requirements: The Learning Sciences in Educational Studies minor is available to any student at Purdue University with an interest in learning and education. A grade of C- or higher is required in all courses used for the minor.
Description: The Learning Sciences in Educational Studies minor is designed for students who are interested in the study of learning, instruction, and technology. Students will explore how people learn and how to design effective learning environments in a variety of settings.

ProgramName: LGBT Studies Minor
Requirements: The LGBT Studies Minor is an interdisciplinary minor that requires 15 credit hours. Students must take WGSS 28200: Introduction to LGBT Studies and 12 credits from the following list. No more than two courses (6 credits) may be taken in any one department (e.g. SOC, HIST, ENGL). All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better.
Description: The LGBT Studies minor provides students with an interdisciplinary program of study that explores the historical, social, and cultural contexts of sexualities and gender identities. Students will learn about the diverse experiences and expressions of LGBT people, as well as the impact of heteronormativity and cisnormativity on society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts,
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in the College of Liberal Arts at Purdue University, freshman applicants must meet high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Additionally, Purdue requires a personal essay submitted via the Common Application and official SAT or ACT scores. Admission is determined through a holistic review process that considers academic performance, test scores, and personal background.
Description: The Liberal Arts major is designed for students who desire a broad-based, liberal arts education rather than a specialized major. It provides a flexible curriculum that allows students to explore multiple disciplines in the humanities, social sciences, and the arts. Students will develop critical thinking, communication, and analytical skills through a diverse range of coursework.

ProgramName: Linguistics Minor
Requirements: The Linguistics minor provides students with a general introduction to the field of linguistics, plus a solid foundation in the two primary areas of linguistics (phonology and morphology/syntax). Students then have the opportunity to take two additional courses in areas of linguistics that most interest them. Required Courses (9 credits): LING 20100 - Introduction To Linguistics, LING 31100 - Fundamentals Of Phonology, LING 31500 - Fundamentals Of Morphology And Syntax. Elective Courses (6 credits): Select two courses from the following list: LING 31200, LING 31300, LING 31700, LING 32100, LING 36800, LING 39800, LING 49000, LING 49800, LING 50000-level and above, or SLC 30000-level and above. Total Credits: 15.00.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguists examine how language is structured, how it is acquired, how it is used, and how it changes. Since language is a human phenomenon, linguistics is a social science. Since language is also a cognitive phenomenon, linguistics is a part of cognitive science. At the same time, because linguistics deals with the products of the human mind, it is one of the humanities. The linguistics minor is an interdisciplinary minor designed to introduce students to the field of linguistics and to its applications. To meet the requirements for the minor in linguistics, students must take 15 credits of course work, including LING 20100 (Introduction to Linguistics) and LING 31100 (Fundamentals of Phonology) or LING 31500 (Fundamentals of Morphology) or LING 32100 (Fundamentals of Syntax).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics,
Requirements: To apply for the Linguistics, BA program, applicants must submit the Common Application or the Purdue application, which includes Purdue-specific essay questions. Applicants must meet high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, Purdue University requires the submission of SAT or ACT scores for freshman admission.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. It seeks to answer such questions as: What do all languages have in common? How do languages differ? How do children acquire language? How does language change over time? How is language processed in the brain? Linguistics is an interdisciplinary field that draws on insights from many different areas, including psychology, philosophy, computer science, and anthropology. The linguistics major provides students with a strong foundation in the core areas of linguistics: phonology (the study of sound systems), morphology (the study of word structure), syntax (the study of sentence structure), and semantics (the study of meaning). In addition, students can choose from a variety of elective courses in areas such as sociolinguistics, historical linguistics, psycholinguistics, and computational linguistics.

ProgramName: Management Minor
Requirements: 2.0 average GPA for all minor courses. All courses must be taken for a grade (no P/N). A minimum of 9 credits must be completed at Purdue West Lafayette. The Management minor is not available to students in the School of Management. Students should consult with their academic advisor to add the minor.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The Management minor is available to students in all majors except those in the Krannert School of Management. Students must have a minimum of 50 percent of the credits (8 hours) for the minor taken at Purdue. A minimum grade of C- or higher must be earned in all courses for the minor. Students must have a 2.0 GPA in the minor courses to graduate with the minor. The program requires 15.00 total credit hours.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Management,
Requirements: Admission to the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is competitive and based on a holistic review of academic achievement (high school coursework and grades), standardized test scores, and personal background. For students applying for the Fall 2024 term and beyond, Purdue University is test-required (SAT or ACT). To earn the Bachelor of Science degree in Management, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, including University Core requirements, the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business Core, and Management Major courses.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Concentration: Accounting, Analytical Consulting, Business Analytics and Information Management, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Operations and Supply Chain Management, and Strategy, Structure and Organizations
Description: The Management major provides students with a broad-based education in business and management, covering various functional areas of business. All Management students choose at least one concentration to develop depth in a specific area. Concentrations are available in: Accounting, Analytical Consulting, Business Analytics and Information Management, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Operations and Supply Chain Management, and Strategy, Structure and Organizations. Students may also choose to complete a second concentration or a minor to further tailor their degree to their career interests.
Accredidation: The Krannert School of Management is accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Manufacturing Minor
Requirements: The Manufacturing Minor is designed for students in Management, Science, Technology and Engineering to provide them with the opportunity to explore technical, economic, and management issues related to manufacturing. Students must complete 18 credit hours.
Description: Manufacturing is an essential part of the engineering process that takes a concept and creates a physical product. This minor is intended for students in an engineering or technology program who have an interest in manufacturing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marketing,
Requirements: To be considered for admission, you must submit: a completed Common Application, the Purdue-specific questions and essay, self-reported or official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores. Purdue is a test-required university. For the 2024-25 application cycle, we require either the SAT or ACT for all freshman applicants.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The Marketing major provides students with the fundamental concepts and the analytical tools needed to develop and implement marketing strategies. Marketing graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in brand management, marketing research, professional selling, and retail management. Marketing consists of those activities that anticipate and satisfy consumer needs and wants through an exchange process. These activities include marketing research, product development, pricing, distribution, and promotion. The study of marketing is helpful for any organization that provides a product or service to a customer.
Accredidation: The Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Materials Science and Engineering Minor
Requirements: Minor Code: MTLS. 15-16 Credit Hours. Students must have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher. Students must receive a 'C' or higher in MSE 23000 to move on to selectives. Minor is not available to Materials Science and Engineering majors.
Description: Materials engineering is an interdisciplinary field that involves the study of the structure, properties, and processing of materials and how these factors affect the performance of the materials in various applications. The minor in Materials Science and Engineering is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the field and to prepare them for careers in a variety of industries where an understanding of materials is important.

ProgramName: Materials Science and Engineering, BSMSE
Requirements: All students must complete the First-Year Engineering program requirements before entering the Materials Science and Engineering program. The program requires a minimum of 126 credits for graduation, which includes core engineering courses, 27 credits of MSE Technical Electives, and 18 credits of General Education Electives. Additionally, students must earn a minimum grade of C- in specific core courses: MSE 23000, 23500, 26000, 27000, 33500, 37000, and 38200.
Department: School of Materials Engineering, College of Engineering
Description: Materials engineering is an interdisciplinary field that investigates the relationship between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Materials engineers design, produce, and test materials for a wide range of applications, from medical devices and electronic components to aerospace structures and energy systems. The School of Materials Engineering offers a program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering (BSMSE). The curriculum is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the structure, properties, processing, and performance of all classes of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and electronic materials.
Accredidation: The Materials Science and Engineering (BSMSE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Economics,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Mathematical Economics, BS program, first-year applicants must meet Purdue's high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or higher), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Additionally, Purdue is a test-required institution, requiring the submission of SAT or ACT scores, and applicants must complete a personal essay as part of the Common Application.
Department: College of Science and Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The Mathematical Economics major is designed to provide students with the mathematical and statistical skills needed for graduate study in economics and for quantitative careers in business and government. It is a joint program offered by the Department of Economics in the Krannert School of Management and the Department of Mathematics in the College of Science.

ProgramName: Mathematics Minor
Requirements: 15-18 Credits Required. All courses for the Mathematics minor must be completed with a grade of C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette. Any course required for the minor may be used as an elective in any other major or minor. No course may be used to satisfy more than one requirement for the minor.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Mathematics, BS program at Purdue University, applicants must meet general freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of a high school curriculum with 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Additionally, Purdue requires the submission of official SAT or ACT scores and the completion of the personal essay provided in the Common Application.
Description: The Mathematics Department offers several programs leading to the Bachelor of Science degree. Mathematics is the study of number, structure, and change. The basic major provides a solid foundation for those who want to use mathematics in another field, such as business, law, or medicine. The Mathematics major is also good preparation for graduate study in mathematics, statistics, or a related field. Students may choose from several different plans of study: Mathematics; Mathematics Education; Applied Mathematics; Business Mathematics; Mathematics/Computer Science; Mathematics/Statistics; or Operations Research.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering Technology,
Requirements: Admission to the Mechanical Engineering Technology BS program requires completion of high school coursework including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Pre-calculus or higher), 6 semesters of Lab Science (Chemistry and Physics are recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. The program itself requires 120 credit hours for graduation and is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET.
Description: Mechanical Engineering Technology (MET) is a broad field of study. It includes such areas as: design and analysis of machines and mechanisms; manufacturing and production processes; fluid power and thermal systems; and engineering materials and their applications. MET students learn how things are made and how they work. They learn to use computer-aided design (CAD) software, 3-D modeling, and advanced simulation tools. In addition to technical courses, students also take courses in communications, humanities, and social sciences.
Accredidation: The Mechanical Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Mechanical Engineering, BSME
Requirements: To earn the degree of Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering (BSME), a student must complete the 128-credit hour program. To be eligible for graduation, a student must earn a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in all courses taken at Purdue University and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in all ME courses (ME GPA). Most students are admitted to the School of Mechanical Engineering after completing the First-Year Engineering (FYE) program.
