General freshman application requirements for Purdue include the Common Application, a personal essay, Purdue-specific questions, high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores.
Description: Mechanical engineering is the broadest of the engineering professions, and its practitioners can be found in a wide range of industries including aerospace, automotive, energy, medicine, and manufacturing. Students take a common core of basic courses in math, science, and engineering followed by more specialized courses in areas such as thermal-fluid sciences, solid mechanics, and systems and controls. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences and engineering fundamentals while also allowing students to tailor their studies to their specific interests through technical electives. The program culminates in a two-semester capstone design sequence in which students work in teams to solve real-world engineering problems.
Accredidation: The Mechanical Engineering (BSME) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Sciences,
Requirements: The Medical Laboratory Sciences (MLS) program consists of three years of pre-professional study on the Purdue campus followed by one year (usually 12 months) of clinical laboratory curriculum in a program accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS). Students must apply for the clinical year of study during the fall of their junior year. Admission to the clinical year is competitive and is not guaranteed.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Medical Laboratory Sciences (MLS) program provides students with a strong background in the biological and physical sciences and the specialized knowledge and skills needed for a career in medical laboratory science. Medical laboratory scientists perform a wide variety of laboratory tests used in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. The program consists of three years of pre-clinical study on the West Lafayette campus followed by a fourth year of clinical training at an affiliated school of medical laboratory science. Admission to the clinical year is competitive. Upon completion of the program, students are eligible for national certification.
Accredidation: The clinical programs are accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Medieval and Renaissance Studies,
Requirements: To apply for the Medieval and Renaissance Studies, BA program, applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores. Recommended high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 6-8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Students are also required to complete Purdue-specific essay questions as part of the application process.
Description: The Medieval and Renaissance Studies program is an interdisciplinary program of the College of Liberal Arts that draws its faculty from several departments: Art and Design; English; History; Interdisciplinary Studies; Languages and Cultures; Music; Philosophy; Political Science; and Theatre. It offers both a major and a minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies. This program provides students with a broad and yet deep understanding of the two periods that were most influential in the formation of the modern world. It gives students an appreciation for the historical development of Western culture and its contact with the cultures of the Mediterranean and the Near East.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechatronics Engineering Technology,
Requirements: Admission to the Mechatronics Engineering Technology program is based on Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. Applicants are required to submit high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores. The high school curriculum should include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. The program itself is a STEM-certified program that requires 120 credit hours for completion.
Description: Mechatronics is the synergistic integration of mechanical engineering, with electronics and intelligent computer control in the design and manufacturing of industrial products and processes. Mechatronics engineering technology at Purdue University is a unique program that uses a problem-solving, hands-on, and project-based approach to teaching students. It is designed for students who want to be able to design, create, and maintain the complex systems found in modern manufacturing environments. This curriculum provides students with a solid foundation in the fundamental areas of mechatronics engineering technology, including circuits, electronics, motors and drives, robotics, programmable logic controllers, fluid power, mechanics, and product lifecycle management.
Accredidation: The Mechatronics Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Meteorology and Climatology,
Requirements: The Meteorology and Climatology program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the study of the atmosphere and its phenomena. To apply as a freshman to Purdue University, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Purdue is a test-required institution for students applying for 2024 and beyond; therefore, SAT or ACT scores are required. For graduation, the program requires 120 semester hours and a minimum 2.0 graduation GPA.
Description: Meteorology and climatology is the study of the earth’s atmosphere and the processes that cause what we know as weather and climate. Students are prepared for a variety of careers in weather forecasting, research, and data analysis. The curriculum meets the requirements of the American Meteorological Society and the federal government for employment as a meteorologist.
Accredidation: The curriculum meets the requirements of the American Meteorological Society and the federal government for employment as a meteorologist.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology,
Requirements: Applicants for the Microbiology, BS program must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include the completion of high school coursework (4 years of English, 4 years of math, 3 years of lab science, etc.), submission of SAT or ACT scores, and the Common App personal essay along with Purdue-specific supplemental questions. The degree requires a total of 120 credit hours for graduation, including the Biology Core (21-23 credits), Microbiology Emphasis (16-20 credits), and supporting coursework in Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00 is required.
Description: Microbiology is the study of the smallest living organisms—bacteria, viruses, algae, fungi, and protozoa. Microorganisms are used in many ways, from the production of medicines to the cleaning up of environmental pollution. Students in the microbiology major study the role of microorganisms in disease, the environment, and industry, and the basic biology of these organisms.

ProgramName: Military Science and Leadership Minor
Requirements: The Military Science and Leadership Minor requires a total of 18.00 credits. Required courses include MILT 10100, MILT 10200, MILT 20100, MILT 20200, MILT 30100, MILT 30200, MILT 40100, and MILT 40200. Additionally, Army ROTC Cadets must complete a summer internship (MILT 39500) between the junior and senior year.
Department: Division of Military Science and Technology
Description: The Military Science and Leadership minor is designed for any student desiring to improve their leadership skills and is mandatory for any student who desires to receive a commission in the United States Army. This minor consists of 18 total credit hours from the courses listed below.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Multidisciplinary Engineering,
Requirements: Students normally apply for admission to the Multidisciplinary Engineering (MDE) or Interdisciplinary Engineering (IDE) programs during their second semester in First-Year Engineering. After being admitted to the School of Engineering Education, the student is assigned a faculty advisor to assist in the development of a plan of study.
Description: The Multidisciplinary Engineering (MDE) program provides students with the opportunity to develop a custom engineering degree that is tailored to their specific interests and career goals. Students choose from one of several pre-defined concentrations or work with an advisor to create a self-designed concentration. MDE is for students who want to be engineers and need a curriculum that is not available in a traditional engineering discipline.
Accredidation: The Multidisciplinary Engineering (BSMDE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Music History and Theory Minor
Requirements: The Music History and Theory Minor is available to all undergraduate students at Purdue. A grade of C- or better is required in all courses for the minor. Students may use a maximum of 6 credits from other institutions to satisfy the requirements for this minor. No audition is required for this minor. Course Prerequisites: Enrollment in MUS 16100 (Music Theory I) requires credit for MUS 13200 (Music Theory Fundamentals) or a passing score on the Theory Placement Exam.
Description: The minor in Music History and Theory provides students with the opportunity to pursue an interest in music. Students will gain foundational knowledge and skills in music theory and aural perception, and explore the history of music through a variety of genres and eras.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Theory,
Requirements: To be admitted to the Music Theory, BA program, applicants must meet the general freshman admission requirements for Purdue University. This includes the completion of a high school curriculum with 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Admission is also based on academic achievement (GPA), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. Specifically for the Music Theory major, an audition is not required.
Description: Music theory is the study of how music works. It examines the language and notation of music. It seeks to identify patterns and structures in composers' techniques across or within genres, styles, or historical periods. In a broader sense, music theory also distills and analyzes the fundamental parameters or elements of music — rhythm, harmony (harmonic function), melody, structure, form, texture, etc. Any person who plays, orbits, or writes music is using music theory. Music theory provides a way to explain what a listener hears.
Accredidation: The Department of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Native American and Indigenous Studies Minor
Requirements: This minor is available to any student at Purdue University. The Native American and Indigenous Studies minor consists of 15-18 credit hours. Students must complete one required core course (3 credits) and 12-15 credits of electives.
Description: The Native American and Indigenous Studies (NAIS) minor provides students with a program of study that centers on the histories, languages, cultures, and contemporary issues of Indigenous peoples. Students will gain an understanding of the complex social, political, and historical contexts that shape the experiences of Indigenous communities globally, with a particular focus on North America. Through interdisciplinary coursework, students will develop critical thinking skills and engage with diverse perspectives and methodologies related to Indigenous studies.

ProgramName: Natural Resources and Environmental Science Minor
Requirements: 18.00 Credit Hours. The Natural Resources and Environmental Science minor is available to students in all colleges. Students must complete a minimum of 18 credit hours of coursework. A maximum of 6 credits from a student’s major or another minor can be used to satisfy the requirements for this minor. Course requirements include NRES 20000 - Introduction To Environmental Science and NRES 29000 - Introduction To Natural Resources And Environmental Science Academic Career.
Description: The Natural Resources and Environmental Science minor is available to students in all colleges of the university. It is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to environmental and natural resource issues.

ProgramName: Naval Science Minor
Requirements: The Naval Science minor is available to students who have been admitted into the Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps (NROTC). The minor requires 18 credits of Naval Science (NS) courses. A minimum of 18 credits must be earned in Naval Science courses with a grade of C- or better. All NS courses are 2-3 credit hours. Required courses include: NS 11000, NS 21300, NS 21400, NS 31000, NS 31100, NS 41000, NS 41100, NS 41200, and NS 41300.
Description: The Department of Naval Science offers a curriculum in Naval Science to midshipmen in the Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps (NROTC) and to other interested students. The curriculum includes courses in leadership, management, navigation, ship systems, and the history and evolution of warfare. The program’s objective is to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to serve as commissioned officers in the Navy or Marine Corps. The curriculum is also available to students who are not participating in the NROTC program but who have an interest in naval science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Neurobiology and Physiology,
Requirements: The program in neurobiology and physiology offers students a strong background in the basic disciplines of biology, including cell biology, genetics, and molecular biology. In addition, students take a variety of courses in neurobiology, physiology, and related areas. The program provides an excellent foundation for students planning to attend medical, dental, or veterinary school, as well as those planning to pursue graduate study in a variety of fields. A minimum of 120 credit hours is required for graduation, and the Department of Biological Sciences requires a C- or better in all BIOL courses used to satisfy degree requirements.
Description: This major provides a foundation for the study of the biological basis of behavior, and of the function of the various systems of the human body. Because it emphasizes biological, chemical, and physical principles, the major provides an excellent background for those planning to go to medical, dental, or other professional schools, as well as for those planning to go to graduate school in several of the biological sciences. For those wishing to enter the workforce after receiving the bachelor’s degree, there are opportunities in research, the pharmaceutical industry, and laboratory and clinical settings.
CostPerCredit: $347.85 per credit hour (Resident), $948.30 per credit hour (Non-resident)

ProgramName: Nuclear Engineering Minor
Requirements: The minor in nuclear engineering is open to any student at Purdue University. A student must complete 12 credit hours of nuclear engineering (NUCL) courses at the 20000 level or above. At least 6 of these credit hours must be at the 30000 level or above. All courses must be taken for a grade. A GPA of 2.0 or better must be achieved in the courses used for the minor.
Description: The minor in nuclear engineering consists of 12 credits of nuclear engineering course work as specified below. Students interested in the minor in nuclear engineering should apply through the School of Nuclear Engineering.

ProgramName: Nuclear Engineering, BSNE
Requirements: The First-Year Engineering program is the entry point for all beginning engineering students. In this program, students complete a common first-year curriculum which includes chemistry, calculus, physics, and English composition, as well as an introduction to engineering. After completing the First-Year Engineering requirements, students can apply for transition into the School of Nuclear Engineering. The School of Nuclear Engineering requires a total of 126 credit hours for the Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering degree.
Description: Nuclear engineering is the field of engineering that deals with the practical application of nuclear processes and radiation. These include the design, development, and operation of nuclear power plants for electricity generation and propulsion, the use of isotopes and radiation in medicine and industry, and the management of nuclear waste. The curriculum in the School of Nuclear Engineering is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences and mathematics, followed by courses in the fundamental principles of nuclear engineering. The program includes study in reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear materials, and radiation detection and measurement. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research projects and to gain experience through internships and co-operative education programs.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Nuclear and Radiological and similarly named engineering programs.

ProgramName: Nursing, BSN
Requirements: Admission is competitive and is based on high school record and SAT or ACT scores. The number of students admitted to the nursing program is limited by the availability of faculty and clinical facilities. Enrollment in the professional nursing program begins in the freshman year. To be considered for admission, students must have a minimum of: 4 years of English, 4 years of math (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 3 years of lab science (including biology and chemistry), 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of foreign language. High school students are encouraged to complete as much biology and chemistry as possible.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The School of Nursing program is designed to prepare a nurse who can function in a variety of health care settings. The program leads to a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree. The program consists of a minimum of 120 credit hours.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree program, the Master of Science in Nursing degree program, and the Doctor of Nursing Practice program at Purdue University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org). The School of Nursing is also approved by the Indiana State Board of Nursing.

ProgramName: Nutrition Minor
Requirements: Enrollment in the Nutrition Minor is open to any student currently enrolled at Purdue University. A grade of C- or higher is required in all NUTR courses.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: This minor is available to any student outside of the Nutrition Science Department. To enroll in the minor, contact an advisor in your home department. Students must have a 2.0 GPA to enter and complete the minor. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition Science,
Requirements: Admission to the Nutrition Science, BS program at Purdue University requires a completed Common Application, including a personal essay. Applicants must provide high school transcripts showing completion of 8 semesters of English and Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science and Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue University is a test-required institution; therefore, all undergraduate applicants must submit official SAT or ACT scores for admission consideration.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The nutrition science major provides students with a strong background in the basic sciences of biology and chemistry. Students explore how nutrients in food are metabolized and used by the body and the role of nutrients in health and disease. Students find that this major is excellent preparation for graduate study in nutrition or other biological sciences. The major also provides the prerequisites for admission into medical, dental, and other health-related professional schools.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition, Fitness, and Health,
Requirements: Purdue’s admission process is holistic. Requirements for freshman applicants include high school course expectations (8 semesters of English, 8 of Math, 6 of Lab Science, 6 of Social Studies, and 4 of Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. The application is submitted through the Common App, including Purdue-specific questions.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: Nutrition, fitness, and health is a major for students who are interested in the roles of nutrition and physical activity in the maintenance of health and the prevention of disease. Students focus on the roles of nutrition and exercise in the maintenance of health and the prevention of disease. This program is for students interested in careers in the health and fitness industry, such as health and wellness coaching, personal training, and corporate wellness.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Occupational Health Sciences,
Requirements: To finish the Occupational Health Sciences major, a student must complete a minimum of 120.00 semester credits. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required for graduation. A minimum grade of C- or better is required in all Health Sciences (HSCI) courses. General undergraduate admission to Purdue University requires the completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of World Language recommended) and the submission of SAT or ACT scores for students applying for Fall 2024 and beyond.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: Occupational health science is the science of anticipating, recognizing, evaluating, and controlling workplace conditions that may cause workers’ injury or illness. Industrial hygienists use environmental monitoring and analytical methods to determine the extent of worker exposure and employ engineering, work practice controls, and other methods to control potential health hazards. The program is designed to provide the student with the necessary background in the basic sciences, such as chemistry, physics, and biology, and in-depth training in the specialized areas of industrial hygiene.
Accredidation: The Occupational Health Sciences program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Organizational Leadership Minor
Requirements: Total Credits: 18.00. Required courses include TLI 11200 - Foundations Of Organizational Leadership, TLI 15200 - Business Principles For Organizational Leadership, TLI 21300 - Project Management, and TLI 25300 - Principles Of Personnel Management. Additionally, 6 credits of selective courses are required. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. Transfer credit for TLI 11200, TLI 15200, TLI 21300, and TLI 25300 is not accepted. These courses must be taken at a Purdue University campus.
Description: The Organizational Leadership minor is available to all students at Purdue University, regardless of their major. The program focuses on the human side of organizations, including leadership, supervision, human resources, and organizational behavior.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Organizational Leadership,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Science degree in the Purdue Polytechnic Institute, students must satisfy the following requirements: a minimum of 120 credit hours, a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00, and at least 32 credit hours of Purdue coursework at the 30000 level or higher. Applicants must also meet Purdue University undergraduate admission criteria, which include submission of the Common Application, personal essay, and Purdue-specific responses. High school course expectations include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language.
Description: Organizational Leadership (OL) is a leadership-focused, business-oriented degree. Leadership is the process of influencing others to achieve a common goal. Our curriculum covers the practical aspects of leading people and organizations, with an emphasis on communication, team building, and strategic planning. The program is designed for students who want to develop the skills necessary to lead in a variety of organizational settings, including business, government, and non-profit organizations.
Accredidation: Association of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering (ATMAE); Accredited

ProgramName: Peace Studies Minor
Requirements: The Peace Studies Minor requires a total of 15 credit hours. A GPA of 2.0 is required in courses for the minor. At least 6 of these 15 credits must be taken at Purdue.
Description: The Peace Studies minor provides students with the opportunity to study the causes of conflict and the potential for peaceful solutions. Students explore the history of nonviolence, the nature of war, and the ethical issues involved in peace and justice.

ProgramName: Pet Food Processing Minor
Requirements: The Department of Food Science and Department of Animal Sciences offer a Pet Food Processing minor to undergraduate students interested in careers in the pet food industry. This minor is designed to provide a background in pet food processing, nutrition, and safety. Contact the Department of Food Science for more information or to apply for the minor. 15 credits are required.
Description: The minor in Pet Food Processing is available to students in all majors at Purdue who have met the course prerequisites. This minor is intended for students who have an interest in the processing and manufacturing of food for companion animals. This minor is housed in the Agricultural and Biological Engineering Department.

ProgramName: Pharmaceutical Sciences, BSPS
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the BSPS program, students must meet the general admission requirements of Purdue University. Admission is competitive and based on several factors, including: High school grades, Strength of high school curriculum, SAT or ACT scores, and student's essay and Purdue-specific questions. Recommended high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences (BSPS) program is designed for students who want to work in the pharmaceutical industry in the area of drug discovery and development or to pursue graduate or professional school in a variety of fields. This program is not intended for students who wish to become a licensed pharmacist.

ProgramName: Philosophy Minor
Description: Philosophy, the oldest and most fundamental of the liberal arts, is the study of the fundamental problems of existence, knowledge, and value. Its primary aim is to help students think clearly and critically about these problems and to express their thoughts precisely and effectively. The minor in philosophy is designed to provide students with a broad introduction to the field and its history, while allowing them to pursue their own interests in specific areas of philosophy. The program is available to students in all colleges of the University and requires 15.00 total credits.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy,
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy provides students with a broad and rigorous training in the history of philosophy, its main figures and movements, as well as its core areas (logic, metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics). Philosophy students learn to analyze and evaluate arguments, to read carefully and critically, and to write with clarity and precision. The program requires a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation.
Description: Philosophy is the search for a clear and comprehensive understanding of the universe and of the human condition. It is an attempt to define and think through the basic problems of life and to see how they are related. Philosophy asks about the nature of truth and knowledge, of right and wrong, of God, of the relation of mind and body, and of the individual and society. Philosophy is excellent preparation for many professions, including law, medicine, teaching, and business.

ProgramName: Physics Minor
Requirements: Minimum Credits: 18-21. Students must complete the following core courses: PHYS 17200 - Modern Mechanics and PHYS 27200 - Electric And Magnetic Interactions (or equivalents). Students who take PHYS 22000, PHYS 22100, PHYS 23300, or PHYS 23400 should contact the physics departmental advisor regarding equivalent courses. Electives: Students must select 6-9 credits from the following courses: PHYS 31000, PHYS 32200, PHYS 33000, PHYS 34000, PHYS 34200, PHYS 34400, PHYS 36000, PHYS 41000, PHYS 41100, PHYS 41600, PHYS 41700, PHYS 42200, PHYS 43000, PHYS 43100, PHYS 45000, PHYS 46000, PHYS 46100, and any PHYS 50000-level course. Other Requirements: PHYS 23500 and PHYS 24100/PHYS 25100/PHYS 26100 are not applicable toward the minor. PHYS 34200L and PHYS 34400L are not applicable toward the minor. No more than 4 credits of lower-level (10000 or 20000) courses taken elsewhere may be used toward the minor. No more than 3 credits of upper-level (30000, 40000, or 50000) courses taken elsewhere may be used toward the minor.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics,
Requirements: Application requirements for the Physics, BS program include the submission of the Common Application, which requires a personal statement (essay). Purdue University is test-required, meaning official SAT or ACT scores must be submitted for freshman admission. High school course requirements include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of Foreign Language. Once admitted, students must complete a minimum of 120 credits, maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and fulfill the College of Science Core Curriculum requirements to graduate.
Concentration: Applied Physics, Astrophysics, Honors Physics, Physics Education, Physics
Description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers several programs of study leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science. These programs are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of physics and astronomy, as well as the mathematical and analytical skills necessary for a wide range of careers in research, industry, and education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Planetary Sciences,
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Planetary Sciences, students must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and response to Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must also provide high school transcripts or use the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Purdue University is a test-required institution, and all students applying for undergraduate admission are required to submit SAT or ACT scores. The program curriculum includes core requirements in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences, along with significant coursework in Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry.
Description: Planetary Science is the study of the origin and evolution of the solar system and its component parts. This includes planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and meteorites. This degree program provides students with a strong background in physics and mathematics, as well as a broad understanding of the Earth and the solar system.

ProgramName: Plant Biology Minor
Requirements: 15.00 semester credits are required for the Plant Biology Minor. Required Courses: BTNY 12000 - Introduction To Plant Science or BTNY 12100 - Introduction To Plant Science (3 credits) and AGRY 32000 - Genetics or BIOL 44000 - Phylogenetic Biology (3 credits). Additionally, 9 credits must be chosen from a specific list of approved courses including: AGRY 32100, AGRY 43500, BIOL 23100, BIOL 23200, BIOL 24100, BIOL 24200, BIOL 30100, BIOL 43800, BIOL 43900, BIOL 48300, BIOL 53300, BTNY 11000, BTNY 21000, BTNY 21100, BTNY 30100, BTNY 30400, BTNY 55100, BTNY 55300, BTNY 56000, ENTM 31100, FNR 33100, FNR 43411, HORT 20100, HORT 30100.
Description: Plant biology is an area of study that provides students with a detailed understanding of the biology of plants and their importance in the world. Plant biology research and education includes the study of plants at all levels of organization, from the molecular to the ecosystem levels. Areas of research include physiology, genetics, development, and evolution. To explore these issues, students complete a range of courses in chemistry and biology, as well as plant-specific courses.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Biotechnology,
Requirements: 120.00 Semester Credits required for graduation. The Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Biotechnology curriculum provides a base in the plant sciences, including plant biology, genetics, and molecular biology. The core curriculum focuses on plant breeding, molecular genetics, and biotechnology. Students are also required to take a set of core courses in chemistry and mathematics. Students must have a 2.0 overall GPA to graduate. Application requirements include high school coursework, SAT or ACT scores, and the Common App essay/Purdue-specific questions.
Description: This major focuses on the plant sciences and develops the skills needed for the genetics, breeding and biotechnology industries. Students learn about genetic control and the manipulation of plant traits, the molecular biology of plants, and the application of these to the improvement of crops for food, fuel and fiber. This program prepares students for positions in the seed and biotechnology industries or for graduate study.

ProgramName: Plant Pathology Minor
Requirements: A minimum of 12 credits. Grade of C- or better in each course used for the minor. A minimum of six credit hours must be taken at Purdue.
Department: Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, College of Agriculture
Description: The minor in Plant Pathology is available to any student at Purdue University. The minor is designed for students who want to learn more about the causes and management of plant diseases. Students will learn about the biology of plant pathogens, the interactions between plants and pathogens, and the strategies used to control plant diseases.

ProgramName: Political Science Minor
Requirements: 15 credits required. At least a C- must be earned in all courses used for the minor. At least 9 credit hours must be taken at the West Lafayette campus. Required courses include POL 10100, one of (POL 12000, POL 13000, or POL 14100), POL 15000, and 6 credits of POL courses at the 30000 level or above.
Description: The Department of Political Science offers a minor in political science to students who want to explore how we are governed, how public policy is made, and how we can be more effective citizens. The minor in political science is designed to provide students with an understanding of political systems, behavior, and policy. It is an excellent complement to majors in business, communication, history, and many other fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science,
Requirements: To earn the Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, students must complete 120 total credits, including 33 credits specifically for the major. Admission requires completion of the Common Application, which includes a personal statement and Purdue-specific short-answer questions. Applicants must provide high school transcripts and official SAT or ACT scores. The program requires completion of the University Core Curriculum and the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements, including proficiency in a foreign language through the level of 202nd-semester equivalent.
Concentration: American Government and Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, Political Theory, Public Policy and Public Administration
Description: Political science is the study of how people make collective decisions. It is the study of power and how we decide who gets what, when, and how. Political scientists study the exercise of power and how power can be used to improve the lives of citizens. In political science courses, you will learn how governments are organized and how political systems work, and you will learn about the role that ordinary citizens play in shaping those systems. You will learn about the major problems and challenges that different societies and the international community face and how we can best go about solving them. You will learn how to analyze political and social data and how to evaluate competing arguments about politics and public policy.

ProgramName: Portuguese Minor
Requirements: 15 semester hours required. All PTGS credits must be C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken in residence (on the West Lafayette campus). Students may also take PTGS 10500 - Accelerated Portuguese for Speakers of Spanish (3 cr.) as a substitute for PTGS 10100 and PTGS 10200.
Description: The Portuguese minor is designed to provide students with a basic proficiency in the language and an introduction to the cultures and literatures of the Luso-Brazilian world.

ProgramName: Pre-Communication
Requirements: Students are admitted to Pre-Communication if they do not meet the direct admission requirements for the Lamb School of Communication. CODOing into Pre-Communication requires a 2.0 GPA. To move from Pre-Communication to a major in the Lamb School of Communication, students must complete at least 30 credit hours of college-level coursework, at least 12 of which must be from Purdue West Lafayette, and have a minimum 3.0 cumulative Purdue GPA.
Description: Pre-Communication is a non-degree granting program for students who intend to pursue a major in the Brian Lamb School of Communication. Upon completion of pre-communication requirements, students may apply to a major in Communication.

ProgramName: Pre-Dentistry
Requirements: Pre-dentistry, pre-medicine, and pre-veterinary medicine are not majors at Purdue University. Students interested in these areas should choose a major and also complete the specific requirements for the professional school of their choice. Most students in these areas choose a major in the College of Agriculture, the College of Health and Human Sciences, or the College of Science. Pre-professional students are expected to maintain high standards of scholarship and to exhibit the characteristics of integrity and maturity. Students should visit Pre-Professional Advising (PPA) early in their first year at Purdue.
Description: Dental schools seek students who have a strong foundation in the sciences, as well as those who are well-rounded and have demonstrated a commitment to service and leadership. Admission to dental school is highly competitive, and students are encouraged to seek the advice of a pre-professional advisor in the Center for Career Opportunities (CCO) Pre-Professional Advising office (Young Hall, Room 132; 765-494-3981). Pre-dentistry is not a major; students must choose a degree-granting major and complete the specific courses required by the dental schools they plan to attend.

ProgramName: Pre-Law
Requirements: Pre-law is not a major at Purdue University. It is a set of activities and advising services that help students prepare for law school. Students interested in law school are encouraged to choose a major in an area that interests them and to pursue a rigorous course of study that develops their analytical and communication skills.
Description: Purdue University has long provided a superior background for students who go on to law school. There is no specific pre-law major at Purdue. Law schools do not require a specific major. Instead, they seek students with diverse backgrounds who have developed the necessary skills and have an excellent undergraduate academic record. Students with a serious interest in law should consult with an advisor in their major and the pre-law advisor for assistance in choosing a major and elective courses that will help prepare them for the study of law. It is important to remember that most students find success in law school after completing a degree in an area in which they have a genuine interest. Students with questions about pre-law should contact the Center for Career Opportunities (CCO), Pre-Professional Advising at (765) 494-3981 or by email at preprofessional@purdue.edu.

ProgramName: Pre-Medicine
Requirements: Pre-medicine is NOT a major. Students should choose a major in which they have an interest and can excel. Any major is acceptable, as long as the student completes the required prerequisite courses for medical school. Admissions committees evaluate a candidate’s application based on several factors: Academic Excellence, Admissions Test (MCAT), and Co-curricular activities including Clinical/Direct Patient Care Experience, Service/Volunteer Experience, Research, and Leadership/Involvement. Although each medical school has its own set of prerequisites, most require two semesters each of: General Biology, General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physics, and English.
Description: Preparation for medical school requires strong academic performance, as well as significant experience in a health care setting and a history of community service and leadership. There is no “pre-med” major at Purdue. Most pre-medical students choose a major in the College of Science or the College of Health and Human Sciences. However, medical schools accept any major as long as the student has completed the required science and math courses. Common majors include biology, chemistry, and brain and behavioral sciences, but students can also choose majors such as engineering, nutrition, or even the humanities.

ProgramName: Pre-Nursing
Requirements: Minimum Semester Credits: 12; Minimum Cumulative GPA: 3.0; Minimum Program GPA: 3.0. Other: 3.0 CUM GPA and 3.0 Program GPA. Student must have a 'C' or better in any Nursing program course already completed. A grade of 'C' or better in the following courses (as applicable): BIOL 11000, 20300, 20400, 22100; CHM 11100, 11200, 11500, 11600; PSY 12000; HDFS 21000; SOC 10000; ENGL 10600, 10800; COM 11400; MA 15300 or higher; STAT 30100; NUTR 30300. Space in the Pre-Nursing and Nursing majors is limited. CODO is a competitive process; meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee CODO into the major.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: The Pre-Nursing (PNUR) program is a one-year (two semester) program for students who intend to apply to the professional Nursing program. Pre-Nursing students apply to the Nursing program during their second semester of study for a possible start in the Nursing program in their sophomore year.

ProgramName: Pre-Pharmacy
Requirements: Students who are interested in the Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) program usually choose Pre-Pharmacy as their major for their first two years. This is not a degree-granting program. After completion of these two years of study, students may apply to the Doctor of Pharmacy program. Pre-Pharmacy requires 63-65 credits. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. All required courses must be taken for a grade, not Pass/Not Pass.
Description: This two-year non-degree program provides the prerequisite course work required for application to Purdue’s four-year professional Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) program. Students who complete the two-year program are also eligible to apply to other pharmacy schools. Course work includes chemistry, biology, mathematics, physics, and communication, as well as several elective courses. After completing the pre-pharmacy requirements, students apply for admission to the professional program. Admission to the Pharm.D. program is competitive and is based on a student’s academic record, letters of recommendation, and an interview. Pre-pharmacy students are eligible to join the Pre-Pharmacy Club and the professional pharmacy fraternities.

ProgramName: Pre-Physical Therapy
Requirements: Purdue University provides several avenues for students to prepare for graduate study in Physical Therapy. Students are encouraged to pursue a bachelor’s degree in a field that is of interest to them and includes the required prerequisites for graduate school. Pre-physical therapy requirements include: two semesters of general chemistry with labs; two semesters of general biology with labs; two semesters of general physics with labs; two semesters of anatomy and physiology with labs; and one semester of psychology, and one semester of statistics. Other courses may be required depending on the specific graduate program. In addition to a strong academic record, students should seek opportunities to gain clinical experience in a physical therapy setting and participate in extracurricular activities.
Description: The Pre-Physical Therapy program at Purdue is not a major; rather, it is a set of prerequisites that prepares students for admission to a doctor of physical therapy (DPT) program. Students can choose any major they wish as long as they complete the required courses for physical therapy school. Common majors for students interested in physical therapy include Kinesiology, Health and Disease, and Brain and Behavioral Sciences. Most physical therapy programs require a bachelor's degree before entry. Students should work closely with their academic advisors to ensure they are meeting the requirements for both their chosen major and the physical therapy programs to which they intend to apply.

ProgramName: Pre-Physician's Assistant
Requirements: Pre-physician assistant students choose a degree-granting major in any of the colleges at Purdue University. While physician assistant programs do not require a specific major, students must complete the required and recommended prerequisite coursework for each physician assistant program to which they plan to apply. Extracurricular activities including significant clinical/healthcare experience (often 500-2,000 hours), shadowing a physician assistant, and leadership/community service are also key components of preparation.
Description: Physician assistants (PAs) are health care professionals licensed to practice medicine with physician supervision. PAs provide a broad range of diagnostic and therapeutic services. A PA’s practice may also include education, research, and administrative services. PA education is based on the medical model. Physician assistant programs are typically master’s level programs and generally 24-27 months in length. The first year of the program is didactic (classroom) and the second year consists of clinical rotations. PAs are found in all areas of medicine including primary care and family medicine, emergency medicine, surgery, and psychiatry. For more information, please visit the Pre-Professional Advising website: https://www.purdue.edu/preprofessional/

ProgramName: Pre-Veterinary Medicine
Requirements: Students interested in veterinary medicine may choose any major they wish. They most often choose a major in the College of Agriculture, the College of Science, or the College of Health and Human Sciences. To be eligible for consideration for admission to the professional DVM program, students must complete at least 70-71 semester hours of undergraduate work. Required pre-requisite courses include: General Chemistry (8 credits), Organic Chemistry (8 credits), Biochemistry (3 credits), Biology (8 credits), Genetics (3 credits), Microbiology (4 credits), Physics (8 credits), Statistics (3 credits), English Composition (3 credits), Communication/Public Speaking (3 credits), and Humanities (9 credits). While it is possible to complete the pre-veterinary requirements in three years, most students complete a four-year baccalaureate degree program.
Department: College of Agriculture; College of Science
Description: The College of Veterinary Medicine offers a pre-veterinary medicine program for students who wish to complete the requirements for admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) program. Students may follow the pre-veterinary medicine program in either the College of Agriculture or the College of Science. Students may enter the professional DVM program after completing a minimum of 70 semester credits of pre-veterinary course work. Most students, however, complete a bachelor’s degree before entering the professional program. Students who are interested in the pre-veterinary medicine program should consult with an academic advisor in the College of Agriculture or the College of Science.

ProgramName: Product Lifecycle Management Minor
Requirements: A student must complete 15 to 18 credit hours from the following: Core Courses (9 hours): CGT 22600 - Introduction To Constraint-Based Modeling, CGT 32600 - Manufacturing Graphics Standards, CGT 42600 - Product Lifecycle Management. Selectives (9 hours): Select three from the following: CGT 10301 - Geometric Modeling Concepts, CGT 11000 - Technical Graphics Communications, CGT 21500 - Computer Graphics Programming I, CGT 25001 - Computer Graphics Technology Standards, CGT 30302 - Virtual Product Integration, CGT 35102 - CGT Project Management, CGT 40301 - Product Data Management, CGT 45001 - Professional Practices, MET 14300 - 2D and 3D Tooling and Modeling, MET 24500 - Manufacturing Systems, MET 34600 - Advanced Product Development. Note: Students may use up to 6 credit hours of CGT courses towards both this minor and a CGT major.
Description: The Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) minor provides students with a foundational understanding of the processes and tools used in industry to manage a product from its initial conception, through design and manufacture, to service and disposal. The PLM minor is intended to provide students with a cross-functional perspective of the product development process and the role of PLM in the modern enterprise. Students will learn about the business processes, organizational structures, and information technology systems used to manage product-related information and to support collaboration across the extended enterprise.

ProgramName: Professional Writing Minor
Requirements: The Professional Writing minor (PWRT) requires 15 credit hours. Students may not use more than two (2) courses from their major(s) to satisfy the requirements for this minor.
Description: The Professional Writing minor (PWRT) is an interdisciplinary minor offered by the Department of English. It is designed to help students across the University develop the writing and communication skills they will need in their careers. Students in the minor learn to write for various audiences, purposes, and contexts, and to use various media and technologies to produce effective professional documents.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Professional Writing,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Professional Writing BA program, freshman applicants should have completed the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Purdue University is a test-required university; students must submit SAT or ACT scores. The application process also requires the Common Application and a personal essay.
Description: Professional writing is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for careers as writers, editors, and designers in diverse fields such as publishing, technology, business, law, and non-profit organizations. Students in the program learn how to communicate effectively with different audiences using a variety of media and technologies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychological Sciences,
Requirements: Purdue University’s holistic application review process considers several factors: high school coursework, grades in core subjects, SAT or ACT scores, personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: Psychological Sciences is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. It is a diverse field that includes many areas of study. At Purdue, the Department of Psychological Sciences offers two undergraduate majors: the Bachelor of Science (BS) and the Bachelor of Arts (BA). Both majors provide students with a strong foundation in the core areas of psychology, including clinical, cognitive, developmental, industrial-organizational, mathematical and computational, neuroscience and behavior, and social psychology. The BA degree is designed for students who want a broad education in psychology and may be interested in pursuing careers in fields such as business, law, or social services. The BS degree is designed for students who want a more intensive science-based education in psychology and may be interested in pursuing careers in research or healthcare.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychological Sciences,
Requirements: To earn the Bachelor of Science degree in Psychological Sciences, students must complete a total of 120 credit hours. This includes the Purdue Core Curriculum, College of Health and Human Sciences (HHS) Core Requirements, and Psychological Sciences Departmental Requirements. Specific departmental requirements include core courses such as Introductory Psychology, Psychological Statistics, and Research Methods in Psychology, as well as several psychology electives.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The Psychological Sciences major provides students with a broad foundation in the core areas of psychology, including clinical, cognitive, developmental, industrial-organizational, learning and memory, neuroscience, and social psychology. The curriculum emphasizes the development of research and analytical skills, as well as an understanding of the biological, social, and environmental factors that influence behavior. The major prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as human services, business, and research, as well as for graduate study in psychology or related areas.

ProgramName: Psychology Minor
Requirements: The Psychology minor requires 15.00 credit hours. Required Course: PSY 12000 - Elementary Psychology (3 credits). Electives: Select 12 credits of PSY courses (Note: PSY 20100, 20300, 39000, 39100, 49100, 49200, 49600, 59100, 69000, 69100, and 69500 cannot be used to satisfy minor requirements). Additional Requirements: At least 6 credits must be 30000 level or higher. At least 9 credits must be from Purdue University. All PSY courses must be completed with a C- or better.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health,
Requirements: To apply for the Public Health, BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of a high school curriculum with a minimum of 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science (including Biology and Chemistry), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Applicants must submit either SAT or ACT scores and complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific writing prompts.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: Health Policy and Management, Health Promotion and Education
Description: The Public Health major provides a multidisciplinary approach to protect and improve the health of people and their communities. Students are prepared to address health challenges through education, promotion of healthy lifestyles, and research for disease and injury prevention. This major provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate public health programs. Students also gain experience in public health policy, ethics, and environmental health. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for entry-level positions in public health or for further graduate or professional study.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Public Health (BSPH) is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Relations and Strategic Communication,
Requirements: To apply for freshman admission to the Public Relations and Strategic Communication program, students must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must also provide high school transcripts (via self-reported course work) and are required to submit official SAT or ACT scores. Purdue uses a holistic review process that considers high school academic rigor, grades, and standardized test scores, as well as personal background and experiences.
Description: Public Relations and Strategic Communication majors focus on the way organizations communicate with their internal and external audiences to build and maintain mutually beneficial relationships. Public relations and strategic communication is practiced in almost every segment of society including corporations, non-profits, government, health care, and sports. Students gain foundational knowledge and skills in theory, research, writing, ethics and strategy. Practical experience is gained through a mandatory internship and opportunities to work in the student-run firm, Boiler Communication. After graduation, students pursue a wide range of career paths as account executives, media relations specialists, social media managers, public information officers and corporate communication managers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Quantitative Biology,
Requirements: Admission to the Quantitative Biology, BS program is based on a holistic review of several factors. Minimum high school course requirements include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus for College of Science majors), 6 semesters of Lab Science (Biology, Chemistry, and Physics are recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are required for admission.
Description: The Quantitative Biology major provides students with a strong background in mathematics and physics, while also providing them with a solid foundation in the biological sciences. This program is designed for students who want to apply quantitative methods to biological problems and for those who wish to pursue graduate study in quantitative biology, biophysics, bioinformatics, or related fields.

ProgramName: Radiological Health Sciences Minor
Requirements: 15-16 credits. Credits must be earned at Purdue. GPA must be 2.0 or higher. No more than 3 credits of 10000-level courses may count toward the minor.
Description: The Radiological Health Sciences minor provides students with a foundational knowledge of the physics and biology of radiation, as well as the safety principles and regulations related to its use in medical, industrial, and research settings. Students will learn about radiation detection and measurement, radiation protection, and the biological effects of ionizing radiation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Radiological Health Sciences-Medical Physics,
Requirements: The Radiological Health Sciences major provides a curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science degree. Students select one of two concentrations: Health Physics or Pre-Medical Physics. The Pre-Medical Physics concentration is for students who wish to pursue a career as a medical physicist. This concentration provides students with a strong background in physics and mathematics, making them well-prepared for admission into a medical physics graduate program.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: Medical Physics
Description: The Medical Physics concentration in Radiological Health Sciences provides students with the prerequisite knowledge for entering an accredited graduate program in Medical Physics or related areas. This concentration prepares students for a career in clinical medical physics or medical physics research. It emphasizes the application of physics and mathematics to the diagnosis and treatment of human disease, particularly in the use of radiation for medical imaging and cancer therapy. Students take courses in biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics, as well as specialized courses in radiological health, medical physics, and imaging sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Radiological Health Sciences-Health Physics,
Requirements: The Radiological Health Sciences major leads to the Bachelor of Science degree. Students select one of two concentrations: Health Physics or Pre-Medical Physics. Each concentration provides students with a strong foundation in physics, biology, and mathematics. To complete the Bachelor of Science degree, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours. For freshman admission, Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores and expects applicants to have completed high school coursework including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: Health Physics
Description: Radiological Health Sciences (RHS) includes the Health Physics (HP) and Pre-Medical Physics (PMP) majors. These concentrations focus on the effects of radiation on living things and the environment. Health physics is a profession devoted to the protection of people and their environment from potential radiation hazards, while making it possible to enjoy the beneficial uses of radiation. Students find employment as health physicists in areas such as: medical facilities, national laboratories, state and federal government agencies, nuclear power plants, and industrial organizations. This major also provides a foundation for graduate study in Health Physics or other radiological sciences. The Health Physics (HP) program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Accredidation: The Health Physics (HP) program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Real Estate,
Requirements: The Real Estate major provides students with a strong foundation in real estate fundamentals, including real estate finance and investment, real estate development, and real estate law. To earn the BS degree with a major in Real Estate, students must complete a minimum of 120 credits. A 2.0 Graduation GPA is required for all courses taken at Purdue University and all courses taken in the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business. Application requirements include the submission of the Common Application, a personal essay, high school transcripts, and official SAT or ACT scores.
Department: Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business
Description: The Real Estate program provides students with a solid foundation in real estate fundamentals, including valuation, finance, investment, development, and law. Students gain an understanding of the economic, social, and political forces that shape the built environment. The program prepares students for careers in various sectors of the real estate industry, such as commercial and residential development, corporate real estate, investment analysis, and property management.

ProgramName: Religious Studies Minor
Requirements: 15 credits are required for the minor. Core Courses (3 credits): REL 20000 - Introduction To Religious Studies. Electives (12 credits): Choose 12 credits from the following list. No more than two courses from any one department can be used to satisfy the elective requirement. Note: REL 49900 - Directed Reading and REL 59000 - Directed Reading may count toward the Religious Studies minor with the permission of the Director of the Religious Studies Program.
Description: Religious Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on many different departments in the College of Liberal Arts to offer students a multi-faceted approach to the study of religion. The Program’s offerings provide students with a cross-cultural and multidisciplinary perspective on the religions of the world and their impact on history, culture, and society. Students have the opportunity to investigate the origins and development of religious traditions, the roles of religion in the lives of individuals and communities, and the interactions of religion with other social systems such as politics, art, and law.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Arts degree in the College of Liberal Arts, students shall satisfy the following requirements: 1. A minimum of 120 credit hours. 2. The College of Liberal Arts core requirements. 3. The Religious Studies major requirements. 4. A minimum of 32 credit hours at the 30000 level or above at Purdue University. General admission is based on a holistic review of the applicant's record including high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.
Concentration: The Religion and Culture option, The Religion and Social Sciences option
Description: Religious studies is a multi-disciplinary field of study that examines the history, literature, beliefs, practices, and institutions of religions. The program encourages students to investigate religion in its historical and contemporary contexts and to develop a critical understanding of the role religion plays in human life and society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Retail Management,
Requirements: To apply for the Retail Management, BS program, applicants must submit an application through the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must provide self-reported high school grades and official SAT or ACT scores, as Purdue University is a test-required institution. The program requires the completion of 120 credit hours, including major-specific courses in Consumer Science (CSR) and core requirements from the College of Health and Human Sciences.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: Retail management is a dynamic, fast-paced industry with a wide range of career opportunities. Graduates are prepared for careers in buying/procurement, retail management, merchandise coordination, and e-commerce. Retail management majors focus on the business of the retail industry. Students complete a common core of courses that provide a foundation in retail management, buying/merchandising, professional selling, and accounting/finance. These are complemented by coursework in economics, psychology, sociology, and communications. Practical experience is provided through a required internship.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Robotics Engineering Technology,
Requirements: The robotics engineering technology (REGT) program prepares students for the challenges and opportunities of the 21st-century manufacturing and robotics-dependent industry. REGT combines mechanical, electrical, and computer engineering technology to provide students with a solid foundation in the principles and practices of robotics. The program requires 120 credit hours for graduation.
Description: Robotics engineering technology (RET) is a multidisciplinary field that combines mechanical, electrical, and computer engineering to create and maintain robots and robotic systems. Students in the robotics engineering technology program learn how to design, build, and program robots for a wide range of applications, including manufacturing, healthcare, and exploration. The program emphasizes hands-on learning, with students working in labs to build and test their own robotic systems. Graduates of the robotics engineering technology program are prepared for careers in a variety of industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, and defense.
Accredidation: The Robotics Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

ProgramName: Russian Minor
Requirements: Students must complete 15 credit hours. Minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in all courses for the minor.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sales and Marketing,
Requirements: The Sales and Marketing major provides a curriculum for students who are interested in sales and marketing in the food, agribusiness, and general business industries. The curriculum focuses on preparing students for professional sales and marketing careers. It includes courses in economics, marketing, and professional selling, along with foundational courses in business, science, and the humanities. For admission, applicants must meet Purdue's freshman criteria, which include the completion of specific high school coursework (8 semesters of English and math, 6 semesters of lab science and social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language), submission of SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.
Description: The Sales and Marketing major is designed for students who are interested in pursuing careers in professional selling, sales management, and marketing. The curriculum focuses on the development of skills in communication, problem-solving, and strategic thinking as they relate to the sales and marketing process. Students learn to analyze markets, understand buyer behavior, and develop effective marketing strategies. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in business and economics, with specialized coursework in professional selling, marketing research, and strategic marketing. Graduates are well-equipped to enter a variety of industries, including agribusiness, retail, and manufacturing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social Studies Education,
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the SSED program, students must meet the following requirements: 1. Completion of at least 30 credit hours of college-level coursework. 2. Minimum 2.50 overall GPA. 3. Minimum 3.00 average in Social Studies content courses. 4. Grades of C- or higher in all Social Studies content and Professional Education courses. 5. Satisfactory score on the CASA or equivalent (ACT/SAT/GRE) as required by the Indiana Department of Education. 6. Completion of EDCI 20500 and EDCI 28500.
Concentration: Economics, Geography, Government and Citizenship, Psychology, Sociology
Description: The Social Studies Education (SSED) program is an interdisciplinary major that prepares students for a career as a secondary (grades 5-12) social studies teacher. The program includes content coursework in history and other social sciences, as well as professional education courses. Students will develop a deep understanding of the social sciences and the pedagogical skills necessary to teach diverse learners in today’s classrooms.
Accredidation: Purdue University’s College of Education and its educator preparation programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Sociology Minor
Requirements: 15.00 Credit Hours. Required Courses: SOC 10000 - Introductory Sociology. Sociology Electives: 12 credits of Sociology courses, 9 of which must be at the 30000-level or above.
Concentration: Family and the Life Course, Health and Aging, Inequality and Social Justice, Social Control and Deviance, Social Organizations and Movements
Description: A student may choose a general sociology minor or a concentration in one of the specific subfields: Family and the Life Course; Health and Aging; Inequality and Social Justice; Social Control and Deviance; Social Organizations and Movements. To earn a Sociology Minor, students must complete at least 12 credit hours in sociology, at least 6 of which must be at the 30000-level or higher. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. All SOC courses are eligible for the minor.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sociology,
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Science in Sociology, students must complete 120 total credits. This includes a 13-credit Sociology Core consisting of SOC 10000 (Introductory Sociology), SOC 38200 (Introduction To Statistics In Sociology), SOC 38300 (Introduction To Research Methods In Sociology), and SOC 40200 (Sociological Theory). Additionally, students must complete 18 credits of Sociology electives and the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements. For undergraduate admission to Purdue University, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions, and self-report their high school grades and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT).
Description: Sociology is the study of human social life, groups and societies. Sociology examines how our individual lives are influenced by our social environments, and in turn, how we change those environments. Topics of study range from small groups to global social processes. Sociology majors learn to think critically and analytically, communicate effectively, and identify and solve problems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Soil and Water Sciences,
Requirements: The program in Soil and Water Sciences is designed to provide students with a strong background in the basic sciences, with an emphasis on the chemistry, physics, and biology of the soil. Students take a core of courses that deal with soil-water-plant relations, soil chemistry, soil microbiology, and soil physics. These courses are supplemented by electives in the basic sciences and in related applied fields. The curriculum is flexible enough to allow students to prepare for careers in environmental consulting, soil and water conservation, land use, or for graduate study. Completion of the program provides the student with the necessary course work to be a Certified Professional Soil Scientist. General freshman admission requires a high school transcript, a personal essay, and SAT or ACT scores.
Concentration: Environmental Quality, Soil Science, Water Science
Description: Soil and Water Sciences involve the study of the physical, chemical and biological processes in the environment. Soil is the medium for plant growth and is a regulator of water flow and quality in the landscape. Students in the Soil and Water Sciences program apply their knowledge to solve problems of environmental quality, land use and management and agricultural productivity. In addition to a core of soil and water sciences, students choose one of three concentrations: Environmental Quality, Soil Science, or Water Science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sound for the Performing Arts,
Requirements: Successful audition/interview/portfolio review is required for admission to this major. Students must complete a portfolio review and interview. To schedule an interview/review, applicants should contact the Theatre department. General Purdue University admission requirements also apply, including the Common Application personal statement and high school transcripts. Purdue University is a test-required institution; SAT or ACT scores are required for admission.
Department: College of Liberal Arts (Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance)
Description: The Sound for the Performing Arts major provides a balance of technical and artistic skills through classes in music, theatre, and physics, as well as several specialized courses in sound and recording. Students get hands-on experience by running sound for several productions each year. Coursework covers live sound reinforcement, studio recording, and sound design for theatre. All students in the major must also complete the requirements of the College of Liberal Arts.
Accredidation: The Department of Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Spanish for the Professions Minor
Requirements: Minimum Credits: 15. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken in residence at the West Lafayette campus. At least one of the SPAN 40000-level courses must be taken in residence at the West Lafayette campus. A grade of C- or better is required in all courses for the minor. Minimum GPA: 2.00.
Description: The Spanish for the Professions minor provides students with the linguistic and cultural skills necessary to communicate effectively in a professional environment. Students will develop proficiency in Spanish and gain an understanding of the cultural nuances that are essential for success in a global workforce.

ProgramName: Spanish Minor
Requirements: Students must complete 12 credits of SPAN coursework at the 30000-level or above. All courses must be taught in Spanish. At least 6 credits must be completed on the West Lafayette campus. All courses must be completed with a C- or better.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish,
Requirements: Candidates must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours for the Bachelor of Arts degree. The Spanish major specifically requires 30 credit hours of Spanish courses above the 20200 level, with a minimum grade of C- in all major courses. At least 15 of these 30 credit hours must be completed on the Purdue West Lafayette campus. General undergraduate admission requires the submission of official high school transcripts, a personal essay (Statement of Purpose), and SAT or ACT scores.
Description: The Spanish major provides students with high-level proficiency in the Spanish language and a deep understanding of the cultures, literatures, and linguistics of the Spanish-speaking world. Through a wide range of course offerings, students explore the diverse perspectives and histories of Spain, Latin America, and Spanish-speaking communities in the United States.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Special Education Dual Licensure: Elementary Education and Mild Intervention P-12,
Requirements: The program requires a total of 120 credit hours and a minimum graduation GPA of 2.80. Students must be admitted to the Teacher Education Program (TEP) and complete all professional education and content courses with a grade of C or better. General undergraduate admission to Purdue University requires the submission of high school transcripts, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.
Description: The Special Education Dual Licensure: Elementary Education and Mild Intervention P-12 program leads to the Bachelor of Arts degree and Indiana licensure in both Elementary Generalist (K-6) and Mild Intervention (P-12).
