Students must complete all courses with a grade of C- or better and maintain a 2.80 GPA to be eligible for licensure.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Special Education,
Requirements: Admission to the Professional Education Program: 1. Minimum 3.0 overall GPA (subject to change). 2. No grade lower than a 'C-' in any course required for the major. 3. Current, valid ‘Expanded’ Criminal Background Check on file with the Office of Field Experiences. 4. Completion of required Teacher Education foundation courses.
Concentration: Mild Intervention, Intense Intervention, Early Childhood Special Education
Description: The Special Education Program is designed to prepare undergraduate students for licensure to teach learners with disabilities in preschool through grade 12. Graduates of the program are prepared to work with students who have various types of disabilities (e.g., learning disabilities, intellectual disabilities, autism, emotional/behavioral disorders, etc.) and their families.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences,
Requirements: The SLHS major provides a scientific foundation for students interested in careers in the fields of speech-language pathology, audiology, and other health related fields. Enrollment in the SLHS major is open to any student who is in good standing with the University. For a student to remain in good standing in the SLHS major, they must maintain a cumulative GPA of 2.000 or higher. A student who falls below a cumulative 2.000 GPA will be placed on SLHS departmental probation. Students must have a 2.000 cumulative GPA in all courses to graduate.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences (SLHS) involves the study of the communication process, including its anatomical, physiological, and psychological bases, and communication disorders. The undergraduate program provides students with a broad background in the basic sciences related to speech, language, and hearing, as well as an introduction to the clinical aspects of communication disorders. Completion of the Bachelor of Science degree prepares students for graduate study in speech-language pathology or audiology, which is required for clinical certification and licensure.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics - Applied Statistics,
Requirements: Freshman applicants are evaluated based on several criteria including: high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of natural science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language), grades in academic courses, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions. For the College of Science, completion of calculus is highly recommended.
Concentration: Applied Statistics
Description: Statistics is the science of designing studies, and of collecting and analyzing data, for the purpose of helping people make decisions in the face of uncertainty. The study of statistics is much more than the study of mathematical proofs. It involves learning how to ask the right questions, how to design an experiment or survey to answer those questions, how to handle the data that is collected, and how to use the results to make decisions and provide insights. The Applied Statistics concentration is for students who want to apply statistical techniques to another field such as agriculture, computer science, economics, engineering, or health sciences. This concentration is a good choice for students who want a career in industry, government, or a non-profit organization.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics-Mathematics and Statistics,
Requirements: The Mathematics and Statistics program is a joint program between the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics. It is designed to provide students with a strong background in both mathematics and statistics. For admission, freshman applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants to the College of Science are expected to have completed 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus), 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single Foreign Language. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.
Concentration: Mathematics and Statistics
Description: The Statistics major with a concentration in Mathematics and Statistics provides students with a strong background in both fields. It is specifically designed for students who may want to pursue graduate study in statistics or a related field. It provides students with a strong foundation in the concepts and tools of modern statistics and mathematics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Studio Arts and Design,
Requirements: Admission to the Studio Arts and Design, BA program is based on Purdue University's general freshman admission criteria, which include completion of the high school Core 40 curriculum (or equivalent), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. According to the Patti & Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance, no portfolio is required for freshman admission to the Studio Arts and Design major.
Concentration: Art History, Ceramics, Drawing, Electronic and Time-Based Art, Metalsmithing, Painting, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture, Textiles
Description: The Studio Arts and Design (BA) degree is designed for students who want a broad-based education in the visual arts. Students in this program choose a concentration in one of several areas, including art history, ceramics, drawing, electronic and time-based art, metalsmithing, painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, or textiles.
Accredidation: The Department of Art and Design is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Supply Chain and Operations Management,
Requirements: Students are admitted to the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business as first-year students. Factors that are considered in the admission process include: High school course expectations, High school GPA, SAT/ACT scores, and Personal background and experiences. In addition, students may also apply for admission as a transfer student from either another college or university or from another academic unit at Purdue University (CODO). Transfer students from outside of Purdue University must have at least a 3.0 or higher GPA and must have completed at least 12 credit hours.
Description: The Supply Chain and Operations Management (SCOM) major focuses on the management of business processes. These processes include the design, control, and improvement of business operations involved in the production and distribution of goods and services. SCOM professionals ensure that resources are utilized effectively and efficiently to meet customer requirements and achieve organizational goals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Supply Chain Management Technology,
Requirements: Purdue University has a holistic admissions process. Evaluation is based on several factors, including: High School Coursework (including meeting minimum subject requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, etc.), Grades in High School Coursework, Strength of your overall high school curriculum, Overall grades (GPA), SAT or ACT test scores, Personal Essay, and Evidence of motivation, leadership, and service.
Description: Supply chain management technology (SCMT) focuses on the movement of goods and services from the source to the final customer. Global in scope, SCMT encompasses all activities associated with planning, sourcing, making, delivering, and returning products and services. To manage these processes, SCMT professionals use the latest technology to synchronize the flows of materials, information, and financial resources. The SCMT curriculum is designed to prepare students for leadership roles in various sectors, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, and consulting. Core courses cover topics such as procurement, operations, inventory management, transportation, and supply chain analytics. Students also gain practical experience through internships and industry-sponsored projects, ensuring they are well-equipped to solve real-world supply chain challenges.
Accredidation: The Supply Chain Management Technology program is accredited by the Association of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering (ATMAE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Biomaterials-Process and Product Design,
Requirements: To apply for the BS in Sustainable Biomaterials-Process and Product Design, applicants must meet Purdue University’s general undergraduate admission requirements. Admission is based on a holistic review of high school coursework (including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of lab science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a single world language), grades, official SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay with Purdue-specific writing prompts. The degree program itself requires the completion of 120 credit hours, including core courses in biology, chemistry, math, physics, and specialized forestry and natural resources (FNR) courses.
Concentration: Process and Product Design
Description: Sustainable biomaterials (SBIO) students learn about the biology, chemistry, and physics of renewable, plant-based materials and how they are used for many of the products we use every day. Students study the science and technology that goes into converting trees and other plants into sustainable products, such as buildings, furniture, paper, and biofuels. The Process and Product Design concentration is designed for students interested in manufacturing, marketing, and the design and use of wood and other plant-based materials for construction and consumer products.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Food and Farming Systems,
Requirements: To apply for the Sustainable Food and Farming Systems, BS program, students must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include a minimum of 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. A personal essay and Purdue-specific responses are required as part of the application. The program itself requires a minimum of 120 credits for graduation, including the University Core Curriculum and College of Agriculture requirements, with specific coursework in Biology, Chemistry, and Mathematics (Calculus or Statistics).
Description: The Sustainable Food and Farming Systems (SFFS) major focuses on the production of food, fiber and medicinal plants. The core of this major is an understanding of the ecology of farming systems, and the practices that result in high productivity while protecting the environment and supporting the local community. The curriculum includes plant and soil science, cropping systems, integrated pest management, and the business and marketing of farm products. This major is highly interdisciplinary and can be customized to your individual interests. It provides great preparation for careers in farming, agricultural education, consulting, greenhouse and nursery production, processing and marketing of organic and specialty products, and non-profit organizations focused on food security.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Systems Analysis and Design,
Requirements: Admission to Purdue University is based on a holistic review of each application. For freshman admission, Purdue requires the Common Application and a personal essay. Applicants must meet high school coursework requirements, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of mathematics (including precalculus or calculus for most Polytechnic programs), 6 semesters of laboratory science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a single foreign language. Additionally, Purdue University is test-required; SAT or ACT scores are expected for all students applying for freshman admission.
Description: The Systems Analysis and Design (SA&D) major in Computer and Information Technology (CIT) focuses on the development of computer-based information systems. The major provides a strong foundation in systems analysis, database systems, and project management. Students learn to analyze business and organizational needs and to design and implement information systems to meet those needs. Graduates are prepared for careers as systems analysts, business analysts, and project managers.
Accredidation: The Computer and Information Technology program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Information Technology Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Teaching Physical Education/Health,
Requirements: To complete the Teaching Physical Education/Health, BA program, students must earn a total of 120.00 semester hours. A minimum GPA of 2.80 is required for all Professional Education and Content courses. Additionally, all Professional Education and Content courses must be completed with a grade of C- or higher. Students completing this program will be eligible for Indiana licensure in Physical Education (P-12) and Health (P-12).
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Description: This program is designed for students who are interested in teaching physical education and health at the elementary, middle, and/or high school levels. Students who complete the program are eligible for an Indiana dual license in Physical Education (P-12) and Health (P-12).
Accredidation: Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Turf Management and Science,
Requirements: To apply for the Turf Management and Science, BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University’s freshman admission criteria, which include the completion of a high school curriculum with 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Applicants are required to submit SAT or ACT scores and a personal statement (Common App essay). The program requires a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation, including core coursework in Agronomy and Turfgrass Science.
Description: The turfgrass industry is a multi-billion dollar a year industry with career opportunities in several areas including: golf course management, professional and collegiate sports field management, professional lawn care, sod production, and grounds management for municipalities, parks, and schools. Other opportunities include sales and marketing, research and development, and technical support within the turfgrass industry. The Turf Management and Science major is designed for students who are interested in a career in any of these areas. This major provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences of botany, soils, and chemistry, and also provides students with the specialized knowledge and skills needed to manage turfgrass systems. Students will also take courses in business and management to prepare them for the business aspects of the turfgrass industry.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, financial need, and leadership (General Purdue financial aid information)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Unmanned Aerial Systems,
Requirements: To apply for freshman admission, you must submit: The Common Application, Purdue-specific questions (including those about your choice of major), Self-reported high school grades, and Self-reported SAT or ACT test scores.
Department: School of Aviation and Transportation Technology, Purdue Polytechnic Institute
Description: The unmanned aerial systems (UAS) major provides students with the skills and knowledge to design, build, and operate unmanned aircraft. Students will learn about flight dynamics, control systems, sensors, and data analysis, and will have the opportunity to participate in hands-on projects and internships.
Accredidation: The unmanned aerial systems program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in User Experience (UX) Design,
Requirements: Admission to the User Experience (UX) Design program at Purdue University requires the submission of a completed Common Application, including a personal essay and Purdue-specific short-answer questions. For the current application cycle, Purdue University requires self-reported SAT or ACT scores from all freshman applicants. High school course expectations include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, Geometry, and a higher-level math course), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single Foreign Language. The program itself requires 120 credit hours and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 for graduation.
Description: User experience (UX) design is a multidisciplinary field that focuses on the design of the interaction between users and products, such as websites, applications, and devices. The goal of UX design is to create products that are easy to use, efficient, and enjoyable for the user. Students in the UX design program learn about the user-centered design process, which includes research, prototyping, and testing. They also learn about visual design, information architecture, and interaction design. The program emphasizes hands-on, project-based learning, and students have the opportunity to work on real-world projects for clients.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Veterinary Nursing,
Requirements: Admission to the Veterinary Nursing Program is competitive. Selection is based on several factors, including: academic performance in the required prerequisite courses, overall academic performance (Cumulative GPA), a minimum of 40 hours of practical experience with a veterinarian, and a personal statement/essay.
Description: The Veterinary Nursing Program (formerly the Veterinary Technology Program) provides students with the knowledge and skills required to become a veterinary nurse. The Veterinary Nursing Program is an integral part of the College of Veterinary Medicine. Veterinary nurses are an essential part of the veterinary medical team. Veterinary nurses perform many of the same tasks for animal patients that nurses and other professionals perform for human patients. Students learn through a combination of classroom, laboratory, and clinical experiences. During the clinical rotations, students work alongside veterinarians, veterinary nursing students, and veterinary nurses in the Purdue Veterinary Teaching Hospital.
Accredidation: The Veterinary Nursing Program is fully accredited by the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Virtual Product Integration,
Requirements: To earn the Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Virtual Product Integration, students must complete 120 credit hours with a minimum 2.0 Graduation GPA. Application requirements for undergraduate freshman admission include the Common App personal essay, high school transcripts, and self-reported or official SAT or ACT scores. Completion of a college-prep high school curriculum is expected, including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language.
Description: Virtual Product Integration graduates are prepared to help companies build and improve their virtual enterprises. These specialists take digital product designs and add information and intelligence that allow a company to evaluate its lifecycle, manufacturing and performance. Students utilize 3D modeling, product data management (PDM), product lifecycle management (PLM) and other high-end software tools to create and simulate the entire lifecycle of a product from its initial concept to its eventual disposal.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Web Programming and Design,
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate programs at Purdue University, including Web Programming and Design, applicants must submit the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required documents include official high school transcripts and self-reported or official SAT or ACT scores. Admission is based on a holistic review of academic performance, including core subject requirements (4 years of English, 4 years of Math, 3 years of Lab Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language).
Description: The web programming and design major is for students who want to be involved in the design and development of the websites we use every day. Students will learn how to design, build and manage complex websites and web applications using the latest technologies and tools. The program is a collaboration between the Brian Lamb School of Communication and the Department of Computer Graphics Technology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Welding Engineering Technology,
Requirements: The welding engineering technology (WET) program is intended to produce graduates who are prepared to handle the responsibilities and requirements of a welding engineer. Graduates of this program will be experts in the application and implementation of welding technology. They will have the skills and knowledge to oversee the implementation of the equipment, procedures, and quality control. Admission to the program requires meeting Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which includes the completion of specific high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), submission of SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. A total of 124 semester hours are required for the degree.
Description: The Welding Engineering Technology program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in the application of welding technology, materials science, and engineering principles. The program emphasizes the practical application of welding processes, design, and inspection techniques. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in a wide range of industries, including manufacturing, construction, aerospace, and energy. Students in the WET program have access to state-of-the-art welding equipment and laboratories. They also have the opportunity to participate in internships and research projects with industry partners.
Accredidation: The Welding Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Wildlife,
Requirements: Admission to the Wildlife, BS program is based on a holistic review of several factors. Required high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (including Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and answers to Purdue-specific questions. Evaluation also considers the applicant's GPA and the strength of their high school curriculum.
Description: The Wildlife major provides students with a broad background in the life sciences, plus specific knowledge in the ecology, management, and conservation of wildlife and their habitats. The curriculum is designed to meet the educational requirements for certification as an Associate Wildlife Biologist by The Wildlife Society. Students are prepared for careers with state and federal agencies, non-profit organizations, and private firms. Many students also pursue graduate degrees.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies,
Requirements: The Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) major consists of 33 credit hours of coursework. Students must also complete the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements and the University Core Curriculum. All courses for the major must be completed with a grade of C- or better.
Description: The Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Program (WGSS) offers an interdisciplinary undergraduate major and minor. In WGSS, we study the way gender and sexuality are shaped by and within political, social and cultural contexts. We study why social inequalities exist and how to make the world more just and inclusive. We think about gender and sexuality in relation to race, class, disability and nationality. We study diverse subjects—like politics, history, literature and media—to understand the complexity of human experience.
